title: Man City 5-0 Norwich: Floyd Samba enjoys dream debut with double to book place in Carabao Cup fourth round for Enzo Maresca's side
author: Patrick Rowe
content:
Man City 5-0 Norwich: Floyd Samba enjoys dream debut with double to book place in Carabao Cup fourth round for Enzo Maresca's side
Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Manchester City and Norwich City at the Etihad Stadium; Floyd Samba, son of ex-defender Chris, scored twice on debut; Allan also marked first appearance with a goal and Rayan Cherki scored
Thursday 17 September 2026 22:18, UK
Floyd Samba enjoyed a dream debut by scoring twice as holders Manchester City booked their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 5-0 home win over Norwich.
Samba, 17, the son of former Premier League defender Chris, introduced himself in perfect style with his stooping header to open the scoring before Rayan Cherki doubled City's lead soon after.
Having assisted the first for Samba, fellow debutant Allan joined in on the scoring after dancing into the box and driving a low shot into the bottom corner to mark another emphatic introduction to the home fans at the Etihad Stadium.
- Carabao Cup fourth round draw in full
- Got Sky? Watch the Carabao Cup LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream the Carabao Cup with no contract📺
Samba built on his strong start to life in the senior squad, as his father watched on from the stands, when he calmly curled home a fourth goal for City.
Norwich were denied a consolation goal when substitute Mohamed Toure's effort was disallowed for offside, meaning the visitors walked away without a shot on target registered, and Ryan McAidoo would add to their misery with a late goal to make it five for the hosts.
A sixth straight win for Enzo Maresca's side now tees up a fourth-round clash with Brighton at home in the next round.
The key moments from the Etihad
29: GOAL! Dream debut for 17-year-old Samba as his stooping header opens the scoring.
32: GOAL! Cherki doubles the lead with a neat finish into the bottom corner after latching onto an Ayyoub Bouaddi pass.
39: BIG CHANCE FOR SAMBA! The young forward takes it in his stride and breaks into the box but Bruno Alves makes a strong recovery challenge to deal with the danger before he can shoot.
48: GOAL! Allan scores on his debut after assisting the opener with a low driven shot into the bottom corner.
54: GOAL! The pick of the goals as Samba grabs his second with a curling effort into the bottom-right corner.
68: MCAIDOO DENIED! Samba at the heart of it again as he feeds in McAidoo, who has a low strike across goal which is well saved by Daniel Grimshaw.
74: DISALLOWED! Toure slots a consolation goal in but the offside flag cuts their celebrations short.
90: GOAL! McAidoo completes the scoring with a fifth goal for the hosts.
Maresca praises debutants Samba and Allan
Man City boss Enzo Maresca:
"Not just for the two goals, for the entire performance he was good. He didn't play many games as a nine, we tried in the last two or three games.
"He is very good at finishing the action. It was a good game for him. I have said since day one, I am happy with the way we are working.
"It was not an easy game. The players were serious and professional."
On the performance of Allan on debut: "It was not easy for him, first time with 90 minutes. It is always complicated but it was important for him to play.
"English competition is different to South America. He has scored a goal and an assist so overall, he is happy.
"We have many games and we are just at the beginning of the season. The ones who play tonight will play Premier League or Champions League."
'Enzo's dream start at Man City rolls on'
Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom at the Etihad Stadium:
"Enzo Maresca's perfect start as Man City boss is rolling on. Since his players lifted the tempo, they have shown more than enough energy and craft.
"To make 10 changes and win so handsomely is a real statement of intent. Not many would have predicted Maresca winning his first six competitive matches after taking over from Pep Guardiola.
"With Cherki off at half-time attention can now firmly switch towards the visit of Sunderland at the weekend, and the ambition to make it a perfect seven before the international break."
Clement blames naivety for City defeat
Norwich City boss Philippe Clement:
"The team played in a good structure, well organised and the boys were disciplined. After 20 minutes, Man City started to get a little bit annoyed because they could not create.
"Then you get the first goal and we need to do better on that cross. Then on a transition they get a second goal; we were naive.
"There are good lessons to take. We missed the right choices in the final third; we had some good opportunities. We scored a goal but it was offside.
"I saw good individual performances from players but it is hard to take five goals with just six shots on target. Those are not good statistics."
summary: Holders Manchester City secured their place in the Carabao Cup fourth round with a 5-0 victory over Norwich City at the Etihad Stadium. Seventeen-year-old debutant Floyd Samba scored twice, while fellow debutant Allan and Rayan Cherki also found the back of the net. Ryan McAidoo completed the scoring late in the game, extending manager Enzo Maresca's winning start to six matches.
key_points: Floyd Samba scored a brace on his senior debut for Manchester City.
Allan marked his first appearance with a goal and an assist.
Rayan Cherki and Ryan McAidoo scored the remaining goals in the 5-0 win.
Norwich failed to register a shot on target and had a late Mohamed Toure goal disallowed for offside.
The victory advances Enzo Maresca's side to a fourth-round clash against Brighton.

title: Manchester City 5-0 Norwich City: Carabao Cup third round – live
author: Michael Butler
content:
Manchester Cityface Brighton in the fourth round and there are cheers around the Etihad as the stadium announcer reminds tonight’s crowd of the Seagulls’ result on the other side of Manchester on Wednesday.
Brighton are obviously a different beast to Norwich, but I wonder if Maresca will adjust his starting XI accordingly or continue to use his academy players in this competition. It would be a shame if Samba and McAidoo don’t continue to get opportunities.
Maresca is all smiles as he greets his City players, with a special smile for Samba.
Fair play to the Norwich fans, who never stopped singing and give a standing ovation to their side, despite the 5-0 scoreline. They face a long journey home to East Anglia.
GOAL! Manchester City 5-0 Norwich City (McAidoo 90)
O’Reilly gets free on the left. He centres for Lewis, who plays a sensational dummy to completely fool the Norwich defenders, and McAidoo arrives perfectly at the back post to sidefoot a finish into the corner. Three City academy products combining there for a flourishing finish.
Ryan McAidoo steers in number five! Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters
87 min: A loose backpass from Khusanov and Touré is nearly onto it, but Rulli springs out of goal quickly to clear the danger. Good goalkeeping from the former Marseille and Villarreal stopper.
80 min: City have wrestled back a bit of control. O’Reilly feels like a senior player for City now. It’s crazy to think he only really broke into the side a couple of years ago.
78 min: A word for Allan, another of City’s debutants. He wasn’t cheap, coming for £34m from Palmeiras, but there were definitely flickers of quality. Yongwa gave Allan a rough time in the opening minutes but the Brazilian finished with a goal and an assist, despite not playing particularly well. He’ll be happy overall.
76 min: Norwich are definitely finishing the stronger. It is perhaps forgivable when City are 4-0 up, but there isn’t much of the classic control that was always a trademark of the Pep era. I suspect that Maresca will be a little bemused at City’s performance in the last few minutes.
74 min: Musaba releases Touré, just on, and the Norwich forward converts nicely with a bouncing finish past Rulli. Touré is judged to be offside. There’s no VAR tonight, but replays show that the officials made the correct call.
70 min: City again close to a fifth! Lewis gets the byline and rips a heavy cross towards O’Reilly, who can’t divert the cross goalwards despite being six yards out. It was a very awkward ball to deal with, in fairness.
68 min: Samba at the heart of things again, the 17-year-old bumping off tackles and then finding McAidoo with a slide-rule pass. McAidoo closes in on goal and forces a good save out of Grimshaw but Samba – on a hat-trick, remember – cannot get to the rebound!
64 min: From the corner, Khusanov clears the cross but the ball falls to Norwich sub Musaba, who loses his footing but still gets a shot away, just wide! Rulli was panicking, and dived to his left but wasn’t getting there.
63 min: Norwich win a corner and over in the away end, the Norwich fans give an ironic cheer, celebrating almost as though they have scored a goal. Jacob Wright, who was a City player until joining Norwich last year, gives a little smile as he trots over to take the corner.
60 min: “I was going to send you an email asking if Mancheter City were going to be like United and go 2-0 up and lose 3-2 but I won’t bother now!” writes Dave Manby.
58 min: Samba’s two goals have both been full of quality. The first was an instinctive header right into the far corner after Samba picked up a good position in the middle. His second goal was even better, casually stroking a bending shot (with a ridiculous amount of curl) past Grimshaw on the angle, a good 20 yards out. Remember, Samba is normally a midfielder.
56 min: The cameras pan to Christopher Samba, Floyd’s father, in the stands and the former Blackburn Rovers defender is wearing a smile as wide as the Colin Bell Stand, shaking his head in delight and disbelief at his son’s debut. A special moment.
A second goal for the 17-year-old! Absolute scenes! Norwich try to play out from the back but gift possession to Ait Nouri. The Algerian stumbles but gets a pass off to Samba, who takes a touch and bends the ball into the corner from 20 yards. That looked so simple. Or rather, Samba made it look simple. What a talent.
Floyd Samba steers in his second! Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters
51 min: An opening for Norwich! Yongwa canters forward on the overlap and delivers a fierce low cross across City’s six-yard box. Rulli gets an awkward hand on the cross, but the ball falls to Fisher on the rebound and the right-back fluffs his lines, slicing wildly. That was a real chance for the visitors.
City immediately get a third! Allan, City’s new £34m signing, makes an instant impact after switching to the left wing, cutting inside Field and then pivoting back onto his left, and arrowing a fine low finish into the far corner. I’m not sure that was elite defending but it was still an excellent goal to go with the Brazilian’s first-half assist.
Allan drills in a third for City! Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters
City bring on McAidoo for Cherki, which seems sensible. That means Allan moves to the left flank, McAidooto the right wing, and O’Reilly has moved from left-back to No 10, where Cherki was. Ait Nouri, who was playing left wing, goes to left-back. Phew. Got that?
In simpler Norwich developments, Diallo has come off for Maghoma on the left wing.
Got a minute to spare? Why not try our daily Premier League trivia game, On the ball? Every day a star player past or present is hidden behind nine clues. How many will you need to identify them? It’s available in the Guardian apps.
Quick Guide
Play our football trivia game, On the ball
The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?
42 min: If the game is looking safe for City in the second half, I wonder if we’ll see the introduction of a couple of other academy products from the bench with McAidoo and Braithwaite.
39 min: Not just because of his assist for Cherki, but Bouaddi is quietly beginning to assert himself in central midfield with his passes, breaking the lines.
37 min: Samba, who also played a key part in City’s second goal, finds another pocket of space on the left of Norwich’s box, but blazes an effort high and wide. The 17-year-old looks a real player, though. There is definitely a spot as Haaland’s understudy going at study. City have never really replaced that deputy striker role since losing Julián Alvarez in 2024. They do have first-team players than can play there – Semenyo, Ndiaye – but there is definitely an opportunity for an academy player like Samba to make his mark.
GOAL! Manchester City 2-0 Norwich City (Cherki 32)
City are purring now. Samba holds the ball up well, draws a couple of Norwich defenders and pops it around the corner to the onrushing Bouaddi. The Moroccan drives forward and plays a perfectly-timed pass through to Cherki, who breaks the offside trap. Clean through, Cherki takes a couple of touches and finishes low, neatly with his weaker right foot, past Grimshaw.
Rayan Cherki makes it two! Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA
30 min: Fisher is booked for a nasty challenge on Ait Nouri. The Norwich right back is lucky that the City man doesn’t make much of a fuss because Fisher really snapped into that with full force. That was bordering on wreckless.
A debut goal for the 17-year-old! What a moment for the young man! O’Reilly dinks a cross to the back post, Norwich keeper Grimshaw flaps at it, but the ball breaks loose. Allan is first to the ball and loops another cross into the middle where Samba nods it home! A brilliant header.
Floyd Samba stoops th had City into the lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters
26 min: There are plenty of City players with their hair bleached blonde. We’re not quite at Romania levels, but it’s not the easiest trying to pick each player out.
24 min: Norwich are really holding their own. Sam Field and Jacob Wright are snapping into challenges in the middle are City haven’t yet raised the tempo.
22 min: Samba looks second best to reach a through pass but bursts past Darling and briefly looks like he might have a free shot on goal, before the Norwich defender recovers to get a toe in. Samba showed genuine pace there, he is normally a central midfielder but you can see why he can also be deployed in forward areas. I’m surprised he is only 6ft tall though, his father, former Blackburn defender Christopher Samba, was a man mountain!
19 min: Maresca will be frustrated. Samba has looked the only bright spark in City’s attack. Cherki hasn’t got into the game and the wingers, Allan and Ait Nouri haven’t been at the races. As if to prove the point, Yongwa flattens Allan with a strong tackle and wins a goal kick for his side. Allan hasn’t been near it, physically.
17 min: Good from Kovacic, who tidies up on the half-way line and then drives straight through the middle of Norwich’s midfield – just as Howson did all those years ago for the Canaries here. Kovacic is felled right on the edge of the visitors’ area but referee Ruebyn Ricardo waves play on. Darling got the ball.
15 min: Diallo is now much more incisive. After collecting a diagonal cross-field ball, the Norwich left winger drives at Khusanov and bends a lovely low cross towards the City back post. It’s not close enough to trouble Rulli and too far in front of Kvistgaarden but that was a promising ball. Perhaps if the Norwich striker had gambled a little bit.
12 min: Whisper it, but Norwich are looking quite threatening on the counter-attack. A few times they have broken and City – with their full-backs high up the pitch – have looked a little exposed. Norwich just haven’t picked the right pass when they have got near to City’s box, Diallo wasteful for the visitors on this occasion.
9 min: Nice flick from Samba, who is playing as a false nine, and the debutant releases Lewis, who is through on goal, albeit a little wide. Lewis steadies himself but with Bruno Alves covering for Norwich, the City man curls his shot a yard over the bar.
6 min: Norwich on the counter-attack and Allan works back to stop Yongwa from crossing. The ball comes loose and the Norwich left back crunches the Brazilian in the tackle. Welcome to English football, Allan.
Allan is closed down by Benjamin Chrisene. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP
City are far from full-strength but this is still an elite team, captained by Kovacic. There are three debutants: Argentina international Gero Rulli (in goal), Brazilian winger Allan (signed for £34m in the summer) and Floyd Samba (academy midfielder and son of former Blackburn defender Christopher).
Norwich make nine changes to the Canaries’ starting XI from their 4-3 defeat at Middlesbrough. NINE! Jacob Wright, who grabbed a goal and an assist off the bench at Boro, is one of the players rewarded with a start.
Norwich’s Jacob Wright (left) celebrates after scoring against Middlesbrough on Saturday. Photograph: Bruce Rollinson/PA
Recent trips to the Etihad Stadium have been rough for Norwich City fans. There were the 5-0 Premier League drubbings in 2020 and 2021, while City went two better in 2013, scoring seven, with Sergio Agüero, Yaya Touré, David Silva, Alvaro Negredo and Edin Dzeko adding to two own goals from Bradley Johnson and Russell Martin. Just once did Norwich run City close in recent years, in 2015, but an 89th-minute penalty for City saw them run out narrow 2-1 winners.
But that was the league and this is the cup, which means Norwich can dream Carabao-infused dreams, and the Canaries will be channelling the spirit of Jonny Howson tonight.
Allow TikTok content?
This article includes content provided by TikTok. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.
City, of course, are the League Cup holders and with the visit of Sunderland on Sunday, they will surely rest some or most of their best tonight. The issue for Norwich is that Maresca’s benchwarmers are still some of the best players in the world, with £85m teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi and £60m recruit Iliman Ndiaye expected to start.
The big question for Norwich and manager Philippe Clement is whether to go for it: the Championship side are reeling from a dramatic 4-3 defeat at Middlesbrough (and the long trip home) and the play-off hopefuls, currently in mid-table, have a crucial home match against Bolton this weekend.
The winner of this tie will face Brighton in the fourth round, which really isn’t ideal for either City or Norwich. The Seagulls’ comeback win at United on Wednesday robbed us of a potential Manchester derby, then, but there is plenty of work for City and Norwich to get through here, before we start looking too far ahead.
summary: Manchester City secured a comfortable 5-0 victory over Norwich City in the Carabao Cup third round. Seventeen-year-old academy product Floyd Samba starred on his debut by scoring twice, while Rayan Cherki, new £34m signing Allan, and Ryan McAidoo added the remaining goals. The win advances City to the fourth round to face Brighton.
key_points: Manchester City defeated Norwich City 5-0 in the Carabao Cup third round.
Seventeen-year-old Floyd Samba scored two goals on his debut for City.
New £34m signing Allan contributed a goal and an assist for Manchester City.
Rayan Cherki and Ryan McAidoo scored the other goals to complete the 5-0 scoreline.
Manchester City advanced to the fourth round to face Brighton.

title: Manchester United: What's to blame for latest problems and results increasing scrutiny on Michael Carrick after Carabao Cup exit?
author: William Bitibiri
content:
Manchester United: What's to blame for latest problems and results increasing scrutiny on Michael Carrick after Carabao Cup exit?
Michael Carrick is under increasing scrutiny at Manchester United; Man Utd have crashed out of the Carabao Cup and have produced their joint-worst start to a Premier League season; Vote on what you think the main issue is at Old Trafford below
Thursday 17 September 2026 14:17, UK
Manchester United's collapse against Brighton has intensified the scrutiny on Michael Carrick - but the problems at Old Trafford run deeper than the head coach.
United led 2-0 after just 10 minutes against Brighton on Wednesday night. By full-time, they had lost 3-2, exited the Carabao Cup at the third-round stage for a second successive season and been booed off by their own supporters.
It was the first time in 50 years United had lost at Old Trafford after going 2-0 up. They had won 143 of the previous 145 matches in which they had established that advantage. They also failed to register another shot on target after Mason Mount's 2-0 goal until the 76th minute.

- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
The defeat leaves Carrick under pressure only months after his interim spell was rewarded with the permanent job. He had won 12 of his 17 matches last season, drawing three and losing two, giving him a 70.6 per cent win rate. This season, his record is two wins, one draw and three defeats from six games - a 33.3 per cent win rate.
United have now also matched their joint-worst start to a Premier League season after four games, while their Carabao Cup exit has removed an opportunity for silverware.
So what is the main issue at Old Trafford?
United are being outrun
United's lack of urgency on the pitch has been stark, and the numbers match what we're seeing in matches.
United rank 14th in the Premier League for distance covered this season, with 449.1km, but their rankings drop sharply when the intensity of those movements is measured.
They are 18th for sprints, with 379, 19th for high-speed runs, with 1,364, 18th for sprints per kilometre covered and 19th for high-speed runs per kilometre.
That paints a picture of a team covering ground without doing enough of it at the speeds required to press, recover and defend transitions.
It was particularly obvious against Brighton. United's nine changes from the side that started the Manchester derby provided some context, with several players coming into the team after spending time on the bench. But Brighton also made six changes, including four players making their first starts for the club.
Jamie Redknapp questioned United's physical condition.
"They didn't look fit enough," he said. "I don't know if a lot of them do enough. I saw too many players not running back or not looking fit enough."
Leny Yoro's recovery for Brighton's third goal was one example. He was jogging back as Brighton broke, rather than sprinting into a position from which he could make a challenge.
It is a concern that stretches beyond one night. If United cannot match opponents for intensity, they are left defending larger spaces and spending longer without the ball.
Your views
Bomer86: "Why are Brighton fitter and faster than Man Utd? What is happening in training that the players are not fit? They were slower to every ball. No desire, no energy after 10 mins."
Ossy: "Fitness/intensity and Carrick's inability to read game state and react accordingly is going to be Man Utd's undoing this season."
United have spent, but is the squad balanced?
This summer United made seven permanent signings, alongside four loan arrivals, while 13 players left permanently and 10 went out on loan.
The headline investment has been concentrated heavily in midfield and attack. Around £85m of that spending started against Brighton in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, while Carlos Baleba - signed from Brighton for around £70m - was watching from the stands.
The broader squad remains one of the most valuable in the Premier League. Transfermarkt values United's first-team squad at £791.2m, the fifth-highest figure among the clubs shown, behind Manchester City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool.
However, concerns remain over whether the distribution of that value has provided Carrick with enough tools to work with.
United's forwards account for £317.2m of the squad valuation and midfielders another £249.9m. The defensive group is valued at £193.8m, with the goalkeeper position accounting for the remainder.
The defence was already an obvious area of concern before the transfer window closed, yet United went into Wednesday's game with two inexperienced centre-backs in Yoro and Ayden Heaven and limited options at full-back.
Your views
EmmaRachael: "Why do Man Utd persist in buying quantity instead of real quality."
Cheese: "Appalling defence please invest in defensive reinforcements."
Gazza D: "United haven't backed Carrick. Desperately need two wing-backs of quality and that is evident in what we've seen with Dalot and Mazraoui."
Owners and INEOS: Who built this squad?
Supporters have repeatedly questioned the direction of the club, particularly after another transfer window in which significant money was spent but defensive reinforcements remained an issue.
United have now cycled through several managers since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, yet familiar complaints about the squad, recruitment and performances remain.
That is why Carrick's position can't be judged in isolation. The manager is responsible for the team on the pitch, but the squad he is selecting was built through decisions made at board and recruitment level.
Your views
S. Prime09: "United had a real chance to build on last season. The transfer window was so important. But we wouldn't spend over £70m. And all our top targets went some other team."
Ziggy: "The club has been lacking a clear plan since Fergie left. They don't know what they're doing."
Carrick: From interim hero to man under pressure
Carrick's interim spell last season was impressive enough to earn him the permanent job.
But it is the nature of the performances that has caused concern as much as the results.
United have struggled to control games and Carrick has faced questions over his in-game management and team selection. His nine changes against Brighton left him open to criticism when United's performance deteriorated after the early two-goal burst.
He accepted full responsibility for United's abject performance after the game.
"We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it," Carrick told Sky Sports. "The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me."
Your views
Jefft: "I'm so grateful for Carrick getting us into the top four but I said it then, the club should have said thanks but get in an elite coach who tactically has it."
Jon S: "At what point do you stop blaming managers and start blaming players? You can't keep swapping manager after manager after manager."
United ignored defensive warning signs
Wednesday's game exposed perhaps the clearest squad weakness. Yoro and Heaven formed an inexperienced centre-back pairing and Brighton repeatedly found space around them.
For the second goal, Luka Vuskovic won the header ahead of Benjamin Sesko, and the ball fell to Pascal Gross, who had space to finish. Heaven failed to anticipate the danger and Yoro could not prevent the shot.
For the third, Yoro was again caught behind the play as Brighton broke.
Full-back remains another concern, with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui facing criticism for their positioning and distribution - and the depth behind the established defensive options remains questionable.
Your views
John S: "The gaps between Heaven and Yoro were too big, the full backs were beyond poor and the midfield looks average."
HN: "Why would you use an inexperienced back line in a must win game? Nothing against playing young players but pair them with experience."
No more cohesion in attack
Last season, United had a more settled attacking combination with Matheus Cunha on the left, Bryan Mbeumo through the middle and Amad Diallo on the right. Sesko remained an option introduced off the bench.
Rashford's return has altered that balance, with supporters questioning whether the change has affected the team's attacking rhythm.
The time without a shot on target against Brighton is a major concern: after the early burst, United could not consistently supply Sesko or create enough pressure to prevent Brighton from taking control.
Rashford did have a late chance to equalise but saw his near-post effort saved.
Your views
Dhanyaal: "Last season Cunha on left and Mbeumo on right and Sesko as number 9 was working. Why's he changed it and put Rashford on left?"
Platty7: "Rightly or wrongly the major change from last season is Rashford, he hasn't exactly set the world alight."
summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is facing intense scrutiny after a 3-2 defeat to Brighton eliminated the club from the Carabao Cup at the third-round stage. The loss marked United's joint-worst start to a Premier League season and the first time in 50 years they lost at Old Trafford after leading 2-0. Beyond results, critics and supporters have raised concerns regarding the team's physical fitness, low running intensity, defensive vulnerabilities, and squad imbalance following the summer transfer window.
key_points: Manchester United suffered a 3-2 defeat to Brighton after leading 2-0, resulting in their second successive third-round Carabao Cup exit.
Michael Carrick's win rate has dropped from 70.6 per cent last season to 33.3 per cent across six games this term.
United rank poorly in physical metrics, placing 14th for distance covered, 18th for sprints, and 19th for high-speed runs in the Premier League.
Critics and fans have questioned squad construction, noting heavy investment in attack and midfield while leaving the defense inexperienced and thin.
Changes to the attacking lineup and a lack of tactical cohesion have contributed to United's struggles to control matches.

title: Man United player ratings v Brighton: Mazraoui 3, Santos 4, Lacey 7 | The National
author: Andy Mitten
content:
Unhappy Manchester United fans witnessed something unseen at Old Trafford in half a century on Wednesday as their side lost 3-2 at home to Brighton & Hove Albion in the third round of the League Cup after going two goals up.
The last time United lost at home after leading by two goals was in September 1976 when Tottenham Hotspur won by the same scoreline.
While Brighton progress to the last 16, defeat was another blow to a Manchester United side who suffered a controversial 1-0 loss to rivals Manchester City in the Premier League last weekend and are 13th with one win from four games.
United conceded twice in four second-half minutes after teenager Shea Lacey had put them ahead in the eighth minute and Mason Mount made it 2-0 two minutes later.
Charalampos Kostoulas pulled one back in first-half stoppage time before Pascal Gross equalised in the 65th and Maxim De Cuyper hit the winner in the 69th, with the home fans booing at the final whistle.
It was the third successive domestic cup loss for United after they went out in the second round of the League Cup on penalties at fourth-tier Grimsby Town last season and lost 2-1 at home in the third round of the FA Cup to Brighton in January.
What they said
United manager Michael Carrick: "We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me."
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler: "The longer the game went, the more we had control. I thought we deserved to win."
Man United ratings
Karl Darlow - 4/10: His United debut was a forgettable one. Weak punch from a Brighton corner as the visitors had a good spell after going 2-0 down. Some commendable keeping under heavy Brighton pressure, but could he have come out for Brighton’s opener? Then he conceded another two. 
Diogo Dalot - 4/10: Struggled against the pace of Yalcouye as, for the first time in 50 years, United lost a home game after leading 2-0 at half time.
Leny Yoro - 4/10: Partnership with Heaven looked shaky as Brighton created chance after chance. Led his side into trouble on more than one occasion.
Ayden Heaven - 3/10: Early forced pass intercepted by Costinha, then sloppily lost the ball, which allowed Brighton to attack. Did well to get back and pressure a Brighton attack, but the ball flew past him before Brighton’s first goal. Bested by Kostoulas throughout the night.
Mansour Mazraoui - 3/10: Went down injured on 19 minutes. Shredded for the third goal. What on earth has happened? He was very good in his first season. 
Andrey Santos - 4/10: First start since the opening day defeat against Hull and did little to convince that he’s worth a starting place in future.
Youri Tielemans - 4/10: Tidy start when he passed to Lacey for the opener. Fine challenge in the box as Brighton attacked in the first half. Lovely turn on 50 minutes before he shot miles over. His 62nd minute effort was closer, but should have been on target. Must do better.
Marcus Rashford - 6/10: Top work as he won the ball back, then shot before the second goal. Good feet, strong running. Clean through on 76 minutes and had to score, but Steele saved. United’s best player by far.
Mason Mount - 5/10: Finished the second after nine minutes, striking a shot downwards after getting over the ball just 98 seconds after the first. Not enough as Brighton took control almost from the point they went 2-0 down. 
Shea Lacey - 7/10: Sent off against Brighton last time he played them. Took three touches before banging one into the corner in the seventh minute with his left foot for his first senior goal. Encouraging performance. 
Benjamin Sesko - 4/10: Didn’t get much service near the opposing goal. Fluffed an opportunity after an hour after dallying on the ball. Tried to win a 65th-minute ball, but didn’t, and Gross scored. A pathetic goal to concede. United had 17 touches in Brighton’s box against 39 for the visitors.
Substitutes
Bryan Mbeumo (on for Lacey, 66') - 5/10: Offered little as Brighton dominated, with 35-year-old Pascal Gross the best player on the pitch.
Kobbie Mainoo (on for Santos, 66') - 6/10: An upgrade on the player he replaced. 
Joshua Zirkzee (on for Sesko, 65') 3/10: Struggled to get into the game.
Bruno Fernandes (on for Mount, 73') 6/10: Set Rashford up but he should never have been needed to come off the bench with the team winning 2-0.
Matheus Cunha (on for Rashford, 80') - N/A.
summary: Manchester United suffered a historic 3-2 home defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion in the League Cup third round after squandering a two-goal lead established by Shea Lacey and Mason Mount. Goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross, and Maxim De Cuyper sealed the comeback win for Brighton. This marks the first time in 50 years that United has lost a home match after leading by two goals at half-time.
key_points: Manchester United lost 3-2 to Brighton after leading 2-0 through goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount.
Brighton advanced to the League Cup last 16 thanks to goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross, and Maxim De Cuyper.
This is the first time since September 1976 that Manchester United has lost a home game after holding a two-goal lead.
The defeat marks Manchester United's third successive domestic cup loss.

title: Chelsea: Clearlake Capital acquires full control as Todd Boehly, Mark Walter and Hansjorg Wyss sell stakes
author: Jack Skelton
content:
![Todd Boehly (left) and Mark Walter (right) at the 2025 Fifa Club World Cup final](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/9719/live/c0654da0-b223-11f1-a9d3-d1d2b06c2bad.jpg)
Todd Boehly (left) and Mark Walter (right) had been part of Chelsea's ownership group since 2022
- Published
Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly and director Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the club to majority owner Clearlake Capital.
It means Clearlake - led by co-founders Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano - have now acquired full control of the club.
Boehly, Walter and Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss each had a 12.8% stake, with Clearlake previously owning 61.5% of the Blues.
In a statement the club said Wyss "will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group".
However American Boehly will leave his role as chairman, a position he has held since 2022 when the consortium bought the club for Â£2.3bn from Roman Abramovich in the wake of the Russian being sanctioned by the UK government over alleged links to his country's president Vladimir Putin - something he has denied.
BBC Sport reported in August that Boehly and Walter were exploring selling their stakes.
Multiple sources said talks started within Chelsea's ownership group after a rift, first apparent in 2024, led both sides to explore buying each other out.
Boehly, who is a co-owner of baseball franchise the Los Angeles Dodgers, said it had been an "honour" to serve as Chelsea chairman.
"I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans," he added.
"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the club. I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake's leadership."
Boehly and Walter have also sold their shareholding in Chelsea's partner club, French Ligue 1 side Strasbourg.
Since the takeover in 2022, Chelsea's highest Premier League finish is fourth in 2024-25, with the club also winning the Uefa Conference League and Fifa Club World Cup that season.
The club have also had a remarkably high turnover of players over the past four years, with the initial strategy focusing on signing young players to long-term contracts.
Chelsea finished 10th in the Premier League last season and appointed Xabi Alonso as their manager in the summer.
Eghbali and Feliciano thanked Boehly for his "time and contribution" as chairman, saying he will "always be a part of the Chelsea story and family".
They added their focus is to "continue investing in the club's infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club's supporters".
Chelsea have ongoing plans either to redevelop Stamford Bridge or move to a new stadium, which sources say had created tension at times between Boehly's camp and Clearlake.
A club statement said there will be "no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the club" as a result of Clearlake assuming full control.
Walter, the co-owner and chief executive of global finance firm Guggenheim Partners, where Boehly also began his financial career, last month sold the Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5bn (Â£9.23bn) - a year after buying a majority stake in the NBA franchise.
Separately, US federal prosecutors and the Securities and Exchange Commission are investigating companies in Walter's business empire.
summary: Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly and director Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the club to majority owner Clearlake Capital, giving Clearlake full control of the club. Boehly is stepping down from his role as chairman, which he held since the consortium purchased the club in 2022. The ownership changes follow a rift within the group that led both sides to explore a buyout.
key_points: Clearlake Capital has acquired full control of Chelsea after purchasing the stakes held by Todd Boehly and Mark Walter.
Todd Boehly has stepped down from his position as Chelsea chairman.
Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.
Clearlake stated there will be no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership, or strategy at the club.
Boehly and Walter also sold their shareholding in French partner club Strasbourg.

title: Man Utd 2-3 Brighton: Michael Carrick's Old Trafford tenure is only heading in one direction as Red Devils face familiar story
author: Sam Blitz
content:
Man Utd 2-3 Brighton: Michael Carrick's Old Trafford tenure is only heading in one direction as Red Devils face familiar story
Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup, surrendering a two-goal lead against Brighton to lose 3-2 at Old Trafford; it is the first time in 145 attempts where United have held a two-goal lead at Old Trafford and lost, ramping up the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick
Thursday 17 September 2026 00:04, UK
This wasn't just a defeat. This wasn't just a collapse. This wasn't just a cup exit. Another Manchester United managerial project is heading in that one, same direction. And even Michael Carrick recognises that.
"We've gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that," he said. "I'm happy enough to be honest about that. That's how it feels."
It's a story that's been seen before. A dismal Carabao Cup experience at the first hurdle - this time throwing away a 2-0 lead to exit to Brighton - harks back to memories of Ruben Amorim's disappointing defeat at Grimsby last year, which helped signal the beginning of the end.

- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
A cup exit to the Seagulls was also reminiscent of the FA Cup defeat United suffered to Fabian Hurzeler's side at the start of the year. That was the last match before Carrick returned to the club and sparked a mini-revival. Now it seems like United are back to square one again.
Even Pascal Gross scoring the equaliser at Old Trafford brought back memories of how he netted twice at United's home in August 2022 to put Erik ten Hag's tenure on the back foot, in the same way Carrick is facing an uphill battle now.
Gross still doing the business four years later is a great testament to the German's longevity at 35 years old - but it's an even more damning reflection of United's lack of progression in that time.
Since that match in 2022, which came 1,502 days ago, Gross has secured European football for Brighton, left the club for Borussia Dortmund, rejoined the Seagulls, got them back into Europe, watched on as United spent £365m on seven new central midfielders - and still he stood tall above the United midfield.
Around £140m of that pot started for United against Brighton in Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Andrey Santos, while a further £70m in Carlos Baleba watched on from the stands as his old club beat his new one. What must he be thinking?
Just like against Hull on the opening weekend of the season, United were outfought by Brighton. "They didn't look fit enough," said Jamie Redknapp. "I don't know if a lot of them do enough. I saw too many players not running back or not looking fit enough."
Many can point towards the nine changes Carrick made, with many of United's players coming into the team after weeks on the Premier League bench. But Brighton also made six changes to their regular line-up, including first starts for the club to four summer signings. What was their excuse?
Once again, the lack of investment in the defensive positions during the transfer market was very clear. The warnings about not addressing that position were there - and a big reason for Brighton turning the game on its head was the defensive displays of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.
"The inexperience of the two young centre-backs definitely showed," said Redknapp. "The pair of them were just inept in everything they did. If you look at Luka Vuskovic, who is 18 or 19, at this level he has aggression, winning challenges, recovery runs.
"And you looked at the two who played at United who played like everything was easy, making bad decisions - there was a difference in Brighton's defending when it came to going about their business."
The difference was seen in the second goal, as Vuskovic won a header ahead of Benjamin Sesko and the ball ran straight through the heart of the United defence for Gross to score easily.
Heaven was caught on his heels and failed to come across. "He doesn't anticipate the danger. Sprint, get to the penalty spot. But he's jogging.
"And Yoro, what kind of an effort is that to stop the shot? How easy was that? This isn't a five-a-side competition."
And for the third goal, Yoro was caught jogging back again as Brighton broke to score - not only highlighting Redknapp's defensive concerns about United, but their fitness ones too. "You've got to sprint Leny," he said. "He's jogging. If he sprints, he gets back and makes that block."
But while United are making familiar mistakes, they are still making unwanted history.
Not only was this the first time in 50 years that an opposition team has won at Old Trafford having been 2-0 down in the game, but it was the first time United have lost at home after holding a half-time lead in 551 half-time leads.
The time before the defeat to Brighton came in 1984, which pre-dated Sir Alex Ferguson's time at the club. Throw in a joint-worst start to a Premier League season after four games and the pressure is really growing on Carrick.
United's only win so far this season has been a 5-2 win over Ipswich that saw United struggle for the best part of an hour. And while there have been some mitigating factors - worldies at Everton and a contentious Manchester derby winner - there have been too many of those to be one-offs already.
It all sets up a massive Super Sunday game this weekend away at winless Fulham, facing their own early woes under Alvaro Arbeloa. What follows is a three-week international break which is prime time for an early managerial change.
A win at Craven Cottage buys Carrick time. Defeat and it will be a long period of questions.
summary: Manchester United crashed out of the Carabao Cup after surrendering a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 against Brighton at Old Trafford. This historic defeat—the first time United have lost at home after holding a two-time goal lead or a half-time lead in decades—has intensified the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick. Defensive frailties, fitness concerns, and a familiar lack of progression further compounded the disappointing cup exit.
key_points: Manchester United lost 3-2 to Brighton in the Carabao Cup after giving up a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford.
This marks the first time in 145 attempts that United have held a two-goal lead at home and lost.
Pundit Jamie Redknapp heavily criticized the fitness levels and poor defensive displays of young center-backs Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.
The defeat sets up a high-pressure match against Fulham ahead of a three-week international break that could influence Carrick's future.

title: Who is JJ Gabriel's dad? Former Arsenal defender key to Man Utd transfer saga
author: Tashan Deniran-Alleyne
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
![Michael Carrick press conference after Manchester United 0-1 Man City](<https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/16/9/42/FotoJet-(2).jpeg?width=1280&auto=webp&quality=75>)
It’s understood that Man Utd believe they can convince the wonderkid to stay and are able to challenge the request as Premier League rules state all parties - the club, player and their parent or carer - must agree to the cancellation for it to be valid.
Interestingly, Gabriel’s father - Joe O'Cearuill - has been the talk of social media since the news broke as reports claim he has played a huge part in his son’s career to date.
O'Cearuill is a big supporter of Gabriel, particularly on X - formerly Twitter - regularly posting videos of his goals and clips from behind-closed-doors training sessions and games.
Though, as per the Manchester Evening News, sources claim O'Cearuill can be difficult to deal with.
Who is Joe O'Cearuill?
Joe O'Cearuill is the father of JJ Gabriel, whose birth name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill.
According to reports, the reason behind Gabriel’s name change was to make the teenager more “marketable”, with the youngster tipped for big things.
While, O'Cearuill was named on the bench for the Gunners’ League Cup third round tie away at West Brom in September that year, he was loaned out to Brighton before joining Barnet permanently the following summer.
From there, the former defender went on to represent 11 different clubs across the lower leagues in English football and St. Patricks Athletic in the League of Ireland, before retiring in 2016 after a third spell with Haringey.
O'Cearuill was also a Republic of Ireland international, having won two senior caps in May 2007, three years before his son was born, against Ecuador and Bolivia.
summary: Manchester United believe they can convince wonderkid JJ Gabriel to stay amid a transfer saga involving Premier League cancellation rules. Gabriel's father, former Arsenal defender and Republic of Ireland international Joe O'Cearuill, has played a major role in his son's career. Sources report that O'Cearuill can be difficult to deal with and is very active on social media supporting his son.
key_points: Manchester United believes they can convince JJ Gabriel to stay, as Premier League rules require all parties to agree to a contract cancellation.
JJ Gabriel's father is Joe O'Cearuill, a former Arsenal defender and Republic of Ireland international.
O'Cearuill is very active on X, frequently sharing videos of his son's goals and training clips.
Sources claim that O'Cearuill can be difficult to deal with.
Gabriel's birth name is Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill, which was shortened to make him more marketable.

title: Max Dowman: Arsenal prodigy delivers latest statement performance as Mikel Arteta urges caution over 16-year-old
author: David Richardson
content:
Max Dowman: Arsenal prodigy delivers latest statement performance as Mikel Arteta urges caution over 16-year-old
Max Dowman scored twice for Arsenal in their 4-2 win at Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup third round; the 16-year-old forward was making his first appearance of the season; Dowman has had to wait for his chance after becoming the Premier League's youngest scorer
Wednesday 16 September 2026 13:10, UK
Max Dowman has waited patiently for opportunities in Arsenal's first team, but when he gets them, he delivers.
Mikel Arteta has managed the prodigy carefully since his big moment last season, when he became the Premier League's youngest scorer in a vital 2-0 home win over Everton on their title charge.
Dowman has played six times since then, mostly in cameos, and has been an unused substitute on four occasions this season. Last Saturday, he played an hour for the U21s in their 4-1 defeat to Chelsea while the first team won at Sunderland. Arteta warned Dowman afterwards that he must earn his minutes this season.

- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
But Dowman did not have to wait long for his chance. While £63.5m striker Viktor Gyokeres failed to take his opportunity during Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night, Dowman excelled, and the ease with which he scored twice was frightening.
His first, in just the seventh minute, came after he stole possession in midfield, burst onto the ball before Gyokeres, shimmyed past Cedric Kipre to leave the defender on the ground, before sending goalkeeper Christian Walton the wrong way with his weaker right foot.
"That's something very natural for him," said Arteta. "He can deliver those actions effortlessly. I would say that's his biggest quality."
Dowman had to be more precise for his second. Martin Zubimendi's pass deflected off Jacob Greaves's left arm, and Dowman, with little space inside the penalty area, adjusted to the ricochet with two quick touches to set up an accurate, composed shot on his left foot that almost trickled over the line, such was the perfectly measured weight of the effort.
Dowman's performance will only increase the hype around him. How will Arteta manage that?
"Well, it depends. If he does what he does on the pitch, it's not easy, I understand," said Arteta. "But what we have to do is look after him. He's 16 years old. You don't see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that's a totally different context.
"But in this league, with the demands that the league [has], the players and everything put on you, we really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he's in the right context with the right preparation. That's what we are trying to do."
It wasn't all about the goals at Portman Road. Dowman, who only completed his GCSEs in August, also showed his work rate off the ball, pressing Ipswich into a mistake for Noni Madueke's goal.
"Defensively, his application, his capacity as well to sustain the actions, is not easy," added Arteta.
"He's 16 years old, and he can create moments, but to consistently go through the game, every phase, with the demands that we put on them, to be able to do that is extremely difficult. And he's coping better and better and better.
"He did the action where he regained the ball and won it. In the first goal, he loses his man. And that's the thing that we need to continue to reiterate with him because he's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage and still handle the situation with such naturality."
The evening wasn't even all about Dowman. Marli Salmon, 17, made only his second start for the first team and impressed at centre-back with an assured performance.
"Just having two 16-year-olds playing for Arsenal at this level against a Premier League team is so fulfilling," said Arteta. "Because I've been there and just to be able to contribute in somebody's career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight is just phenomenal.
"Medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we're going to have two tremendous footballers for the future."
Dowman has benefited from Arsenal's stability under Arteta. The club has been able to nurture and develop him, without the distraction of cycling through managers. On the same day 15-year-old JJ Gabriel asked to leave Manchester United, Dowman made his latest statement on the pitch.
Arsenal fans will be desperate to see more of him. Arteta has warned it's not so easy to play him regularly.
"Everything is possible. The probability [of playing regularly] is probably extremely low because you don't see the players with the capacity to handle just the physicality of the game," he said.
"Not only that, but the demands that you have to put your body through in the week to be able to be in good condition to compete, the amount of information, the challenges that you have to face. But he's doing it and he's doing it really well every time there's a chance."
Merson: Dowman is a generational talent but he needs to be patient
Sky Sports' Paul Merson on Dowman's future:
"I don't know what words you can use. The lad is just unbelievable. You've got to consider his age. He's going past players like they're not there, like he's playing in his own age group.
"The first goal on Tuesday, the way he throws the dummy, leaves the defender on his backside and scores. It's just unbelievable.
"He's at an unbelievable Rolls Royce of a football club. He's got 15 years at least at the top. He's just got to be patient and it's hard because he'll think that he should be playing in the team now.
"It's unbelievable what Arsenal have done and everyone involved there should be very proud of what they have produced and made him the player he is. I cannot talk highly enough about him.
"You've got to look after him. He's quite a big lad. I wouldn't worry about him getting bullied and kicked all over the place in the Premier League. There's VAR and that just doesn't happen any more in this day and age.
"I was disappointed at the Community Shield when Arsenal were 3-0 up. I was thinking, put him on now up against the creme de la creme and they didn't put him on and I just found that a bit strange.
"He'll be playing in the cup games, and hopefully it keeps on continuing because, as I say, these talented generational players come along once in a blue moon with Gazza [Paul Gascoigne], [Wayne] Rooney and now we're looking at Dowman."
summary: Sixteen-year-old Arsenal prodigy Max Dowman scored two goals in his first appearance of the season during a 4-2 Carabao Cup victory over Ipswich Town. Manager Mikel Arteta praised the forward's natural ability and work rate off the ball, while urging caution regarding his development due to his age and the physical demands of the Premier League. Seventeen-year-old Marli Salmon also delivered an impressive performance in central defence for Arsenal during the match.
key_points: Max Dowman scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 Carabao Cup win against Ipswich Town.
Mikel Arteta emphasized the need to manage the 16-year-old carefully amid high expectations and league demands.
Dowman also contributed defensively, pressing to win the ball back for a teammate's goal.
Seventeen-year-old Marli Salmon also made his second start for Arsenal's first team and impressed at centre-back.

11 - SAVE! Bergvall kept out by the legs of Mamardashvili
21 - GOAL! Mac Allister curls the opener high into the net
32 - MISS! Kudus fails to find the target when well placed
54 - GOAL! Gakpo fires the ball home to double the lead
69 - GOAL! Gallagher nods the ball in from close range
86 - SAVE! Amazing by Mamardashvili to deny Marmoush
90+1 - GOAL! Szoboszlai's stunner seals it for the Reds
Lucas Bergvall really should have slotted Spurs in front early in the game but his close-range shot found the legs of Mamardashvili instead. And Liverpool punished them for that wastefulness when Mac Allister curled the ball high into the net for the opener.
Mohammed Kudus contrived to volley high and wide after smart work by Destiny Udogie before half-time. Liverpool were just more clinical, summed up by the manner in which Gakpo slammed in a second in front of the Kop to cap an excellent Liverpool move.
The Dutchman was a target for Tottenham in the summer. He currently has more Premier League goals this season than they do. Out of the Carabao Cup and with Richarlison out of the squad, De Zerbi's only consolation was a spirited effort at Anfield.
For Andoni Iraola, he will be encouraged by the energy and the quality in evidence. Intensity appeared to be an issue against Fulham on Saturday but the 10 changes actually helped with Lewis Koumas eager and Trey Nyoni producing a mature display in midfield.
And when Szoboszlai can do that, it makes everything easier.
Iraola: Szoboszlai goal a 'worldie'
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking in the press conference:
"Three goals we scored were very good goals; the origin of the goals for the first and second ones was also very important for us. The third one is a worldie. With other players you are thinking it is too far. With Dom you are thinking he might score."
Player of the match: Lewis Koumas
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking about Lewis Koumas in the press conference:
"I said in the week and say it for a reason; I see it in training every day. The energy that he shows is contagious for the rest. When they see the ones up front doing it, they are forced to go from behind."
Analysis: Positives for both teams
Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp on Liverpool:
"That's the best I've seen them. Obviously, Tottenham played into their hands as they're trying to play out from the back. But the number of times they (Liverpool) won it back because they were so quick and aggressive to get after them. That's what Andoni did at Bournemouth and that's what he's trying to do at Liverpool. It will take time, but they'll certainly get it."
Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp on Tottenham:
"From Tottenham's point of view, there were positives. They had a sharpness to their game. Bergvall did well. There's lots to look forward to for the weekend. It was a better performance. On another day, they could have had two or three goals. Liverpool just had enough."
De Zerbi: We need things to click
Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi speaking to Sky Sports:
"We created chances to win the game. It's not a very good moment, but I believe in my players, and I told them five minutes ago to stay calm.
"We need a click. I don't know if we are able to make this click Saturday, but playing like this and believing in ourselves and our style of play, I think we'll win many games and score many goals because the qualities of my players is very high.
"There are many, many positives. We are sorry, disappointed and frustrated for the results. I think we didn't deserve to lose, but it's the first season. We are building totally different things with me.
"I believe in my players, this project. I have no doubts. I believe in this club, but now we are not so lucky. It's not good to say too many 'ifs' but we played very well this evening."
summary: Liverpool defeated Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield to advance in the third round of the Carabao Cup. Goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Cody Gakpo, and a stoppage-time strike by Dominik Szoboszlai secured the victory for the Reds. Conor Gallagher scored Tottenham's first goal of the campaign against top-flight opposition, ending their goal drought.
key_points: Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring for Liverpool with a curled shot in the first half.
Cody Gakpo doubled Liverpool's lead with a goal in the second half.
Conor Gallagher scored for Tottenham to narrow the deficit.
Dominik Szoboszlai sealed the 3-1 win with a stoppage-time strike.
Giorgi Mamardashvili made key saves to deny Tottenham players including Omar Marmoush.

title: Max Dowman: Arsenal youngster shows his class - but Gunners wary of rushing him
author: Emlyn Begley
content:
![Max Dowman with a drinks bottle](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/b307/live/6c0e2650-b151-11f1-8912-fb2bed4049e7.jpg)
Max Dowman is the third 16-year-old to score for Arsenal in a League Cup game
- Published
Arsenal teenager Max Dowman shone with two goals in the 4-2 Carabao Cup win over Ipswich Town - but boss Mikel Arteta warned they cannot rush his development.
The 16-year-old played 13 times last season, but has had to settle for a place on the bench so far this campaign - until now.
He scored two lovely goals at Portman Road to stake his claim for more minutes in the Premier League.
But Arteta warned: "He is 16 years old and we have to be really cautious.
"We don't want to stop him, we don't want to put the brakes on him, we need to develop him and we are fully aware what he needs. He will have opportunities."
His first was a fine solo goal as he ran through, leaving defenders on the floor before slotting in.
"Unbelievable, he's unpredictable, he can go either way, so fluid, so nice to watch," said Arteta.
And for his second goal, Dowman showed good composure to place the ball in the bottom corner.
He is just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side in any competition, after Wayne Rooney for Everton against Wrexham in 2002 - which was also in the League Cup.
"With the demands that we put in them, to be able to do that is extremely difficult and he's coping better and better and better," Arteta added.
"He's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage.
"It's not easy [to contain the hype], I understand, but what we have to do is look after him. He's 16 years old. You don't see that in this league.
"In other leagues in Europe, that's a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands that the league has, the players and everything put on you, we really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he's in the right context with the right preparation."
Wonderkid had to wait
Perhaps Dowman might have expected to have more minutes this season.
His breakthrough came last season as he broke several records.
He became the youngest Champions League player ever, aged 15, Arsenal's youngest ever starter as well as the Premier League's youngest starter, goalscorer and title winner.
In 13 appearances in all competitions, he scored once - against Everton to make a win safe during the title run-in.
In fact his strike, where he ran the ball halfway down the pitch before scoring into an empty net - with Jordan Pickford upfield - was voted Arsenal's goal of the season.
And all of this while he was studying for school exams.
He received his GCSEs from Brentwood School in the summer and left school to focus on his football career.
Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp said: "He is a wonderful player who will be able to do everything in the game.
"But just give him time and how they are handling him is perfect. What you don't want to do is not give him the amount of game time he needs. He is an elite player."
Will Dowman get his chance now?
Breaking into the Arsenal first team will be a tough task for Dowman especially when the Premier League champions are in such fine form.
Arsenal have won all seven games this season, across four competitions.
Dowman was an unused substitute in four of those games, and not involved for the other two, before playing all 90 minutes against Ipswich Town.
The Gunners have played the same attackers in each league game so far - Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz.
But Dowman, especially considering Arteta turned to him in key moments in last season's title race, will hope to gain more of a supporting role.
"He's an unbelievable talent," team-mate Mikel Merino told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He will be a star in the future if he keeps his eyes and ears open and keeps learning.
"He's just 16 so he needs a lot of coaching, especially tactically. But I can't take anything away from him. He's always keen to learn. We'll keep helping him."
Quite possibly the best 16-year-old in the world, it is not unthinkable that he could earn his way into England's Euro 2028 thinking.
In fact there was even a debate about whether he should be going to the World Cup earlier this year.
"He is a real superstar," said former England defender Conor Coady on Sky Sports.
"A 16-year-old boy should not be doing this. He has got no better manager than Arteta to look after him. You want him to be looked after properly. If he plays every game at this age, he won't be scoring goals like this."
And it comes on the day it emerged highly rated 15-year-old striker JJ Gabriel is on the verge of leaving Manchester United.
Gabriel had been expected to make his debut in Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie with Brighton.
That will probably deny him the opportunity to break up the stat that the three youngest players to score in the League Cup for a Premier League side all did so for Arsenal.
They are Cesc Fabregas (16y 212d v Wolves, 2003), Dowman (16y 258d v Ipswich) and Jack Wilshere (16y 266d v Sheffield United, 2008).
summary: Arsenal teenager Max Dowman scored two goals in a 4-2 Carabao Cup win against Ipswich Town, showcasing his exceptional talent. Manager Mikel Arteta praised the 16-year-old's performance but emphasized the need to be cautious and carefully manage his development. Dowman previously set multiple records last season during his breakthrough campaign while balancing school exams.
key_points: Max Dowman scored two goals in Arsenal's 4-2 Carabao Cup victory over Ipswich Town.
Manager Mikel Arteta stressed the importance of being cautious and not rushing the 16-year-old's development.
Dowman became the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side in any competition.
He previously broke numerous records during his breakthrough campaign last season while completing his GCSEs.

title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
author: Sam Dean; Ji-Min Lee
content:
![Max Dowman's early goals in the first and second halves sent Arsenal well on their way to a midweek win](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503211172_17895060129000_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqWS14qhYPBGny4Y46-fINE1HmPOpeFd0SyQx9dn7kM_w.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Max Dowman's early goals in the first and second halves sent Arsenal well on their way to a midweek win](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503211172_17895060129000_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqWS14qhYPBGny4Y46-fINE1HmPOpeFd0SyQx9dn7kM_w.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.
Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.
The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.
As Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a new contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.
“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.
“Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”
Dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”
Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.
![tmg.video.placeholder.alt czQetXof7IE](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/czQetXof7IE/maxresdefault.jpg) 
It was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” said Arteta.
Arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.
Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.
The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.
![Marli Salmon held off Ipswich's Zian Flemming, helping his team nullify the home side's attack](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503210676_17895105762150_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq2WhK-BLojejksbeOaNeHR2QrWKkLPlXkmzjqSSq6954.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.
Akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.
Arteta: We have to look after Max
On managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”
Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:
Arteta: Dowman an unbelievable player
Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”
He added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”
![Dowman](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503217091_17895086713090_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqEzw5OF8VsBey80ir11mphkgR7PVUJ79uLnSHs-A1YSI.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Arteta: Some big individual performances
Speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta said: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.
“Individually some big performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”
Cover blown...
![Undercover Arsenal fans](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503215736_17895081171740_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqf31hxWNT7i64oktrHVICFlHmPOpeFd0SyQx9dn7kM_w.jpeg?imwidth=350)
