Struggling to get involved
Gyokeres ended up making 18 touches across the 90 minutes.
Among Arsenal’s substitutes, Julienne took 24 in 26 minutes while Odegaard had 25 in 14 minutes.
The Swede is not the type of player to take scores of touches (his average in the league last year was 18.14, so today was about on par for him), but you feel that there were opportunities for him to work into the half-spaces a bit more, as he did towards the end of the match.
87min: Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4
Arsenal are finishing this match with a 16-year-old, 17-year-old and two 18-year-olds on the pitch. A good evening for the academy.
And right on cue, Salmon picks up the ball on the halfway line and drives forward, eventually forcing a foul from Nunez who goes into the book for his troubles.
84min: Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4
Gyokeres finally gets a sniff at goal but Greaves is wise to his movement in behind and times a slide-tackle perfectly to poke the ball off for a corner.
Ibrahim comes on for Zubimendi before it is taken and joins the crew congregated at the far post but Walton punches Odegaard’s delivery away.
79min: Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4
Chance! A high regain puts Mehmeti into a promising position in the right half-space, but his cross in to Akpom comes to nothing.
Tzolis, who is booed by the home fans owing to his Norwich connections, has a glimpse at goal but is immediately closed down before Ipswich earn a corner after a swift transition but it is easily dealt with.
There is an appeal for a handball off an Arsenal defender in the second phase of the set-piece but Egeli is offside so it matters not.
76min: Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4
Just the 13 touches for Gyokeres tonight, make of that what you will...
Arteta shuffles the pack again, taking off Eze and Madueke for Tzolis and Odegaard.
![Gyokeres](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503212821_17895045798540_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqqVzuuqpFlyLIwiB6NTmJwdL7YqBqbzAUZ-BxrkX0TfE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
69min: Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4
Ipswich’s substitutes have breathed some life into their attack. Akpom fires a cross-cum-shot towards goal but strikes the side-netting.
Another couple of substitutions for O’Neil, who will now be thinking about Everton next weekend. Davis and Walle Egeli are on for Ouattara and McAteer.
67min: Ipswich Town 1 Arsenal 4
For those who are into your statistics, another Dowman goal here would create some history...
The record for the youngest hat-trick scorer across all professional tiers of English football belongs to Trevor Francis.
Playing for Birmingham City against Bolton Wanderers in Division Two on February 20, 1971, Francis scored four goals in a 4-0 win at just 16 years and 307 days old.
54min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3
Chance! It could, and maybe should, have been four. Merino threads a wonderful through-ball beyond Ipswich’s final line of defence and Madueke steals in to poke the ball across the face of goal with the outside of his left boot. Gyokeres was in the middle but could not divert the ball goalwards.
Goal! Dowman at the double
Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 3 (Dowman) Madueke picks out Zubimendi in the box who in turn finds Dowman in the right half space and he gallops on to the ball before arrowing the ball past Walton. The assist had grazed Greaves’ outstretched arm and would surely have led to a penalty had Dowman not done the honours.
Guimaraes proving his worth
Such is the midfielder’s versatility, his heat map tonight paints a wildly different picture to that from his 45 minutes at the Stadium of Light over the weekend. He has played the midfield-sentry role in Suffolk and has executed it well.
It is further evidence as to why Arteta was hell bent on signing him in the summer. You would imagine his all-conquering presence will relieve pressure from Rice and Zubimendi’s shoulders. They were out on their feet by the end of the last campaign.
Scores on the doors
L: Peterborough United 2 Barnsley 2
L: West Ham United 2 Fulham 2
HT: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
HT: Liverpool 1 Tottenham Hotspur 0
HT: Reading 0 Brentford 2
Liverpool are ahead against Spurs at Anfield thanks to this strike from Mac Allister:
Half-time: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
Arteta’s nine changes are looking fairly sensible now. He will be particularly pleased to have seen fringe players like Dowman and Madueke get on the scoresheet so emphatically. Arsenal will need their full squad to achieve their lofty goals this season and that half will give Arteta confidence that they have enough firepower to last the course.
![Dowman](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503203248_17895018682420_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqtkFNGfLQhkpVPeNfby9bQbeHsZFrEmHQDi0eQN40zhg.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
43min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
Arsenal inject a bit of calm to proceedings with a healthy spell of possession. Their horizontal and vertical rotations (Lewis-Skelly is now minding to drop into that Rice role alongside the centre-backs) are proving tricky for Ipswich to track.
Gyokeres gets a shot away after a clever run in behind by Merino but cannot get enough pace behind his strike to trouble Walton.
40min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
Mehmeti brings down a searching ball from deep and faces up to Gabriel as he enters Arsenal box. Such is the Brazilian’s poise, though, that even when the Ipswich forward appears to have worked a yard of space, he telescopes in his leg and stops Mehmeti’s advances with perfunctory ease.
37min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
Ipswich are getting more bodies forward, with both full-backs bombing on. The ball is worked out to Furlong out on the right but, in a promising position, he loses his footing and the ball rolls out of play.
Next comes a foray down the left, Philogene beats Salmon on the outside but Kepa gets down smartly to cut out his cross. The next goal will naturally go a long way to determining how this tie plays out.
27min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
Better from Ipswich! Their best shot at getting back into this contest is through counters when Arsenal are not set, and here Outtara bursts down the left before swinging in a deep cross to Flemming who cuts the ball back to Mehmeti who fires the ball just over the crossbar.
24min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
Guimaraes is slotting in between Arsenal’s split centre-backs in Arsenal’s build-up and Ipswich are not prepared to go three vs three that high up the pitch meaning the Brazilian has all the time in the world to dictate play from there. We’ve seen this all season long from Rice.
19min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 2
A flurry of chances for Ipswich. Philogene’s lopping cross is tipped away by Kepa but the ball falls to Flemming at the back post and his effort pinballs around a thicket of Arsenal limbs before reaching Florentino on the edge of the box, whose effort sails over the bar.
12min: Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1
Florentino’s loose pass is picked off by Dowman and the youngster earns a free-kick as the Ipswich midfielder attempts to recover. It’s taken quickly and Eze bursts into the box - there is a half-hearted shout for a penalty as the ball appears to strike Ouattara’s arm but the contact appears incidental and the referee waves play on.
Goal!! Dowman dances through Ipswich’s defence
Ipswich Town 0 Arsenal 1 (Dowman) Simply majestic. A simple one-two with Eze on the left has Dowman running at Ipswich’s defence. He drops his shoulder and sells Kipre a dream before stroking the ball beyond Walton. “1-0 to the champions” sing the travelling fans.
A kit question...
The players emerge from the Portman Road tunnel, Ipswich in their customary home blue shirts and white shorts, Arsenal in red and also white shorts. Last week Arsenal were made to change into red shorts to avoid a similar clash with Napoli, but apparently that’s no problem tonight. Modern football for ya!
Here’s a reminder of the line-ups in full:
Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming
Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom
Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres
Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz
Final preparations before kick-off
![Max Dowman](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503198390_17894982442490_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
![Anis Mehmeti and Jaden Philogene](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503199394_17894982550780_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqyILZCJqFaBEpuz3ivC4GStHhMh81Y8GqX3ipA8YMo0k.jpeg?imwidth=350)

Intel from Arsenal’s warm-up
Arsenal are warming up with Eze on the left, Madueke on the right and Dowman as the No 10 behind Gyokeres. In defence it looks like Zubimendi at right-back. The formation in the warm-up is not always the formation in the match, though...! They have played that trick before.
Arsenal’s three decades of League Cup hurt
Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).
Their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).
![Nico O'Reilly](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000474924911_17894976359430_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq_lMrXV9no5hl8ysG-zHDM_B4XqtrPvC_vaccYFnCNRM.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Ipswich’s summer buys come good
No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.
It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.
“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”
Some pre-match insights from Arteta on Sky
On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:
“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.
On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:
“Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”
When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:
“Let’s see.”
If you want a fight, Arsenal will have a fight. And Arsenal will win
![Arsenal are not a team to shy away from confrontation](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000502651403_17894969911550_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq9ZGtLOS1-T5GATHtVNx7gUFkQbQzhcNaUb3tpo77yGs.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies said Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”
The “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.
For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.
Saturday’s gritty 2-0 victory away to Sunderland provided evidence that Arsenal have added two more of these characters to their squad this summer.
Good test for youngster Salmon
Tonight will be a good test for young Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who is the latest high-class graduate of the Arsenal academy. Arsenal have extremely high hopes for Salmon, who made four senior appearances last season. He could be in the centre of defence or at right-back tonight. I suspect Ipswich striker Zian Flemming might try to target Salmon with some physical challenges, especially in the air. Let’s see how he handles it.
![Marli Salmon](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503190334_17894966925690_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq_fUAzNFdw__EO-2io-zmQhr5IqEs_EvWfhdIuBP1fGE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
The teams in black and white
Ipswich Town Walton; Furlong, Kipre, Greaves, Ouattara; Florentino, Nunez; McAteer, Mehmeti, Philogene; Flemming
Substitutes Palmer, Davis, O’Shea, Walle Egeli, Enciso, Clarke, Lukic, Maeda, Akpom
Arsenal Kepa; Zubimendi, Salmon, Gabriel, Lewis-Skelly; Guimarães, Merino; Dowman, Eze, Madueke; Gyokeres
Substitutes Meslier, Calafiori, Konsa, Tzolis, Odegaard, Ibrahim, Julienne, Saka, Havertz
Arteta: Dowman will get minutes
Max Dowman announced himself last season, showing off his gilded footwork in impressive cameos off the bench. Who could forget that lung-busting run and goal against Everton?
And while the 16-year-old winger featured in Arsenal’s pre-season, these will be his first minutes of senior football in the season proper. His only game time thus far has come in the Premier League 2 under-21s competition and he was not included in the match-day squad at the Stadium of Light on Saturday.
When asked about Dowman after the victory at Sunderland, Arteta said: “I wish we could have him here, but we have the limitation with the numbers that we can have. He will have his chance, he will have his minutes and he will have to earn them like anybody else. We know the talent that we have, we know the players that we have there and we need to help him and find a way to make sure he continues to develop and help the team.”
![Max Dowman](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000471720098_17894961336680_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqaBJSHwufYM_Fh0ArUj1hel5NUcTKNHKqy85KLqtvPLE.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
O’Neil: ‘Ipswich has worked hard for these moments’
Although keeping Ipswich in the Premier League must be Gary O’Neil’s primary goal, he has insisted that the club will embrace opportunities in the cups.
When asked how he would approach tonight’s tie, O’Neil said: “We’ll have a strong side, we’ve worked our socks off in the transfer window to give ourselves a strong squad. Of course, a different level to Arsenal, but we’ll be strong on Tuesday and we’ll do our best to win the game.
“The club has worked so hard to have these moments and of course it’s a cup game, but to have Arsenal and Liverpool come to Portman Road a week or so apart is what everyone has worked so hard for in recent years, so we’re going to enjoy it, we’re going to have a right go and worst thing that can happen is we lose to Arsenal.”
![Gary O'Neil](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000500760463_17894959531590_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqzsG1RmRUWpnHvml0pBVGHNHhMh81Y8GqX3ipA8YMo0k.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Arsenal academy products on show tonight
![Dowman](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503191808_17894952028570_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqILVW0RXZ3wCP2MAFKk47V_ipp6I7Wmq8QJJkq5qiFBM.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
![Marli Salmon](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503191797_17894952293320_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq0weCWf4rLkwTGzUxF1i3kJQd0gUcdddCv0EDOkSO7vg.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
![Myles Lewis-Skelly](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503190711_17894953698110_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqkJnul-JUIdMoNycZiD7ZllHmPOpeFd0SyQx9dn7kM_w.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
An intriguing Arsenal line-up
Good evening from Portman Road, where it’s a gorgeous night for football. Ipswich have made 10 changes, which is an indication of where this competition sits in their list of priorities. Arsenal have made nine.
The Arsenal line-up is quite hard to decipher. It looks like it might be Martin Zubimendi at right-back or centre-back. I’ll keep an eye on the warm-ups and report back shortly.
No VAR tonight – good news for Arteta?
Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of the Carabao Cup third-round tie between Ipswich Town and Arsenal. Mikel Arteta’s side have won all six of their matches so far this season, but travel to Portman Road fresh off an incident-filled win over Sunderland which thrust officiating back into the spotlight after Ezri Konsa conceded a penalty having been – in Arteta’s words – “judo-rolled” by Dan Ballard.
After the match, the Arsenal manager said: “I watched [the incident] 20 times and I cannot find a way to understand how to even think to give a penalty in this situation or the way the VAR has to intervene. So I don’t know what to think, really. But I’m sad, that we have to discuss, after such a beautiful game, something at this level that has the gravity of that because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship… This cannot happen.”
![Mikel Arteta](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000502608411_17894944855100_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Arteta may be pleased that VAR is not in use at this stage of the Carabao Cup, and all eyes will be on Peter Bankes who takes charge of tonight’s match against Ipswich.
This season Arsenal hope to arrest a startling League Cup record. It has been 33 years since they last lifted the trophy, during which time they have been runners-up seven times. Losing last year’s final will have also added fuel to Arsenal’s fire, and Arteta may resolve he must field a strong starting XI. In fact, he may not have much choice in his backline as Ben White has emerged as a serious injury doubt after picking up an injury at the Stadium of Light and may join Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba on the treatment table. This would likely mean starting Jurriën Timber, who is only just returning from a long-term groin issue. There is more scope for rotation in advanced positions, with Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino contenders to start.
A 90th-minute Zian Flemming winner against Crystal Palace on Saturday helped Gary O’Neil’s Ipswich to their second win in four Premier League games, a feat they required 16 matches to achieve the last time they were in the top flight. Heavy investment into Ipswich’s squad has proved fruitful thus far, though in-form striker Emersonn is expected to sit out tonight having taken a knock at Selhurst Park.
Team news is expected imminently.
summary: Sixteen-year-old Max Dowman scored two goals to help Arsenal secure a comfortable victory over Ipswich Town in the League Cup. His performance made him only the second 16-year-old to score a brace in a game for a Premier League side, joining Wayne Rooney. Manager Mikel Arteta praised Dowman's natural ability and composure while emphasizing the need to manage the hype surrounding the young player carefully.
key_points: Max Dowman scored twice against Ipswich Town, becoming the second 16-year-old to score a brace for a Premier League side after Wayne Rooney in 2002.
Mikel Arteta praised both Dowman and 17-year-old defender Marli Salmon for their standout performances against physical opposition.
Arsenal secured the victory with additional goals from Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, overcoming a late consolation goal from Chuba Akpom.
Arteta highlighted the importance of protecting Dowman and ensuring he is developed in the right context due to his young age.

title: Howard Webb accuses VAR of ‘tunnel vision’ before Haaland goal blunder
author: James Ducker
content:
![Manchester City celebrate Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the derby at Old Trafford](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503097775_17894870641200_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqn241QodPjmpbz0qwTM3y-xWPW5KszlIh0zmLpp_lLXw.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Manchester City celebrate Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the derby at Old Trafford](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503097775_17894870641200_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bqn241QodPjmpbz0qwTM3y-xWPW5KszlIh0zmLpp_lLXw.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Howard Webb has accused the video assistant referees who wrongly awarded Erling Haaland’s winning goal in the Manchester derby of having “tunnel vision”.
Webb said he was “really disappointed” in VAR Matthew Donohue for missing a “really clear subjective offside” in Sunday’s derby after admitting Enzo Fernández had affected the play before Haaland scored in Manchester City’s 1-0 win at Old Trafford.
Webb, the Pro Ref chief refereeing officer, also criticised Donohue’s assistant, Blake Antrobus, for failing to “step in and pull him out of that tunnel” by alerting him to his error, although he added that both officials were “hurting” over the incident and have been stood down until after the international break pending a full review.
Manchester United, to whom Webb formally apologised, have been shown the audio and footage of the incident “to let them know what happened”.
At no point in the official audio of the situation are either Donohue or Antrobus actually heard discussing Fernández being offside – their focus is entirely on Haaland’s position and then whether Fernández touched the ball or not.
Speaking on Match Officials Mic’d Up on TNT Sports 1 on Tuesday, Webb said Donohue had effectively become fixated on Haaland, who was initially flagged offside by the match officials, and that the VAR had failed to “truly evaluate the full impact of Fernández’s position” on United defender Lisandro Martínez and goalkeeper Senne Lammens.
“He [Donohue] has a look to see if he [Fernández] touches the ball, because then that relates to potentially knocking it to Haaland, who goes on to score,” Webb said.
“He [Fernández] doesn’t touch the ball, but he [Donohue] doesn’t truly evaluate other elements of offside. In that moment, he gets tunnel vision.
“He gets focused on Haaland, and it’s down to the rest of his team to pull him out of that tunnel, and unfortunately, that didn’t happen on this occasion.”
Webb said the appointment of assistant VARs was deliberately designed to help guard against such situations and he was disappointed that Antrobus had failed to spot Donohue’s error and rescue his colleague.
“When you watch it casually, you think, ‘Well, this is obviously offside against Fernández’,” Webb said.
“When you’re sat in that chair, and you’ve got other things going through your head in relation to the process that you need to follow to establish Haaland’s position, to follow through the attacking phase of play, you can get that tunnel-vision sort of effect.
“We’ve seen that before. We’ve put processes in place that protect us from that, with the AVAR, the assistant VAR, stepping in to pull the VAR out of that tunnel, but it didn’t happen on this occasion.”
![Howard Webb](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/09/15/TELEMMGLPICT000503009744_17894875563410_trans_NvBQzQNjv4Bq6LI2pSoH95NTG9OZ39cAIamsuMBB6H0ExnqhsKdrzOg.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Pro Ref had issued a statement on Sunday evening to swiftly acknowledge an “error of judgment”.
“We know that Erling Haaland, who was penalised on field for offside, wasn’t in an offside position,” Webb added. “But we also know that Enzo Fernández, who was in an offside position, almost certainly interfered with the Manchester United defence and probably the goalkeeper as well.
“I was really disappointed with this outcome. We all are. None more so than the officials themselves. They take a lot of personal pride in what they do and they’re obviously hurting now, having fallen short in this situation. They’ll not be officiating again until after the international break.
“We’ve reached out to Manchester United and acknowledged the error, as we do when these things happen. They don’t happen that often, but we want to ensure that we are transparent and open, and we’ve played the audio and the footage to the football club to let them know what happened, and we’re going to review this situation to understand what elements of process fell down in this situation which meant we didn’t get to the right outcome.”
Webb admitted Martínez and Lammens were affected by Fernández’s action. “As the ball comes across, we see Fernández sort of dive towards the ball. He gets close to it,” Webb said. “That impacts Martínez, who’s nearby, he can’t come and clear the ball.
“It probably impacts Lammens as well, who can’t dive in the way that he would, or he sets himself for potential contact from Fernández, and that puts him out of position for what then happens later when Fernández misses the ball and Haaland shoots.
“What looks like a really clear subjective offside, because Fernández doesn’t touch the ball but still clearly impacts … doesn’t get identified, and it’s really disappointing.
“It’s clear that Haaland is onside, we use the technology, but that’s only part of the story and the VAR gets super focused on that particular element and, in that moment, misses the evaluation of Fernández’s position, and this goal should’ve been disallowed.
“And highly unfortunately, it wasn’t, and we’ll review it, reflect upon it, and try to take the learning forward to prevent this unusual type of error from happening again.”
Webb added that referee Michael Oliver made the correct decision to send Phil Foden off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes but denied suggestions the United captain should also have been dismissed for his kick at the City player.
“When you look at the footage, there is that petulant kick by Bruno Fernandes into the backside of Foden,” Webb said.
“It is more petulant than violent. To be violent conduct, it has to have excessive force or brutality, and when you look at that, particularly in full speed, it doesn’t have those elements. So therefore, this would be a yellow card offence.
“And the VAR can’t step in to recommend the referee looks at the screen to give a yellow card. Of course, if all of this is missed and nothing is given against Foden, then the VAR could step in so the referee could see Foden’s actions for a possible red card, and they would capture Fernandes’s yellow card action. But because the referee gave the red card on the field, that option is not open to the VAR.”
Webb also claimed the law around accidental handball was a “nonsense” and needed reconsidering after United defender Harry Maguire handled the ball before miscuing a shot against Ipswich Town and watched the ball deflect in off Jacob Greaves in his side’s 5-2 win last month.
“It’s [the law around accidental handball] a bit of a nonsense, isn’t it?” Webb said. “That if he does strike the ball beautifully into the top corner, then the goal gets disallowed. He skews his shot, it becomes an own goal, and it’s awarded.
“I think the law should change away from that idea. I agree with them [the way the officials interpreted the rule], but now we’re in this ridiculous situation whereby the goal is allowed to stand because it’s an own goal.”
Despite addressing the Haaland goal controversy head on, Webb opted not to review a controversial penalty awarded to Sunderland after Arsenal centre-back Ezri Konsa was deemed to have pulled Dan Ballard to the ground when the game was goalless.
Enzo Le Fée missed the resulting penalty and Arsenal went on to win 2-0 but Mikel Arteta described the decision as “unacceptable” and said they would be contacting Pro Ref to discuss failings in the game.
summary: Howard Webb has criticized VAR Matthew Donohue for suffering from "tunnel vision" and missing a clear subjective offside during Manchester City's 1-0 win over Manchester United. Webb admitted that Enzo Fernández was in an offside position and interfered with United's defense before Erling Haaland scored the controversial winner. Both Donohue and assistant VAR Blake Antrobus have been stood down until after the international break following a formal apology to Manchester United.
key_points: Howard Webb stated that VAR Matthew Donohue suffered from "tunnel vision" and failed to evaluate Enzo Fernández's offside position during Manchester City's 1-0 derby win over Manchester United.
Webb formally apologized to Manchester United and shared the audio and footage of the incident with the club.
Both the VAR and assistant VAR have been stood down until after the international break pending a full review.
Webb also addressed other incidents, defending referee Michael Oliver's red card for Phil Foden while describing the accidental handball law as a "nonsense".

title: Manchester United shocked as talented youngster JJ Gabriel asks to leave
author: Dominic Booth
content:
Manchester United have been left confused and shocked by the news that the talented 15-year-old player JJ Gabriel has asked to leave the club, a day before he was to be included in the first-team squad to face Brighton.
Gabriel could have become United’s youngest player in the Carabao Cup third-round tie at Old Trafford on Wednesday. But the Guardian understands he has asked for his registration to be cancelled.
United are unsure what has prompted this decision and believe they have done everything they can to show Gabriel and his family there is a pathway to the first team. Those efforts have included meetings with Ruben Amorim, when the Portuguese was head coach, and Sir Alex Ferguson.
United believe the situation, first reported by the Telegraph, is rectifiable given the time remaining on Gabriel’s contract. Club officials say the player has a deal to the end of the season and cannot be deregistered despite his request. The north London-born Gabriel cannot sign a professional contract until he turns 17 in October next year, but can sign a scholarship agreement when he turns 16.
Gabriel, who has been with United since the age of 11, has emerged as one of the most exciting prospects at Carrington in years, scoring a hatful of goals for the youth teams, most recently a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut against Sabah last week. He regularly plays for older age groups at United, scoring 26 goals in 29 games last season, and has made two appearances for England Under-17s. Gabriel is also the most recent, and youngest, winner of United’s prestigious Jimmy Murphy young player of the year award. He has regularly trained with the first team.
Quick Guide
Carrick say VAR blunder will fuel United
Michael Carrick believes Manchester United will have an edge against Brighton in the Carabao Cup owing to the wrong video assistant referee decision that allowed Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s defeat by Manchester City.
United host Fabian Hürzeler’s side on Wednesday aiming to bounce back after Haaland’s 60th-minute strike was judged to be legal by the VAR, who ruled that Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup. Pro Ref admitted the goal should not have been allowed and that Matt Donohue, the VAR, had made the wrong decision. He has been stood down for this weekend's Premier League action.
Carrick, speaking before Pro Ref’s statement, was asked whether his players would have an edge against Brighton owing to their annoyance at ruling.
“It does give you something, when something like that happens, to use moving forward," the manager said. "The players have got an edge. They've shown that to me since I've been here. We've had setbacks, and they've bounced back particularly well and had some really good performances and good results."
United have taken four points from their first four games. “We've got to move on [from City loss]; we've got to win games,” said Carrick. “We have done – we've won a lot of games, and we need to continue to do that. I understand it's a new season, and the points tally right now is not what we want it to be. I'm not hiding from that, but it's more of about getting back to winning games, that feeling, getting the habit. It's easier said than done, but we're capable of it.”
Luke Shaw may be available after a knock. Jamie Jackson
Speaking after that 5-0 win against Sabah, Adam Lawrence, United’s lead under-21 coach, said: “JJ is surrounded by people that really, really believe in him from the top of the club right the way through. He’s been at the club for so long. He’s got real good relationships with the players, with the staff, so I think over the course of time obviously that helps as well.
“At the moment, just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, it’s about making sure that he’s getting the right exposure across different levels. We’re obviously not perfect but it’s definitely something we put a lot of thought into.”
after newsletter promotion
Barcelona and Manchester City have been linked previously with Gabriel, after reports emerged last year suggesting the player’s family would be planning to move him.
summary: Manchester United are shocked and confused after 15-year-old rising talent JJ Gabriel asked to cancel his registration and leave the club, just a day before he was set to join the first-team squad against Brighton. Club officials believe the situation is rectifiable because Gabriel remains under contract until the end of the season. Gabriel has been with United since age 11, has excelled in the youth ranks, and previously attracted interest from Barcelona and Manchester City.
key_points: JJ Gabriel, 15, asked to have his registration cancelled and leave Manchester United.
The request came a day before he was due to be included in the first-team squad to face Brighton in the Carabao Cup.
United officials state that Gabriel has a deal until the end of the season and cannot be deregistered.
Gabriel has been with United since age 11 and is regarded as one of the club's most exciting young prospects.
Manchester City and Barcelona have previously been linked with the player.

title: Oli McBurnie: New Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli recalls striker & names seven uncapped players in squad
author: Amy Canavan; Andy Campbell
content:
![Hull City forward Oli McBurnie](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/d9f9/live/e9030720-b0f2-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
Oli McBurnie could win his 17th Scotland cap
- Published
Oli McBurnie has been called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in five years, with new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli saying the Hull City forward fits his "style of play".
Uncapped Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken, Josh McPake and Stephen Welsh also make Pocognoli's first selection. As expected, Stoke defender Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure receive their first senior call-ups.
Scott Bain, Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and James Wilson are recalled but Che Adams misses out. Napoli midfielder Billy Gilmour, 25, returns after missing the World Cup injured.
McBurnie, 30, first featured for his country in 2018 and won the last of his 16 caps in 2021.
He has never scored for Scotland but did net one of the penalties in the shootout that sealed a place at the delayed Euro 2020 finals.
"It's a new opportunity for some players, a really new beginning for the other ones," said Pocognoli.
![The Scotland squad with a picture of Robbie Ure](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/544/cpsprodpb/8001/live/d3905580-b0ef-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg)
"I have to start a new journey, start a new book. The most important is regarding the style of play that I want to produce on the pitch. We need to adapt quick.
"To be honest, I can extend this list because I have to make some choices. There are a lot of names who can be also in that squad for that camp. Players who are not there is because for the style of play, it can be from injury or playing time.
"There's many players that I would like to call up. The door is never closed."
Binks, 25, has previously played age grade football for England and Scotland and Pocognoli said in reference to the Brondby player: "The timing was right with him."
Right-back Donovan, 20, has come to prominence filling in for injured Canada right-back Alistair Johnston in Celtic's side this season. Like McBurnie, he has been capped at under-19 and under-21 level. Pocognoli said Donovan had "played some good games" and had dealt with "expectation".
Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.
The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the country's send-off friendly win against Curacao, which was also Steve Clarke's last game in the dugout at Hampden Park.
The defender, who has three caps at under-21 level, has started strongly for The Potters in the Championship, who are unbeaten in their past four games, with Graham an ever-present.
Bain 'ticks every box' for Scotland start - Falkirk boss McGlynn
Four-time capped Falkirk goalkeeper Bain, 34, and Bradford City keeper Jon McCracken, 26, were in squads named by Pocognoli's predecessor Clarke. Bain and McCracken join Angus Gunn and Liam Kelly in the goalkeeping pool.
And Pocognoli commented: "I will not talk about my number one and number two today.
"We have a strong generation in the past. Now we need just to rebirth this but we have good quality. We have experienced goalkeepers and we have some young talents."
Pocognoli's compatriot, Heart of Midlothian head coach Wouter Vrancken, was "confident" there would be a few players from the Tynecastle club included and winger McPake, 25, and 19-year-old attacking club-mate James Wilson, who has two caps, are recognised for their early-season performances. However, Hearts winger Calvin Miller misses out.
Watch best of Josh McPake's scintillating Edinburgh derby display
Swansea City defender Stephen Welsh, 26, may win his first cap while Sassuolo forward Bowie, 23, and left-back Doig, 24, as well as Udinese midfielder Miller, 20, make the cut.
Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - that took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden and it resulted in a Â£5.5m summer transfer to La Liga with Sevilla.
Ure, 22, has yet to find the target in Spain, but given his eligibility for Ukraine, the new head coach appears tempted to tie him down as soon as possible.
"Players who are there are performing well," said Pocognoli. "Robbie is now challenging to adjust to La Liga level."
The inclusion of Bowie, McBurnie, Ure and Wilson come as reports indicate Torino's Adams is injured while Rangers forward Lawrence Shankland is out for up to four months with a hamstring injury.
Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay, 29, is unavailable, having recently had minor heart surgery.
Of the 28 named in this squad, 14 were part of this summer's World Cup.
Gunn and Kelly, defenders Jack Hendry, Aaron Hickey, Scott McKenna, Nathan Patterson, Andy Robertson and Kieran Tierney, midfielders Ryan Christie, Lewis Ferguson, John McGinn and Kenny McLean and forwards Findlay Curtis and Ben Gannon-Doak are all retained.
Goalkeeper Craig Gordon has retired while Grant Hanley has recently returned to fitness at Hibernian while Rangers defender John Souttar has not played this season amid reports linking him with Aris Thessaloniki.
Defenders Dominic Hyam and Anthony Ralston, midfielder Tyler Fletcher and forwards Lyndon Dykes, George Hirst and Ross Stewart miss out.
When asked about the possibility of calling up Scotland-qualified Newcastle winger Harvey Barnes, 28, and Everton midfielder Hayden Hackney, 24, Pocognoli said he was "aware of everything and about the feeling of everybody" and said "it's about timing."
"I don't want to convince players," he explained. "They need to be open to representing in the natural way, the country. We'll see in the future."
Since Pocognoli was announced as Clarke's successor - the former Kilmarnock manager having resigned after the Scots failed to qualify for the knockout stages of a major tournament for the first time - the expectation was that the Belgian would look to freshen up an ageing squad.
Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in the Scots' Nations League B opener against Slovenia and his debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland.
A trip to face North Macedonia on 3 October follows before a home tie with Slovenia three days afterwards.
And the Belgian said: "We have a good mix between experienced players, new faces, first cap players, young lads, players who are back.
"We have a lot of leaders, we have a lot of players who know how to win games.
"We want to be ambitious in this Nations League. We have to use this Nations League to try things, to experiment things but the most important is to be ambitious."
Scotland squad
Goalkeepers: Scott Bain (Falkirk), Angus Gunn (San Jose Earthquakes), Liam Kelly (Rangers), Jon McCracken (Bradford City)
Defenders: Luis Binks (Brondby), Josh Doig (Sassuolo), Colby Donovan (Celtic), Luke Graham (Stoke City), Jack Hendry (Al-Ettifaq), Aaron Hickey (Brentford), Scott McKenna (Dinamo Zagreb), Nathan Patterson (Torino), Andy Robertson (Tottenham Hotspur), Kieran Tierney (Celtic), Stephen Welsh (Swansea City).
Midfielders: Ryan Christie (Bournemouth), Lewis Ferguson (Bologna), Billy Gilmour (Napoli), John McGinn (Aston Villa), Kenny McLean (Norwich City), Josh McPake (Hearts), Lennon Miller (Udinese).
Forwards: Kieron Bowie (Sassuolo), Findlay Curtis (Rangers), Ben Gannon-Doak (Bournemouth), Oli McBurnie (Hull City), Robbie Ure (Sevilla), James Wilson (Hearts).
summary: New Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli has named his first squad, recalling Hull City forward Oli McBurnie for the first time in five years alongside several other returning players. The squad also features seven uncapped players, including Luis Binks, Colby Donovan, Jon McCracken, Josh McPake, Stephen Welsh, Luke Graham, and Robbie Ure. Pocognoli takes charge following Steve Clarke's departure, with the team preparing for upcoming Nations League fixtures against Slovenia, Switzerland, and North Macedonia.
key_points: Oli McBurnie received his first Scotland call-up in five years.
Seven players received their first senior call-ups to the squad.
Che Adams misses out on the squad due to reported injury.
Sebastien Pocognoli will manage his first matches in the Nations League against Slovenia and Switzerland.

title: Leeds 4-1 Newcastle: Matthias Jaissle handed first defeat as Magpies boss as Dominic Calvert-Lewin leads Elland Road rout
author: Callum Bishop
content:
Leeds 4-1 Newcastle: Matthias Jaissle handed first defeat as Magpies boss as Dominic Calvert-Lewin leads Elland Road rout
Report and free match highlights as Leeds defeat Newcastle 4-1 in the Premier League; Dominic Calvert-Lewin was the star of the show as Leeds move up to third in the table; defeat is the first for Matthias Jaissle as Newcastle boss
Monday 14 September 2026 23:57, UK
Leeds United maintained their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign with a breathless 4-1 victory over Newcastle.
Both sides came into the game with five points on the board from the opening three games, but Matthias Jaissle's bubble was emphatically burst as he suffered a dramatic first defeat as Newcastle boss.
Without the electric Anthony Elanga, the visitors offered much less of a threat and could not handle the relentless press from the home side, led by the imperious Dominic Calvert-Lewin.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Latest news and rumours: Leeds | Newcastle
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Leeds felt slighted when Matias Fernandez-Pardo, making his first start for his new club, avoided punishment for an alleged 'handball' inside the penalty area. That was soon forgotten as the hosts' dominance soon paid off.
There was an element of luck to their first, as Ao Tanaka's shot deflected off two Newcastle defenders with the last touch coming off Lewis Miley to wrong-foot Lukas Hornicek.
That then led to the Calvert-Lewin show truly beginning. The striker thought he had his eighth career goal against the Magpies with a bullet header three minutes later. However, replays showed the ball had last come off team-mate Jayden Bogle, meaning he had to settle for the assist.
The Leeds No 9 wasn't to be denied his next goal, bulldozing his way into the penalty area before calmly slotting home a third before the break.
The floodgates remained firmly open after half-time, with Noah Okafor adding a fourth - and the pick of the bunch. The forward produced a delightful weak-foot volley on the bounce, sending it arrowing into the bottom corner.
Bazoumana Toure grabbed a late consolation, but it did little to take the gloss off a thoroughly one-sided display. The result leaves Leeds sitting third at the end of the fourth round of fixtures - their highest position at this stage of a season since the 2000/01 campaign.
The key moments from Elland Road
2: NO PENALTY! Fernandez-Pardo avoids conceding spot-kick for alleged ‘handball.’
14: SAVE! Hornicek makes a top drawer save from close range to deny Bogle.
25: SAVE! Bogle again threatens as he stings the palms of Hornicek with vicious attempt.
32: GOAL! Tanaka’s deflected strike comes off TWO Newcastle players before beating Hornicek.
35: GOAL! Two in three minutes as Bogle gets last touch from Calvert-Lewin's bullet header.
41: SAVE! Best chance of the half for Newcastle as Barnes is denied from close range.
45+1: GOAL! Calvert-Lewin can’t be stopped as he finally gets his goal.
59: GOAL! Okafor gets in on the act with stunning strike on the bounce.
89: GOAL! No clean sheet for Leeds as Toure adds late consolation.
Farke hails 'outstanding' Calvert-Lewin
Leeds boss Daniel Farke speaking with Sky Sports:
“I wasn’t happy that we allowed them to score one goal. But, it doesn’t take anything away from the fact that my boys were brilliant and we fully deserved to win the game. There’s no such thing as a perfect performance though, and this is one of the rare points I have to criticise.
“We have energy, quality, good structure in and out of possession. We have a good fitness level, also. It’s not just the will, otherwise whoever had the strong will would always win the game. We have to have the right triggers and everyone needs to be spot on. It’s lots of work on the training ground to be that compact and intense.
On Dominic Calvert-Lewin:
“He’s in outstanding shape and he plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group and he’s taken the responsibility.
“His work rate is top. It’s not just scoring the goals. The way he plays for us is outstanding. He’s definitely one of the stand out strikers in the league.”
Jaissle: We didn't match Leeds physically
Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking with Sky Sports:
"That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said many times we will have ups and downs and challenges along the way. Tonight, we faced that challenge. It’s really tough. Difficult to digest, but this is a chance to learn because there’s not long until the next match at home to show the right reaction.
"You need to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against a physical and strong team. Leeds are so intense, especially at home and we couldn’t match that physicality in the first half. That was a key element. No excuses, we have to learn from it.
"Injuries are also a challenge that we need to overcome and will. This is the message I have given to the players. There will be no issue with confidence."
Carragher: Newcastle got beaten up
Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football:
"Leeds are fifth in the Premier League table since December. That should make Newcastle feel better as it has been a bad night for them when the world was watching. They have been beaten up by a really good Premier League team.
"It will be a tough season at times for Newcastle with the manager and young players finding their feet in the Premier League. They just got beaten up."
On Dominic Calvert-Lewin:
"Calvert-Lewin was unplayable. One of the greatest sights in football is seeing a centre-forward rise above everyone and attack the ball.
"Look how high his legs are. I don't think there is a better player in the air in the Premier League."
Big learning curve for Jaissle
Sky Sports News' Keith Downie on X:
"That has to be a huge learning curve for Newcastle tonight. Looking at the team sheet for that opening game against Liverpool, with a midfield two and Yoane Wissa in the No 10, it looked like they were going to get overpowered.
"They didn't. Perhaps it was the emotion of the Kevin Keegan tributes, maybe it was because it was the opening game, or perhaps it was the Alexander Isak motivation. There was a lot going on that day.
"But Leeds away on a Monday night, you need physicality & runners. Even a midfield three of Bruno Guimaraes-Sandro Tonali-Joelinton would find that a tough match tonight.
"Newcastle were bullied by Leeds' physicality and numerical advantage in the engine room.
"It's a long season, and it's been a very good start, but that's a real eye opener for the the new Newcastle manager."
summary: Leeds United defeated Newcastle United 4-1 at Elland Road in the Premier League, maintaining their unbeaten start to the season and handing Matthias Jaissle his first defeat as Newcastle manager. Dominic Calvert-Lewin starred in the rout, helping Leeds move up to third in the table after goals from Ao Tanaka, Calvert-Lewin, and Noah Okafor overwhelmed the visitors. Bazoumana Toure scored a late consolation goal for Newcastle, but Leeds dominated a one-sided match defined by their relentless pressing and physicality.
key_points: Leeds United defeated Newcastle United 4-1 to maintain their unbeaten start to the Premier League campaign.
The result handed Matthias Jaissle his first defeat since taking over as Newcastle boss.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin put on an imperious performance, scoring one goal and contributing heavily to Leeds' dominant display.
Noah Okafor added a fourth goal for Leeds with a stunning weak-foot volley before Bazoumana Toure scored a late consolation for Newcastle.
The victory lifts Leeds to third in the Premier League table after four rounds of fixtures.

title: Leeds v Newcastle: How the players rated
author: Ciaran Kelly
content:
![Dominic Calvert-Lewin celebrates after scoring for Leeds United against Newcastle United](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/770/cpsprodpb/ecf4/live/ed0d6f70-b07c-11f1-9592-33d1ede95560.jpg)
Dominic Calvert-Lewin has won 12 caps for England
- Published
Dominic Calvert-Lewin wreaked havoc as Leeds United moved up to third place in the Premier League table following a 4-1 win against Newcastle United at Elland Road.
Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.
Leeds United
James Trafford: A relatively comfortable night against his former suitors. A couple of nervy clearances early on but went on to make an important save to deny Harvey Barnes. 7
James Justin: Teasing cross set up Leeds' second goal. Has become a key component in this system. 7
Nico Elvedi: Only his second Premier League start yet already looks at home at Elland Road. Solid at the back but got it all wrong at the other end after volleying wide at the back post when unmarked. 7
Tarik Muharemovic: The club's player of the month for August for a reason. Made it look rather comfortable at the back on Monday night. 7
Jayden Bogle: Second goal credited to him. Did not know much about it, but has found his shooting boots after his goal at Brighton last time out in the league. Twice forced Lukas Hornicek into big saves before second goal took final touch off him. A real threat. 8
Anton Stach: Won a corner inside 32 seconds. That set the tone for Leeds' relentless display, even if he later wasted chance to score. 7
Ethan Ampadu: Ensured Leeds kept pushing for more as he barked instructions. Saw Dominic Calvert-Lewin inadvertently block a vicious goalbound effort. 7
Ao Tanaka: His goal took two heavy deflections but had the confidence to take the shot. Looking back to his best in recent weeks even if he was relieved to see one misplaced pass unpunished. 7
Gabriel Gudmundsson: Caused Newcastle real problems with his runs down the left. Looked more a winger than a wing-back. 7
Noah Okafor: Fine strike for Leeds' fourth, having also coolly pulled the ball back for Tanaka to let fly for his side's opener. 8
Dominic Calvert-Lewin: Just loves this fixture. A trademark header came off Bogle for Leeds' second and then showed other side of his game to finish calmly on the floor for the hosts' third. Has scored eight goals against Newcastle - more than any other side. 9
Subs:
Melvin Bard (on 72, Gudmundsson): Perfect environment to make his Premier League debut. 6
Brenden Aaronson (on 72, Tanaka): Lots of energy. 6
Harry Wilson (on 72, Okafor): Eager to impress. 6
Lukas Nmecha (on 78, Calvert-Lewin): 6
Daniel James (on 83, Bogle)
Sean Longstaff (on 88, Stach)
Subs not used: Zetterer, Bijol, Bahoya, Nmecha
Newcastle United
Lukas Hornicek: This would have been even uglier for the visitors were it not for Hornicek making fine saves to twice deny Bogle and also to foil Calvert-Lewin. 6
Amar Dedic: Shook off hamstring issue to start, but a tough night as Leeds repeatedly targeted his flank. 4
Malick Thiaw: Captain for night but this was far from a captain's performance. Beaten easily by Calvert-Lewin for Leeds' second goal, slapped turf in frustration after the striker fired past him for the third and then failed to block Okafor's fourth. 3
Sven Botman: Like Thiaw, could not cope with Calvert-Lewin and was skinned so easily for Leeds' second goal. 3
Lewis Hall: Dragged out of position in build-up of Leeds' second goal. Not the night he had in mind after signing a new deal. 4
Nico Gonzalez: Belatedly came off after just 19 minutes after the ball struck him in the head in the early stages. 5
Lewis Miley: Little he could do for deflection for Tanaka's goal, but was overrawed by Leeds' tenacious midfield. Had little time to find passing rhythm. 4
Jacob Murphy: Continued in injured Anthony Elanga's absence, but did not offer enough protection and caused Leeds few problems going the other way. 3
Yoane Wissa: Created Newcastle's best chance and at least battled and chased, even if his final ball was not always great. 5
Harvey Barnes: Has a fearsome record against Leeds and eyes lit up when he danced inside the box only for Trafford to deny him. 5
Matias Fernandez-Pardo: Full debut following his Â£51.4m move from Lille. Had little to feed off as Newcastle repeatedly played long balls forward. 4
Subs:
Sean Steur (on 19, Gonzalez): Thrown into the cauldron after Gonzalez went off. Could do little about deflection before Leeds' first goal but gave the ball away in build up to Leeds' second. Eighteen-year-old will learn from experience. 4

Joe Willock (on 58, Fernandez-Pardo): One decent chance landed on roof of net from tight angle. 5

title: VARs who wrongly confirmed Haaland’s goal at Manchester United are stood down
author: Paul MacInnes
content:
The video assistant referee officials who allowed Erling Haaland’s winning goal in the Manchester derby on Sunday have been stood down. Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, have been told by Pro Ref they have not received appointments for this weekend’s round of Premier League fixtures.
Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer, took the decision with his management team after a review of the weekend’s action. Their availability will be reconsidered after the international break.
Donohue was called on to check Michael Oliver’s decision to disallow Haaland’s 60th-minute goal for offside. Using semi-automated offside technology, Donohue was able to establish that the Manchester City striker was onside and he overturned Oliver’s call. But he failed to spot Enzo Fernández had influenced play from an offside position, an infringement which Pro Ref said should have led him to recommend an on-field review.
This is the first time officials have been made to stand down this season owing to an error. Donohue, an EFL referee since 2018, has taken charge of three Championship matches this season as well as his VAR work. His EFL profile says he has completed Pro Ref’s “Enhanced VAR Training Programme”. Antrobus is also an assistant referee in the Premier League and ran the line in the first three matchdays.

summary: The VAR officials responsible for incorrectly allowing Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby have been stood down for the upcoming weekend of Premier League fixtures. Matt Donohue and his assistant, Blake Antrobus, failed to spot that Enzo Fernández had influenced play from an offside position. Pro Ref acknowledged the error in judgment and contacted Manchester United to explain the mistake.
key_points: VAR Matt Donohue and assistant Blake Antrobus were stood down by Pro Ref following a review of the weekend's action.
The officials correctly overturned an offside call on Erling Haaland's goal using semi-automated technology, but missed an offside infringement by Enzo Fernández.
Pro Ref acknowledged an error of judgment and contacted Manchester United to explain the mistake.
The availability of the officials will be reconsidered following the international break.

title: Man Utd: Pressure on Michael Carrick increasing after Man City defeat, says Gary Neville
author: Gary Neville
content:
Man Utd: Pressure on Michael Carrick increasing after Man City defeat, says Gary Neville
Manchester United failed to beat 10-man Manchester City despite Phil Foden's first-half red card; Gary Neville says United's game management was poor and believes next Sunday's trip to Fulham is a "real pressure game" for Michael Carrick after joint-worst start to a Premier League season
Monday 14 September 2026 11:46, UK
Gary Neville described Manchester United's derby defeat as a "bad day" for Michael Carrick's side, with the pressure increasing after failing to beat 10-man Manchester City at Old Trafford.
United failed to make their numerical advantage count after Phil Foden was sent off early on in the first half, losing 1-0 to Erling Haaland's controversial winner.
Refereeing body Pro Ref admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner just hours after the final whistle.
They revealed it had made contact with Manchester United to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" with Enzo Fernandez, in an offside position, potentially impacting play.
Sky Sports News understands United have received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision.
