- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺
Despite contention around the goal, Neville said the failure to beat 10-man City was a major concern, particularly given United's struggles to manage the game.
"Michael Carrick can be angry about the goal but he should also be angry about the performance," Neville said on the Gary Neville Podcast.
"It was an awful last 10 minutes from an experience perspective for Manchester United because that's where you think, to be fair, you throw the kitchen sink at it, and you're building the crowd up and the pressure up and it's a pressure cooker and you get a goal."
Neville believes Sunday's defeat also highlighted a wider problem with United's apparent inability to navigate matches after an opponent has a player sent off.
United have now lost three games in the last year to 10 men, including a 1-0 defeat to Everton last season following Idrissa Gana Gueye's red card at Old Trafford.
The result leaves United with just four points from four games, matching the club's worst start to a Premier League season. Carrick's record after four games is identical to Ruben Amorim's at this point last season.
Neville acknowledges that it is still early in the season but warns that there are already concerning signs, with the pressure continuing to increase on Carrick.
"It was a bad day for Manchester United, it really was," he said.
"You're losing a derby, it's a shocking day anyway. I've lost derbies myself, it's awful, but then to not score a goal against 10 men is not what I expected today. I expected goals from Manchester United.
"It is early but there are some concerning signs. They're not playing well in matches and they're also struggling in matches.
"Even the game against Ipswich; Ipswich were good for 55 minutes and caused big problems. They could have scored two or three, so there's some questions building."
United's next game is away to Fulham on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, and Neville believes the pressure will increase on Carrick.
"Next Sunday against Fulham, that becomes a real pressure game now because obviously Fulham have not started the season that well," said Neville.
summary: Pressure is mounting on Manchester United manager Michael Carrick following a 1-0 derby defeat to 10-man Manchester City. Despite refereeing body Pro Ref admitting an error regarding City's controversial winning goal, Gary Neville criticized United's poor game management and inability to capitalize on their numerical advantage. The defeat leaves United with only four points from four matches, matching their joint-worst start to a Premier League season.
key_points: Manchester United lost 1-0 to 10-man Manchester City after Phil Foden received a first-half red card.
Pro Ref admitted a VAR error regarding Erling Haaland's controversial winning goal and apologized to United.
Gary Neville criticized Manchester United's poor game management and failure to score against 10 men.
United have accumulated only four points from four games, marking their joint-worst start to a Premier League season.
Michael Carrick faces a high-pressure match in their upcoming fixture away against Fulham.

title: US Open 2026 results: How Alexander Zverev turned tears into triumph in New York
author: Paul Battison; Phil Cartwright
content:
![Alexander Zverev kisses the US Open trophy](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/5f3a/live/c451bc80-afd2-11f1-bc1f-3f186ca4140c.jpg)
Alexander Zverev is the second German man to win the US Open in the Open era after Boris Becker
- Published
As he stepped up to the baseline, Alexander Zverev could be forgiven for letting his mind slip back to the last time he served for the US Open title.
Six years ago, the German top seed threw away a two-set lead in a devastating loss to Dominic Thiem, having served for the match in the fifth set.
This time, instead of his own nerves, it was American Ben Shelton and the majority of the 24,000-strong crowd that stood in Zverev's way.
But this was a different Zverev: a Grand Slam champion now, having won the French Open in June.
Such was his focus that he did not initially realise he had sealed a 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 victory.
After firing down another unstoppable serve to win the match, Zverev returned to the baseline ready to start the next point - only to be told by his team the match was over.
"In that moment I was in the zone a lot. I didn't hear noise at all," Zverev said.
"It's funny - tennis teachers always tell you to just play the next point and forget about the score.
"At that moment I forgot about the score and it helped me."
As the realisation sunk in, the 29-year-old broke into a broad and slightly surprised smile before raising his arms above his head.
It was a direct contrast to his defeat by Thiem in 2020, where a tearful Zverev said during the trophy presentation: "I wish one day I can bring the trophy home."
Now, his wish has come true.
"We went 30 years without winning a Grand Slam title and now we've won two in three months," said Zverev.
"2026 is the outcome of all the years that happened before."
Zverev's parents were not there for his previous final at Flushing Meadows, but his father and coach Alexander senior was on the sidelines this time.
As well as paying tribute to his father, Zverev also thanked his mother for her support following his type 1 diabetes diagnosis as a child.
"When doctors tell you that life and sports will be very limited for that child, it takes a very strong mother to say 'my son will be whatever he wants to be'," Zverev said.
"My mother is the most important and strongest person I know."
'He was in a trance-like state'
World number two Zverev has enjoyed his best year on the Tour, reaching the semi-finals at the Australian Open and the final at Wimbledon alongside his French Open and US Open successes.
He has been aided by injuries to Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz, who swept the majors in the past two seasons, but a strengthened mentality and dedication to fitness has also helped.
"There is no-one as fit as Zverev, he is right up there," former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli said on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"You can argue about Alcaraz and Sinner, and Novak [Djokovic] and Rafa [Nadal] when they were in their prime physically, but Zverev is right up there as one of the best athletes to play the sport."
Zverev was taken to five sets in his first two matches, with both finishing in the early hours of the New York morning.
He was two points from defeat in the first round, but rallied, played his way into form and did not drop a set from the third round until the final.
Faced with a partisan crowd against Shelton, Zverev did not buckle. He kept his emotions deliberately in check and, even though he lost the third set, never loosened his grip on the match.
"I'm so admiring of his strength of character and the zen-like state he's been in since the very beginning of the match," said former British number one Annabel Croft.
"The most extraordinary thing - and I don't think I've ever witnessed it - was that he didn't realise he had won.
"It was so bizarre, but it was like he was in a trance-like state while he was playing."
![Alexander Zverev celebrates winning the US Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/975/cpsprodpb/aa68/live/bff50300-afdb-11f1-85da-1d41c9633ce8.jpg)
Alexander Zverev is now a two-time Grand Slam champion
His serve - one of the best on the ATP Tour - was key against Shelton.
He won 39 of 42 points behind his first serve in the first two sets and did not face a break point until the middle of the third.
Shelton broke at the end of the third set to extend the match but the American made little impact in return games from then on, winning only four of 20 receiving points in set four
Victory means he will now have the world number one ranking in his sights - he trails Sinner by 1,810 points with two Masters 1000 events and the season-ending ATP Tour finals to come.
But Zverev is a polarising figure in tennis.
In October 2023, he was given a penalty order and fined 450,000 euros (Â£392,000) for bodily harm against his ex-partner, with whom he shares a child.
Zverev denied the claims and lodged an objection against the order. A trial in May 2024 was discontinued after a week and there was a separate settlement between Zverev and his ex-girlfriend.
At the time, the court told BBC Sport: "The decision is not a verdict and it is not a decision about guilt or innocence."
Zverev was also accused in October 2020 of physical violence and controlling behaviour by another former girlfriend. He maintained his innocence from the start and there were no legal proceedings.
summary: Alexander Zverev defeated American Ben Shelton 6-3 7-6 (7-2) 5-7 6-2 to win the 2026 US Open title, becoming the second German man to win the tournament in the Open era. Six years after suffering a devastating defeat in the 2020 US Open final, the 29-year-old maintained supreme focus and initially did not realize he had won the match. The victory marks Zverev's second Grand Slam title of the year, following his triumph at the French Open in June.
key_points: Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton in four sets to claim the 2026 US Open title.
He became the second German man in the Open era to win the US Open, following Boris Becker.
Zverev was so focused during the match that he did not realize he had won until his team informed him.
The victory adds to his Grand Slam success in 2026, which also includes winning the French Open in June.
Zverev previously lost the 2020 US Open final to Dominic Thiem after holding a two-set lead.

title: Alexander Zverev claims first US Open after four-set battle with Ben Shelton
author: Tumaini Carayol
content:
For a passing moment at the end of a rugged third set, hope sprung anew for Ben Shelton. He had been outserved and outplayed for nearly three hours, but at 6-5 in the third set, one game from defeat, the American finally broke through. He burst into the return game finally pounding his forehand freely and he willed himself into an unexpected fourth set.
After he had finished pumping his fist, cupping his ear to the crowd and admirably trying to initiate a drastic momentum shift, the next sequence was most revealing. Shelton opened the fourth set with a shaky game, immediately losing his serve at the start of the set. He worked hard until the end, but he was beaten by Zverev, the top seed, who closed out a 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 victory to lift his second grand slam title of the year.
Having started his season desperately searching for his first major title, Zverev has become just the fourth man in the open era, after Jimmy Connors, Guillermo Vilas and Jannik Sinner to win his first two grand slam titles in the same campaign. He ended Shelton’s hopes of becoming the first Black American man since Arthur Ashe in 1968 and the first American man since Andy Roddick in 2003 to win the US Open.
Perhaps the most relevant detail in this rivalry is the head to head. Zverev now leads Shelton 6-0, a comfortable match-up for the German who served far better than Shelton, remained far steadier from the baseline and, as usual, nullified the effects of the left-hander’s forehand with the quality of his elite two-handed backhand.
In a match between two of the biggest servers, the first job for both players was to take care of his service. A visibly tense Shelton served terribly during the decisive moments of the first set, double-faulting on break point in the first game of the match. Shelton then double-faulted on set point to hand over a second break. He was no match for Zverev from the baseline, and his forehand was far too erratic. Zverev, meanwhile, served extremely well throughout the match, landing 69% of first serves and winning 85% of first-serve points.
Shelton managed to build rhythm behind his service games in set two, putting Zverev under some pressure by forcing a tie-break, but the German handled the most important moment of the match well. He snatched the first mini-break with an excellent forehand passing-shot winner off a timid approach from Shelton, then he ended a similarly tense exchange with a vicious down-the-line forehand to take the second mini-break. Two big unreturned serves later, Zverev led 5-0 in the tie-break and the set was all but over.
Although Shelton worked hard to force a fourth set, it did not take long for Zverev to close out a victory that appeared inevitable from the first game.
![Ben Shelton face down on the court after a gruelling rally](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/600adf8216e42287394f89a5c0df65241a7d3e3d/0_0_2738_1825/master/2738.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
This match was a fitting ending to a dreary grand slam season on the ATP tour that has been dictated by the injuries and physical issues suffered by Carlos Alcaraz, who returned from a long injury layoff at this tournament, and Jannik Sinner. Their challenges presented so many players at the top of the sport with golden opportunities to step up and compete for major titles, but so few of them over the past five months even managed to put themselves in real contention. Zverev has been rewarded for his consistency and ability to continue to put himself in positive positions deep in the majors. Each victory has clearly strengthened him mentally.
For plenty of tennis fans and viewers around the world, however, no amount of on-court success can erase the discomfort that comes with seeing Zverev succeed. He has been accused by two of his former girlfriends, Olya Sharypova and Brenda Patea, of physical abuse. In June 2024, during his run to the French Open final, Zverev settled an assault case against him in Germany for allegedly pushing and strangling Patea, his ex-girlfriend and the mother of their daughter. The case was declared no verdict, with a court spokesperson stating: “The truth remains open.” Zverev denied those charges and he has denied all allegations against him.
after newsletter promotion
At the Australian Open last year, Zverev was heckled by a fan before his trophy ceremony speech, with the fan declaring: “Australia believes Olya and Brenda.” Zverev’s three grand slam finals this year have progressed without issue and he remains a popular player at major tournaments.
For Shelton, who began his North American hard court swing attempting to recover from a painful first round loss at Wimbledon, the greatest summer of his career included a second Masters 1000 title at the Canadian Open, a first grand slam final and a new career high ranking of No 4.
His success is testament to his continued improvement and at 23 years old there is much more to come. However, some of those deficiencies, particularly his ground game and return of serve, can still be exposed by the elite, as it was during his lonely Sunday afternoon inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
summary: Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton in a four-set match, 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2, to claim his first US Open title and his second grand slam title of the year. Zverev extended his head-to-head lead over Shelton to 6-0 through superior serving and steady baseline play. The victory marks a successful season for Zverev amid a grand slam year affected by injuries to other top players, while Shelton achieved a new career-high ranking of No 4 after reaching his first grand slam final.
key_points: Alexander Zverev defeated Ben Shelton 6-3, 7-6 (2), 5-7, 6-2 to win the US Open.
Zverev became the fourth man in the open era to win his first two grand slam titles in the same campaign.
Zverev leads his head-to-head match-up against Shelton 6-0.
Ben Shelton reached his first grand slam final and achieved a new career-high ranking of No 4.
Zverev has faced past allegations of physical abuse from former girlfriends, which he has denied.

title: Man Utd 0-1 Man City: Erling Haaland's controversial winner follows Phil Foden's contentious red card in dramatic Manchester derby
author: Sam Blitz
content:
Man Utd 0-1 Man City: Erling Haaland's controversial winner follows Phil Foden's contentious red card in dramatic Manchester derby
Report and free match highlights as Man City beat Man Utd 1-0 in the Manchester derby; Phil Foden was controversially sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes; United hit the post twice but Erling Haaland put City ahead, but Enzo Fernandez was offside in the build-up for the winner
Sunday 13 September 2026 21:38, UK
Erling Haaland's contentious winner earned 10-man Manchester City a derby win over rivals United at Old Trafford - after Phil Foden's controversial first-half red card.
City have now joined Arsenal as Premier League title race pace setters with maximum points from four games - but their winning goal against Man Utd was given via an "error in judgement" by the officials.
In the build-up to Haaland's winner, Enzo Fernandez looked like he impacted play when clearly in an offside position - but the goal was not ruled out. Refereeing body Pro Ref admitted their mistake in awarding the goal three hours after the full-time whistle.
City, however, will feel justice was done after their job became much harder when Foden was given his marching orders earlier. A tepid first half of the 199th Manchester derby was dominated by Foden's shock sending-off.
After United captain Bruno Fernandes kicked the ball into his midriff, Foden reacted by kicking out at the Portuguese. "VAR has described it as a kick with both feet into the stomach," said Gary Neville on co-commentary.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Watch FREE PL highlights
- Latest news and rumours: Man Utd | Man City
- Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Whether there was enough contact from Foden to cross the violent conduct threshold will be debated. Whether Fernandes should have also seen red for kicking out at Foden first will also be talked about.
Despite the man advantage, United struggled to use their dominance to full effect. They did hit the post twice through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo - but when Haaland is on the other team, City always have a chance.
That came true as he tapped home at the back post, yet the offside flag went up. The semi-automated offside technology ruled Haaland onside so the goal was given - but Fernandez being clearly offside and trying to get on the end of the same cross was also approved by VAR.
The Premier League Match Centre claimed the goal was allowed because Fernandez did not touch the ball - when the rules state that is not necessarily relevant, as impacting the play is the crucial line in the rulebook.
While the conversation over the Foden red card and the Haaland winner will go on, City will see themselves as real contenders for the title after a gutsy display with 10 men.
United, who saw Bryan Mbeumo denied a late leveller by a stunning Gianluigi Donnarumma save, will ask themselves why they didn't have the quality to hurt a transitional City with an extra man.
WATCH: The two big calls
The key moments from Old Trafford
23: RED CARD! A slow-starting derby explodes into life as Foden is sent off for kicking two feet out at Fernandes.
45+1: OFF THE POST! Man Utd struggle to fashion chances after the sending-off, but Rashford's 28-yard free-kick comes off the foot of the woodwork.
51: OFF THE POST AGAIN! Mainoo's curling effort beats Donnarumma but lands on the foot of the post.
60: GOAL! Haaland taps home at the far post but is flagged offside. After a lengthy check, Haaland is deemed onside by the semi-automated offside technology - but was Fernandez offside in the build-up?
68: OFF THE POST! Fernandez nearly doubles City's lead but his drive is tipped onto the post by Senne Lammens.
86: WIDE! Harry Maguire has United's best chance of a leveller but he nods wide at a corner.
90+5: WHAT A SAVE! Donnarumma denies Mbeumo late equaliser with amazing stop!
Man Utd furious with Haaland winner standing
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez to Sky Sports: "I think [Fernandez] was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He was there! I went to him because he was in front of me. That's why Haaland was free at the back.
"I want to be calm but it is so hard. Every season the officials come to our club and spend an hour explaining the rules and they look so confident with that.
"Then after, five or six people (officials) doing this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable. We have to go home with this injustice."
Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick: "The explanation I got was that he wasn't interfering with play. I just don't get it, I really don't get it.
"If that's how the rules are interpreted, that you're not interfering with play because you've thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Licha [Martinez] has to react from.
"On top of that, the [offside] was a bit dubious - where we drew the line to start with. It's worrying if that's really how the game is seen by those who are officiating it."
Maresca: Fernandes should have been sent off on top of Foden!
Man City head coach Enzo Maresca:
"I think Phil Foden's red card is a red card, but I also think that in the same action it's a red card for Bruno Fernandes.
"I reviewed the action immediately after the red card on the bench. And it's a clear red card for Phil, because it's a reaction.
"But you can also see in the same action Bruno's intention. So for me, yes, it's a red card for Phil, but it's also a red card for Bruno.
On Man City's winner: "I think Erling was onside and Enzo doesn't interfere with the action."
How the pundits reacted to Foden red card
Roy Keane: "Foden does react. The strange thing is that Fernandes gives a kick...for me, he is the one who is violent here. I don't think it's a red card for Foden, l really don't."
Micah Richards: "Fernandes catches him! I don't agree with Foden's response, but it's Fernandes who started it."
Gary Neville: "It looks like Foden has reacted. He has kicked him in the stomach. You are not going to get away with that."
summary: Manchester City defeated Manchester United 1-0 in the derby thanks to an Erling Haaland goal, despite playing with 10 men following a controversial first-half red card for Phil Foden. Refereeing body Pro Ref later admitted an error in judgment allowed the goal to stand, as Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position during the build-up. Despite hitting the woodwork multiple times and having an extra player, United failed to equalize and missed the chance to secure a result.
key_points: Phil Foden was shown a controversial red card in the first half for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes after Fernandes kicked the ball into him.
Erling Haaland scored the winning goal for Manchester City by tapping in at the back post in the second half.
Refereeing body Pro Ref admitted an error after the match, conceding that Enzo Fernandez impacted play from an offside position during the build-up to Haaland's goal.
Manchester United hit the goalpost twice through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, and had a late equalizer denied by goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

title: Spanish Grand Prix result: Kimi Antonelli wins after Lando Norris loses lead because of virtual safety car timing
author: Andrew Benson
content:
![Kimi Antonelli raises his hand in celebration after winning the Spanish Grand Prix. An image of the Italian flag on a screen can be seen behind him](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/b2ac/live/923150e0-af86-11f1-913a-7151f234deb3.jpg)
Kimi Antonelli has won eight of the 14 grands prix so far this season
- Published
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix after McLaren's Lando Norris lost out because of the timing of a virtual safety car.
Norris was leading comfortably from pole position when the VSC was called on lap 15. The timing was terrible for the world champion - he had already passed the pit entry when the VSC was called.
That meant Antonelli and Red Bull's Max Verstappen were able to pit under the VSC, saving time, while the caution period ended before Norris could make it around to the pits again.
He did then come in but, to make matters worse, the stop was slow and he rejoined in fifth place.
Norris was able to recover only to third around the new Madring track in Madrid where overtaking is next to impossible.
Antonelli's eighth win in 14 races this year puts an even tighter stranglehold on the championship for the Italian.
He is now 81 points ahead of team-mate George Russell, who finished fifth after a difficult race on a confusing strategy, and 101 clear of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who retired early on with brake failure.
"It's good to win but it doesn't feel as good because Lando deserved to win," Antonelli said.
Norris said: "We'll take it on the chin. There could be more wins this year."
The key stories of the maiden Madring race were:
- Norris' terrible luck with the VSC depriving him of a likely third victory this year after a brilliant pole on Saturday
- Antonelli's fortune in a season that is surrendering to him, as well as him grabbing it by the throat with his performances
- The difficulty of overtaking on a new track designed from a clean sheet of paper, yet without obvious passing places
Norris knew that holding on to the lead would be tough from pole but he robustly defended from Antonelli into the first corner.
The Mercedes driver cut the chicanes at Turns One and Two, and again at Turns Five and Six, each time getting into the lead, each time having to give it back.
After that, Norris looked to be in control of the race as he extended his advantage progressively, moving 5.6 seconds clear 10 laps in, and 6.2 when Lance Stroll's Aston Martin stopped at Turn 20 with brake failure.
The VSC was called, but Norris had already reached the pit straight, while Antonelli and Verstappen had not and could come in.
Norris came in the next time around, but the VSC ended a couple of corners before he reached the entry to the pits, allowing the cars still on track to get back up to racing speed - a stop under a safety car saves a driver about 10 seconds over one under green-flag conditions.
To make matters worse, McLaren's mechanics had trouble with both the right-hand side wheels, and the stop took seven seconds rather than the usual two.
Norris came out in fifth place, 6.3secs behind Russell, and his hopes of winning were gone.
At the front, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc, who had been running fourth before the VSC, stayed out, having started the race on hard tyres rather than the mediums chosen by Antonelli and Norris and the softs Verstappen had.
Leclerc stayed out, and led the race with Antonelli close behind but the gap fluctuated as the Mercedes driver managed his tyres.
Ferrari kept Leclerc out as long as possible, hoping for a second safety car to enable him to make his own cheap stop.
But one never came, and Leclerc had to pit eventually, on lap 48 with nine to go. He resumed in fourth behind Antonelli, Verstappen and Norris.
Norris had closed all his deficit to Verstappen by the final stages and was running right on the Dutchman's tail in the closing laps, but was unable to pass.
The closest he came was with two laps to go as Verstappen stumbled over some lapped cars, but despite a mistake at Turn Five, the Dutchman was able to hold on.
Officials briefly looked at an incident with two laps to go when he cut a chicane while fighting to stay ahead of Norris, who complained Verstappen should give the place up. But no action was taken.
- Image source, Getty Images![Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli and McLaren driver Lando Norris](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/cf0b/live/672232a0-af8d-11f1-913a-7151f234deb3.jpg) Image caption, Kimi Antonelli and Lando Norris were in relaxed mood before the race in Madrid
1 of 6
Overtaking proves to be almost impossible
Russell ended up a lonely fifth after starting on the hard tyres and then moving on to a strategy that saw him switch to medium tyres at the VSC, and then have to stop again for hards at about half distance.
He spent much of the race debating strategy with his team before being told to be quiet and they would debate it afterwards.
Red Bull's Liam Lawson took sixth, ahead of Alpine's Franco Colapinto and McLaren's Oscar Piastri, delayed by a front wing issue after colliding with Russell on the first lap.
Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad took ninth place from Audi's Nico Hulkenberg with two laps to go.
The drivers had warned that overtaking would be almost impossible, and so it proved.
The pressure that was already there to rethink the layout for next year and provide a longer straight and big braking zone to allow overtaking will be significant.
Rethinking the fractured and overly extensive breadth of the paddock and pits complex - which covers a vastly greater distance than anywhere else - would also be a good idea.
Top 10
1. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)
2. Max Verstappen (Red Bull)
3. Lando Norris (McLaren)
4. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari)
5. George Russell (Mercedes)
6. Liam Lawson (Red Bull)
7. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)
8. Oscar Piastri (Mclaren)
9. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)
10. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)
What's next?
Formula 1 says goodbye to Europe and heads to Azerbaijan for the first of a triple header, from 24-26 September. The race in Baku takes place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijani national day on the Sunday.
summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli won the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid after McLaren's Lando Norris lost his comfortable lead due to an unfortunately timed virtual safety car. Norris had already passed the pit entry when the VSC was called, and subsequent slow pit stops dropped him down the order before he recovered to finish third. Antonelli's eighth win of the season extends his championship lead, with Max Verstappen finishing second.
key_points: Kimi Antonelli secured his eighth victory of the season, extending his championship lead.
Lando Norris lost the race lead after unfortunate timing and a slow pit stop during a virtual safety car.
Max Verstappen finished second, holding off a late charge from Norris on a track where overtaking proved nearly impossible.
The maiden race in Madrid highlighted significant design flaws regarding the difficulty of overtaking on the new track layout.

title: Premier League schedule today: How to watch, TV channels & live stream
author: Graham Ruthven
content:
The first Manchester Derby of the season comes at an interesting time for both clubs. City are building momentum under new manager Enzo Maresca while United are attempting to move on from a summer that raised questions about their transfer market strategy.
After conceding two goals in each of their three league games so far, Manchester United have made their worst defensive start to a season since 1972. Meanwhile, Manchester City would win their opening four Premier League games for a record seventh time with victory at Old Trafford.
United got the better of City in last season’s league meeting at the Theatre of Dreams. A lot has changed since then, but the Manchester Derby is always one of English soccer’s fiercest fixtures.
Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s Premier League fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks, and online streaming options.
Manchester United v Manchester City
Time (ET): 4.30pm BST (11.30am ET)
Stadium: Old Trafford (Manchester)
How to watch
United States: Stream on Fubo
Canada: Stream on Fubo
United Kingdom: Watch on Sky Sports Main Event
What to watch for
Michael Carrick insists Manchester United’s current outlook “is not that bad” despite the Old Trafford outfit winning just one of their first three league fixtures to start the season. Defeat in Sunday’s derby would make it harder for the United manager to deny the growing malaise around the club.
The failure to land a single new non-midfielder in the summer transfer window left some supporters with the sense Manchester United could have done more to prepare for the season ahead. Nonetheless, Carrick possesses the attacking quality to win any game.
Maresca boasts the same. Erling Haaland already has five goals to his name this season. Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez are bedding in after blockbuster transfers. Rayan Cherki is growing in influence with almost every match he plays. Pep Guardiola might be gone, but Manchester City still have a fear factor.
Player to watch: Bruno Fernandes, Manchester United - If the hosts are to get the better of their rivals on Sunday, their best player will surely have to play a key role. Last season’s Premier League Player of the Season is a creative force of nature. Fernandes has the capacity to win the derby on his own.
summary: Manchester United and Manchester City are set to face off in the first Manchester Derby of the season at Old Trafford. United enters the match struggling defensively with their worst start since 1972, while City aims for a record seventh opening four-game win streak under new manager Enzo Maresca. The fixture kicks off at 4:30 PM BST (11:30 AM ET) and will be broadcast on Sky Sports in the UK and streamed on Fubo in the US and Canada.
key_points: Manchester United has conceded two goals in each of their first three league games, marking their worst defensive start since 1972.
A victory would mark Manchester City's opening four Premier League games won for a record seventh time.
The match takes place at Old Trafford and is broadcast on Sky Sports Main Event in the UK and Fubo in the US and Canada.
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick relies on attacking quality and star player Bruno Fernandes to challenge their rivals.

title: Solheim Cup 2026 live: Europe vs USA final-day singles updates and scoreboard
author: Kieran Crichard; James Corrigan
content:
![Lottie Woad is one of Europe's big guns](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/golf/2026/09/13/TELEMMGLPICT000502813909_17893015087190_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqrZiRCz5gHQhPSIGejW2hNeTnYFyWGbb4POwkTTwt1Os.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Lottie Woad is one of Europe's big guns](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/golf/2026/09/13/TELEMMGLPICT000502813909_17893015087190_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqrZiRCz5gHQhPSIGejW2hNeTnYFyWGbb4POwkTTwt1Os.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
- Europe and USA tied at 8-8 going into final day
- Europe need 14½ points to win Solheim Cup
- USA need 14 points to retain trophy
Coughlin in control
Maguire is under big pressure in match nine after seven holes as Coughlin rolls in a birdie putt to move three up.
Up on 15, Khnag has a chance to cut Hull’s lead to one with a birdie putt but it does not have enough pace on it. Hull is two up with three to play.
Back on the fifth, another hole goes the way of Ciganda, who is already four up over Kupcho.
Yet more European cheers as Madsen rolls in a putt on 10 to go one up over Corpuz. Europe now lead in eight matches!
So close
Grant has the chance on 12 to move four up with six holes to play. However, somehow the ball does not drop and instead hangs over the left edge. Yin rolls in her putt for the half and Grant remains three up.
Team USA were the favourites with the bookmarks this morning and the momentum they gained in Saturday night’s late drama no doubt was a factor. But so will have been the long-held belief that the Americans are better at singles. The recent stats do not tally, however. The last time the US won a Solheim singles session was 11 years ago. So maybe we should not be too surprised at the blue wave. Long way to go, however.
Clutch putt
Hull is under pressure after a poorly-played hole on 14. She still has a lengthy putt just to halve the hole but shows immense bottle and composure to roll it in to remain two up with four to play.
Behind on 13, Al. Lee is cutting into Henseleit’s lead. At one point just a few holes back, Henseleit led by four. Now, with five to play, her lead has been cut to two.
Current state of affairs
Megan Khang vs Charley Hull 2UP (13 holes)
Alison Lee vs Esther Henseleit 3UP (12 holes)
Angel Yin vs Linn Grant 3UP (11 holes)
3UP Nelly Korda vs Mimi Rhodes (10 holes)
Allisen Corpuz vs Nanna Koerstz Madsen Tied (9 holes)
Andrea Lee vs Nastasia Nadaud 1UP (8 holes)
Yealimi Noh vs Julia Lopez Ramirez Tied (7 holes)
Auston Kim vs Lottie Woad 2UP (6 holes)
2UP Lauren Coughlin vs Leona Maguire (6 holes)
Lindy Duncan vs Maja Stark 1UP (5 holes)
Jennifer Kupcho vs Carlota Ciganda 3UP (4 holes)
Rose Zhang vs Celine Boutier Tied (2 holes)
Back to three up
Yin had reduced to it two on the 10th but a bad tee shot on 11 is punished as Grant rolls in a birdie putt at par three to go back to three up. Grant did have two putts to win it but only needed one. Europe will nearly be halfway to victory if the top three matches stay as they are, although Hull could be in some strife at the 14th.
Ciganda dominating
You can now make it three up for the Spaniard, who is control of her match against Kupcho through four holes.
In the second match, Al. Lee is under pressure but she does get a hole back against Henseleit, who is three up through 12.
In match five, Corpuz wins the ninth hole to make it a tied match with Madsen.
Ciganda in control early
Match 11 pits two players who have had clutch moments at the end of both Friday and Saturday. Ciganda is taking on Kupcho, with the former now two up through three holes.
Up ahead at the tenth, maybe Yin is not out of this. Grant makes a bit of a mess of the hole and Yin reduces Grant’s lead to two. It is a few positive American moments in quick succession as Coughlin goes two up over Maguire at the fifth.
Korda dominating at the turn
Despite Rhodes’ best efforts chipping from off the green, world number one Korda takes the ninth and hits the turn at three up. Korda is one of just three Americans to actually be leading their match. There is currently a lot of blue on the board but we know how quickly things change. Remember how the momentum shifted on singles Sunday at the Ryder Cup last year and how nervous all the European fans would have been at one point.
More European momentum
Woad gets another hole on Kim and now is two up through five holes. Kim’s putt to halve the fifth hole somehow stayed up hanging over the right edge.
![Lottie Woad hits a shot during the Sunday singles](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/golf/2026/09/13/TELEMMGLPICT000502813900_17893005576960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqI0P8f9bO4E3qjnGDTmoejZgojZYlP8f0i9h2tPqCNsM.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
More home cheers
Currently, Team Europe are in a great position and big cheers ring around the Bernardus Golf Club. In game ten, Maja Stark goes one up over Lindy Duncan whilst in game 11, Carlota Ciganda has also gone one up over Jennifer Kupcho. Europe now lead in seven matches, although Noh has just taken a one up lead over Lopez Rmairez through five holes.
summary: Europe and USA entered the final-day singles of the Solheim Cup tied at 8-8, with Europe needing 14.5 points to win and the USA needing 14 to retain the trophy. Early updates from the singles matches at Bernardus Golf Club showed strong European momentum, with Europe leading in several matchups. key_points: Europe and USA were tied at 8-8 heading into the final day of the Solheim Cup.

title: ‘I want Teófimo’: Ryan Garcia calls out rivals after two-round destruction of Conor Benn
author: Bryan Armen Graham
content:
Ryan Garcia needed less than four minutes to blow away Conor Benn before turning his sights on the rest of the welterweight division.
The 28-year-old American demolished Benn inside two rounds on Saturday night to retain his World Boxing Council championship at 147lb, dropping the British challenger with a concussive right hand before the referee stepped in moments later at T-Mobile Arena. The sensational finish ignited the mostly pro-Garcia crowd of 18,855 on Mexican Independence Day weekend. Then, with Teófimo López taunting him from ringside and threatening to storm the ring, Garcia made it clear he was ready to take on all comers.
“We got to clear this [division] out,” said Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs), who was making the first defense of the welterweight title he won by flooring and outpointing Mario Barrios at the same arena in February.
Benn (25-2, 14 KOs), who had promised “tenacity, ferocity, spite” throughout an acrimonious build-up and vowed to pressure Garcia from the first bell, made good on that pledge. He set a frenetic pace in the opening frame, bolting from his corner and dragging Garcia into heavy exchanges. Benn scored well to the body and caught the champion with a shot to the back of the head that went unpunished, while Garcia repeatedly threw his signature left hook in an ominous statement of intent.
The decisive sequence came early in the second when Benn was attempting to close the distance. Garcia caught him flush on the chin with a right hand he never appeared to see coming, sending him crashing to the canvas in a heap. Benn made it back to his feet but was plainly hurt, prompting the champion to close in immediately and unload with both hands until third man Thomas Taylor intervened at the 1min 25sec mark.
![Ryan Garcia looks on after knocking down Conor Benn during their WBC welterweight title fight at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/c3bf8a96aa171108d701d675774dfc527961c22c/0_0_7437_4958/master/7437.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
“The first round I was just saying, ‘Just protect yourself. He’s going to get crazy. Just really worry about just watching what he’s doing, download, download, download,’” Garcia said. “Then I started hitting him. I was like, ‘Oh wow, I’m already timing him.’ And then the second round I said, ‘I’m just going to stand my ground a little bit. I’m going to get my respect real quick.’
“And then when I did, I ended up knocking him out.”
The defeat thwarted Benn’s bid to follow in the footsteps of his father, Nigel, who held the WBC super-middleweight title more than three decades ago. The 29-year-old from Essex had not fought at the welterweight limit in four and a half years after campaigning as high as middleweight and described the process of returning to 147lb as going through the “pits of hell”. He nevertheless came in at 146lb at Friday’s weigh-in, his lightest in seven years.
Garcia disputed any suggestion that the stoppage was premature. “They could have stopped it when he was on the ground,” he said. “He was out of it. I looked at him in the eyes and he wasn’t even there. If it would’ve kept going, you would’ve seen a man unconscious on the floor. It’s the ref’s job to stop the fight when it needs to be done, to protect the fighter.”
The fight was co-promoted by Zuffa Boxing, the fledgling venture of UFC supremo Dana White which poached Benn in April after his entire 10-year career with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom. Garcia remains under contract with Oscar De La Hoya’s Golden Boy, which spent months sparring with Zuffa over the matchup before the sides came to a deal.
![Ryan Garcia lands a punch on Conor Benn during their WBC welterweight title fight.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ca7a9818599fbbd5a6a1a8c98bacfdcc44c6df1d/0_0_5079_3544/master/5079.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Saturday’s spectacle also represented the latest step in the rehabilitation of two fighters whose careers had recently been threatened by doping controversies. Garcia tested positive for the banned anabolic agent ostarine around his April 2024 victory over Devin Haney. The result was overturned to a no-contest and Garcia was suspended for one year, with his team blaming contaminated supplements.
Benn’s ordeal was more complicated. Two positive tests for clomifene emerged before his proposed 2022 fight with Chris Eubank Jr, keeping him from fighting in Britain for two years. Benn maintained his innocence throughout and was ultimately cleared by the National Anti-Doping Panel.
Yet there they were on Saturday, reportedly earning around $15m apiece in one of the biggest fights of the year. Garcia leaves Las Vegas with his belt, his reputation burnished and no shortage of lucrative options.
Indeed, the televised post-fight interview quickly descended into the sort of chaos that has followed Garcia, one of boxing’s first Gen-Z superstars, throughout his tumultuous career in the spotlight. He spotted López at ringside and summoned the WBA titleholder toward the ring, shouting: “Unified time. Where you at, Teo?”
When López responded, Garcia escalated matters. “You want to get crazy, we going to get crazy,” he said. “I’ll beat your ass right now.”
![Teófimo López is restrained by security after Ryan Garcia’s victory over Conor Benn.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/44c2c4fe49a4d15a3579dc0ad2d83b13a06bc232/0_0_7598_5065/master/7598.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Then came a challenge to Haney, the WBO champion and another interested observer at ringside given the unfinished business surrounding their drug-tainted first encounter. “Hopefully we get to beat Devin Haney’s ass again for undisputed,” Garcia said. “Fuck the Haneys!”
Nor are those Garcia’s only options. Four-division world champion Shakur Stevenson, campaigning one division below at 140lb for now, was also in the arena on Saturday as a member of the Paramount+ commentary team and expressed interest in a fight with Garcia, who remains one of the sport’s most marketable American stars.
Later, Garcia made his immediate preference clear. “I want to unify against Teófimo,” he said. “I think that’s the move. It’s a huge fight and Teó’s an entertaining dude and it’s going to be a hell of a buildup and he’s a good fighter too, so let’s run it.”
Where Benn goes from here is less clear. He had already suggested this would be his final appearance at welterweight after describing the arduous weight cut to 147lb. Still not yet 30 and a proven attraction in Britain, he is unlikely to lack decent options at a more natural weight. He was transported to hospital after the fight for observation without speaking to reportersm, but struck a gracious note on social media. “Not my night, no excuses,” he wrote, calling Garcia “a great champion”.
summary: Ryan Garcia retained his WBC welterweight championship by defeating Conor Benn with a second-round knockout at the T-Mobile Arena. Benn pressed a frenetic pace in the opening round, but Garcia landed a decisive right hand in the second round to secure the stoppage. Following the victory, Garcia immediately called out potential future opponents including Teófimo López, Devin Haney, and Shakur Stevenson.
key_points: Ryan Garcia defeated Conor Benn in less than four minutes to retain his WBC 147lb title.
The stoppage occurred in the second round after Garcia dropped Benn with a right hand to the chin.
Both fighters entered the bout having recently overcome separate doping controversies.
Following his victory, Garcia called out ring-side rivals Teófimo López and Devin Haney for future unification fights.

title: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka to seal dramatic US Open title triumph
author: Tumaini Carayol
content:
Even when long established as a grand slam champion and a conqueror of all surfaces, Elena Rybakina was always considered lesser than the most successful players of her era. She was one of the most devastating shotmakers in the world, a threat to everybody everywhere, but there were always a couple of more consistent and mentally tougher players above her.
She leaves New York, finally, as the undisputed best tennis player on the planet, the new standard bearer of women’s tennis, after following up her snatching of the No 1 ranking from Aryna Sabalenka by succeeding her as the US Open champion. As she has done throughout this unforgettable week, the Kazakhstani showed her toughness in another spectacular tussle with her great rival, closing out her time at Flushing Meadows with a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory over Sabalenka, the top seed and two-time defending champion.
Before the final, Rybakina had not really played her best tennis this year in New York, but the whole title run stands as the greatest mental performance of her career. She has had to overcome an achilles injury that sidelined her for a week before the tournament and left her uncertain if she would even compete. There was also the potentially suffocating pressure of trying to clinch the world No 1 ranking while being reminded of the exact results required of her to do so. She faced four consecutive grand slam or Olympic champions in the second week of the tournament. She cleared every hurdle without hesitation.
Her trials throughout the past two weeks imbued her with the confidence to play such an assured match against her biggest rival to close out the week. Here, the 27-year-old began the match with her serve, the most important shot in her arsenal, completely misfiring, yet she still showed off the breadth of her game by completely dominating an increasingly dishevelled Sabalenka off the ground. When the Belarusian fought her way back into the match, overturning the momentum and forcing a final set, Rybakina immediately reset, saving her best tennis for the most important stretch.
![Elena Rybakina follows through on a backhand](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/f53d786b9ef12fa67896f73732799db66bd3afc0/0_0_5000_3282/master/5000.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
In addition to taking Sabalenka’s No 1 ranking, Rybakina has now also taken her status as the best hard-court player in the world. She now holds the three biggest hard-court titles: the Australian Open, the US Open and the WTA Finals. She joins figures such as Lindsay Davenport, Jennifer Capriati, Ash Barty, Angelique Kerber and Virginia Wade as three-time grand slam champions. Having previously won Wimbledon in 2022 and the 2026 Australian Open, Rybakina is suddenly a French Open away from completing the career grand slam.
This was a historic encounter, just the second time in the 38-year history of the Australian Open and US Open both being played on hard courts that the same two rivals had competed in both finals, and a rare tussle between the top two players in the world with the ranking certain to switch hands. No matter the terrain or stakes, these two players just seem to force the highest level of tennis from each other. This was the third time they had faced each other in a major final and those meetings have yielded three supreme battles.
As always, they started at a frenetic pace, but it quickly became clear that the cleanliness of Rybakina’s shotmaking was on another level. What ensued was a quite remarkable spectacle. Rybakina, owner of by far the best first serve in the world, started a grand slam final with her biggest strength in total disarray. She landed a shocking 27% of first serves in the set, eight of her 30 attempted first serves landing in. No matter, every other part of her game was flowing perfectly. She used her destructive return to place relentless pressure on Sabalenka’s serve, she dominated the baseline exchanges and her backhand was completely flawless. She gave her opponent no room to breathe.
Considering how difficult things had been for Sabalenka all summer, she had performed incredibly well to reach the final and give herself a shot at a third consecutive US Open title but she was clearly unsettled by the occasion and her opponent’s level from the beginning. After double-faulting to give up the decisive break at 2-3 in the first set, she received a code violation warning after striking a ball into the crowd. She was visibly frustrated and tense throughout the match, particularly considering how badly she failed to take advantage of facing so many second serves.
![Aryna Sabalenka looks dejected as Elena Rybakina is interviewed](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/99b173a9535fe12c321ff21c4f605f3bd6fd167a/0_0_5986_3960/master/5986.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Still, Sabalenka fought hard. A strong run of serving in the second set allowed her to gain rhythm and although Rybakina’s first serve improved, she became slightly more erratic from the baseline. At 5-4, with the pressure beginning to weigh heavily on Rybakina’s shoulders, Sabalenka made her move, pounding a down-the-line backhand return winner to earn her first break points of the match at double set point. Sabalenka was too tense to take advantage of the two second serves that followed, but she was putting the Rybakina second serve under sustained pressure. At 6-5, after muscling her way to a third set point, Sabalenka pounded a backhand return winner to force a decider.
Even in the face of a roaring, charging, two-time US Open champion, Rybakina was totally unfazed. She reset immediately and her serve was finally at its precise, destructive best. Rybakina flitted through her early service games in set three, firing down aces and forcing her opponent to keep up. Sabalenka, like so many players over the past year, simply could not.
summary: Elena Rybakina claimed her first US Open title and the world No 1 ranking by defeating Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 in the final. Despite battling an achilles injury prior to the tournament and an initial misfiring serve, Rybakina displayed remarkable mental toughness to overcome the top seed. With this victory, Rybakina now holds three grand slam titles, including the Australian Open, US Open, and Wimbledon.
key_points: Elena Rybakina defeated Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 to win the US Open and secure the world No 1 ranking.
Rybakina overcame a pre-tournament achilles injury and the pressure of facing four consecutive grand slam or Olympic champions in the second week.
Despite landing only 27% of her first serves in the first set, Rybakina dominated baseline exchanges and neutralised Sabalenka.
Sabalenka fought back to win the second set, but Rybakina reset in the third set to close out the match decisively.
The victory marks Rybakina's third grand slam title, joining wins at Wimbledon and the Australian Open.

title: US Open 2026 results: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka to win New York title
author: Jonathan Jurejko
content:
![Elena Rybakina lifts the US Open trophy with Aryna Sabalenka looking on](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/3840/cpsprodpb/1640/live/9be39be0-aefd-11f1-812c-df2830a6d395.jpg)
Elena Rybakina has now won the Australian Open, Wimbledon and the US Open
- Published
Elena Rybakina demonstrated why she is the best women's player in the world by beating two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka to win her first US Open title.
Kazakhstan's Rybakina already knew she would be the new world number one after Saturday's final regardless of the result, and she celebrated with a 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over the player she will replace.
Rybakina was the more composed of the two throughout as she claimed the third Grand Slam title of her career, having triumphed at Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier this year.
Sabalenka hoped to soften the blow of losing the top ranking by winning a third consecutive US Open title - but looked fraught in a tense performance.
Rybakina and Sabalenka have developed a strong rivalry built not only on their outstanding talent but their contrasting personalities.
And Rybakina's ice-cool composure - the direct opposite of the Belarusian's combustible nature - was a key difference as she took control at Flushing Meadows.
Rybakina stayed calm in an opening set where her first serve let her down and, despite her biggest weapon not firing on all cylinders, was able to execute a devastating returning game which left Sabalenka frustrated.
Sabalenka's groundstrokes improved as Rybakina's level dropped slightly in a tighter second set, taking her third opportunity to force a decider when she swarmed over Rybakina's second serve in the 12th game.
But the loose shots from Sabalenka reappeared in the third set - as did the negativity.
Rybakina's deep returning pinned Sabalenka to the baseline as she broke for a 2-1 lead, which allowed the incoming world number one to grow in stature.
There was a sign of nerves when Rybakina produced a double fault on her first championship point, but she reset admirably to hammer down an ace and underline her status as the best player in the world.
Rybakina claims New York win few predicted
![Elena Rybakina celebrates](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1376/cpsprodpb/e69d/live/2d8cdf60-aefa-11f1-a52c-d92eb1a832de.jpg)
Elena Rybakina had never gone past the US Open fourth round until this year
Rybakina rarely shows emotion on the court but there was a brief flash of a smile as she clinched her second major victory of an outstanding 2026 season.
That illustrated the sense of satisfaction she felt after winning a title few had predicted - not because of her game but her history in New York.
With her penetrating serve and thunderous groundstrokes, Rybakina has a brand of first-strike tennis that can take the racquet out of anyone's hands.
Therefore it has been a surprise she has not enjoyed greater success on the Flushing Meadows hard courts, perhaps a result of her personality not being particularly suited to the brash nature of New York.
"I was coming here for the last 10 years and it was never successful. I'm falling in love with New York more and more," Rybakina, 27, said.
What makes the second seed's victory even more remarkable is that she was unsure if she would be fit enough to even play.
Rybakina was unable to walk for several days after injuring her ankle in the Cincinnati Open quarter-finals, putting her chances of competing here in serious jeopardy.
Not only was Rybakina able to play, but she cruised through her opening four matches thanks to a huge service game that rarely allowed opponents to get into points.
Rybakina's next two wins over China's Zheng Qinwen and home favourite Coco Gauff required more work after losing the first sets, proving she had the durability to come through tough battles.
Against Sabalenka, she showed both facets of her game, bullying her from the baseline and digging in when she had to to leave her a French Open title away from the career Grand Slam.
"Some magic is happening. I was unlucky with injury and just going day by day," Rybakina told Sky Sports.
"We didn't know how it was going to be so I'm super happy and still can't believe it."
summary: Elena Rybakina defeated two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 to win her first US Open title and the third Grand Slam of her career. The victory also confirmed Rybakina as the new world number one, regardless of the match's outcome. Her triumph in New York is even more remarkable as she was unsure if she could compete after suffering a severe ankle injury at the Cincinnati Open.
key_points: Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 5-7 6-2 to claim her first US Open title.
The victory marks the third Grand Slam title of Rybakina's career, following her wins at Wimbledon in 2022 and the Australian Open earlier in the year.
Rybakina entered the final knowing she would replace Sabalenka as the new world number one.
Her participation in the tournament was initially in doubt after she was unable to walk for several days due to an ankle injury sustained at the Cincinnati Open.

title: Sunderland v Arsenal: How the players rated
author: Alex Brotherton
content:
![Bruno](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/ea7b/live/c539ab60-aee9-11f1-a99d-4515748c32d0.jpg)
Bruno Guimaraes scored his first goal for Arsenal
- Published
Bruno Guimaraes' thunderbolt - 121 seconds after David Raya saved a penalty - helped a sub-par Arsenal maintain their 100% start to their Premier League title defence with a 2-0 win against Sunderland.
Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.
Sunderland
Robin Roefs: Poor distribution - two goal-kicks went straight out of play. Hardly troubled in the first half but made a fine save to tip over Kai Havertz's acrobatic effort. 6
Thomas Meunier: Offered a threat on second balls from set pieces but couldn't covert a couple of half chances. Tracked back to help defensively. 6
Nordi Mukiele: Kept Christos Tzolis quiet and provided a good outlet on break, but didn't pick out the right passes. Weak shot when right in front of goal at 1-0 down. Forced Raya into saves with two late chances but should have scored the second. 6
Kevin Danso: An unspectacular but assured home debut. 6
Dan Ballard: Defensively solid as ever and coped well with Arsenal's press. Should have scored from Xhaka free-kick, but won a penalty. 7
Reinildo Mandava: Largely contained Bukayo Saka, though was baited into fouling him and getting booked. Conceded late penalty and sent off. 4
Nilson Angulo: Lively on the wing and diligent in tracking back, but he should have run at Ben White and Ezri Konsa more. 6
Noah Sadiki: Showed willingness to get forward but also track back, but final ball lacked quality. 6
Granit Xhaka: Produced quality set-piece deliveries and busy as ever in midfield. Made a goal-saving clearance with the last kick of the first half. 7
Enzo Le Fee: Alert and always eager to drive attacks, but telegraphed his soft penalty. 6
Brian Brobbey: Made the lives of Konsa and White miserable all evening with his strength and hold-up play. Created space for others but didn't get any shots away, though that wasn't his brief tonight. 7
Subs:
Wilson Isidor (on 70, Angulo): 6
Malick Fofana (on 75, Meunier): 6
Subs not used: Dayann Methalie, Chemsdine Talbi, Chris Rigg, Luke O'Nien, Omar Alderete, Melker Ellborg, Trai Hulme.
Arsenal
David Raya: Little to do until he made a superb penalty save with Arsenal struggling. 8
Ben White: Got into some promising positions with overlapping runs, but looked lightweight when defending. Replaced at the break. 5
Gabriel Magalhaes: Strong in tackles and decent on the ball, but not without his usual theatrics - went down injured then complained when told to leave the field as per the rules. 6
Ezri Konsa: Struggled to deal with Brobbey and looked unconvincing on the ball when pressed. Conceded penalty for hauling down Ballard. 4
Ricardo Calafiori: Solid as usual but didn't provide his usual offensive threat. 6
Myles Lewis-Skelly: Lucky to escape an early booking, sloppy on the ball and withdrawn at half-time. 4
Declan Rice: Hard-working as ever both with and without the ball. Created a great chance for Saka at 0-0, but otherwise a bit sloppy. Recognised opportunity to tee up Guimaraes. 6
Bukayo Saka: Should have opened the scoring but failed to make proper contact. Kept largely quiet and missed one-on-one chance late on. Won late penalty and scored - just. 6
Martin Odegaard: Unable to continue his blistering start to the season. Good free-kick delivery. 6
Christos Tzolis: Looked lively early on but faded. 5
Kai Havertz: Missed a clear chance at 0-0 but almost scored a brilliant effort minutes later. Tried to square when he had the chance to put the game to bed. 6
Subs:
Jurrien Timber (on 45, White): Did a better job up against Angulo and Brobbey and proactive in winning the ball back. Headed in but caught offside. 6
Bruno Guimaraes (on 45, Lewis-Skelly): Brilliant strike moments after Raya's penalty save at a time Arsenal needed help. Not a bad way to score your first goal. 7
Martin Zubimendi (on 81, Rice) 6
Eberechi Eze (on 81, Tzolis) 6
Mikel Merino (on 85, Odegaard) 6
Subs not used: Kepa Arrizabalaga, Piero Hincapie, Viktor Gyokeres, Noni Madueke.
How did you rate the players?
Player of the match
After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.
summary: Arsenal maintained their 100% start to their Premier League title defence with a hard-fought 2-0 win against Sunderland. David Raya made a crucial penalty save before Bruno Guimaraes scored a thunderbolt for his first goal for the club. Bukayo Saka added a late penalty after Sunderland's Reinildo Mandava was sent off for conceding the spot-kick.
key_points: Bruno Guimaraes scored his first goal for Arsenal with a brilliant strike 121 seconds after David Raya saved a penalty.
Bukayo Saka scored a late penalty to seal the 2-0 victory for Arsenal.
Sunderland's Reinildo Mandava was sent off late in the match after conceding a penalty.
Arsenal maintained their 100% start to their Premier League title defence with the win.

title: Spurs 0-0 Everton: How the players rated
author: Phil McNulty
content:
![Everton's Vitalii Mykolenko in a race for possession with Spurs forward Omar Marmoush in the Premier League game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/803/cpsprodpb/5746/live/f2f8be80-aece-11f1-89e2-171455bb2760.jpg)
Everton's Vitalli Mykolenko in a race for possession with Spurs forward Omar Marmoush.
- Published
Tottenham Hotspur are still searching for their first goal - and first win - of the Premier League season after being held to a goalless draw at home by Everton.
Here's how I rated the players and you can see how you scored them below.
Tottenham Hotspur
Antonin Kinsky: Good save from James Garner free-kick but lucky to get away with passing straight to Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, which he redeemed with a save, 6
Archie Gray: Good runs forward from defence to add attacking threat. 7
Jan Paul van Hecke: Early chance at the far post where he could have done better. Composed in defence. 6
Micky van de Ven: Untroubled as Everton lacked attacking clout. 6
Andrew Robertson: Kept Brennan Johnson under wraps and made some trademark surging runs to lend support going forward. 7
Rodrigo Bentancur: Knitted things together well in midfield. Calm on the ball. 6
Sandro Tonali: Showed the odd touch of class but yet to look like a Â£100m midfielder. 6
Savio: Some lively moments on the right flank hinted at the promise of good things to come. Faded as the game went on. 7
Mateus Fernandes: Needs to do more. One shot was greeted with ironic applause - not for him but Spurs having a shot. 5
Omar Marmoush: No shortage of effort but no real impact. 5
Dominic Solanke: First Premier League start of the season and looked rusty and lacking in match sharpness. 4
Subs:
Mohammed Kudus (on 63, Fernandes): Struggled to get into the game. 4
Lucas Bergvall (on 63, Bentancur): Tried to give Spurs attacking thrust. One dangerous cross and almost won it with a late shot. 6
Mathys Tel (on 63, Solanke): Couple of tricky runs. 5
James Maddison (on 77, Marmoush): Little time to make an impact
Tosin Adarabioyo (on 85, Gray): Late entrance
Subs not used: Dubravka, Davies, Gallagher, Senesi.
Everton
Jordan Pickford: Good late save to keep out Bergvall effort. 7
Ainsley Maitland-Niles: Tried a repeat of his blockbuster equaliser against Manchester United. Lightning did not strike twice. 6
Jarrad Branthwaite: Superb early block and very solid. The game's outstanding player. His fitness will be crucial to Everton this season. 8
James Tarkowski: No-nonsense contribution alongside Branthwaite. Effective. 6
Vitalii Mykolenko: Had some tough early moments against Savio but stuck to his task. Wasted the occasional good crossing position. 5
Harrison Armstrong: One of the gifted teenager's quieter days but worked very hard. 6
James Garner: Unsung but had little chance to show his creative side as he tried to build a midfield platform for Everton. 5
Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall: Some lovely touches but was unable to create as Everton looked short of attacking threat and missed one of their best chances. 6
Brennan Johnson: Very poor against his former club. Last touch was missing a huge opportunity. Has looked better as an impact substitute than a starter so far this season. 4
Thierno Barry: Thankless task for the raw striker ploughing a lone furrow up front. 5
Tyrique George: Occasional flashes of pace and trickery but lacked influence. 5
Subs:
Jack Grealish (on 65, George): Couple of typical runs but unable to exert influence.
Jake O'Brien (on 75, Maitland-Niles): Helped keep Spurs out at the end.
Hayden Hackney (on 75, Johnson): Tried to inject some creativity.
Subs not used: Travers, King, Graham, Dibling, Alcaraz, Keane.
How did you rate the players?
Player of the match
After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.
summary: Tottenham Hotspur played to a goalless draw against Everton at home, leaving them still searching for their first goal and win of the Premier League season. Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite was named the game's outstanding player after a solid performance and superb early block. Both teams lacked sufficient attacking threat, resulting in a scoreless stalemate.
key_points: Tottenham remain without a goal or a win in the Premier League after a 0-0 draw with Everton.
Jarrad Branthwaite was the game's standout player, putting in a very solid performance for Everton.
Lucas Bergvall came closest for Tottenham with a late shot that was saved by Jordan Pickford.
Both sides struggled to create clear attacking opportunities throughout the match.

title: Spurs v Everton team news: Porro + Udogie out, Grealish still a sub
author: Skonto Rigga
content:
The penultimate Premier League fixture of the day sees Tottenham Hotspur entertain Everton.
Kick-off in north London is at 17:30 BST.

title: Chelsea vs Hull LIVE: Latest score and updates from Premier League
author: Tashan Deniran-Alleyne; Arthur Ferridge
content:

Chelsea are back in Premier League action today at Stamford Bridge. The Blues face a newly promoted team for the first time this season and are out to show last weekend's defeat to champions Arsenal was just a minor blip, though Hull are yet to concede in the league so far.
Xabi Alonso's side should be in good spirits after coming from behind to beat Leeds in midweek, scoring six goals in the second half to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round and make it three wins from three at home across all competitions. Chelsea have been handed a an injury blow with Moises Caicedo still sidelined, but Romeo Lavia is available for selection after being rested on Wednesday night.
Hull, meanwhile, have made a strong start upon returning to the top flight, picking up seven points from a possible nine. Another clean sheet for the Tigers may go a long way towards securing their most important objective of the campaign - avoiding relegation. Follow Chelsea vs Hull LIVE below with Standard Sport's dedicated match blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from Arthur Ferridge.
Live updates
Arthur Ferridge at Stamford Bridge
A needless moment of aggro from Colwill there as he just steps into the path of Tzolakis after a corner.
The Hull 'keeper goes down and requires treatment. Colwill gets away scot-free.
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
26 min: Hato glances a corner on at the near post but Tzolakis is alert and makes the save at the second attempt after spilling the ball in front of Joao Pedro.
The Hull keeper attempts to get his side going on the counter but is blocked off by Colwill and now requires treatment.
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
24 min: Palmer looks to slide in Rogers but Mendy blocks off the Chelsea goalscorer and Tzolakis rushes off his line to smother the ball.
Arthur Ferridge at Stamford Bridge
That's twice Chelsea have tried that cheeky corner routine, with Reece James playing it low along the floor to Palmer at the front post.
This time he flicks it on into the corridor of uncertainty, but there is nobody there to finish it.
Third time lucky, maybe?
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
22 min: CHANCE!
Better from Tzolakis as he parries Neto’s shot behind for a corner. On second thoughts, the Hull keeper could have caught the ball.
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
19 min: Belloumi tries to fizz a pass into McBurnie but misses the ball completely and the Hull attack comes to a halt.
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
17 min: First yellow card of the game is shown to McBurnie as he slides in on Palmer from behind. Hull striker has a long time to watch his step now.
Pedro Neto chips the free-kick in towards Joao Pedro but gets too much power on his cross and the ball goes out of play.
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
16 min: Hull are yet to get going from an attacking perspective. After conceding for the first time in the Premier League this season, they now need to avoid two goalless games if they’re to maintain their unbeaten start.
Chelsea 1-0 Hull
12 min: Egan with a crucial stretch to get to the ball before Joao Pedro as Gusto looked to present the Chelsea striker with a simple tap-in. Blues do have a corner which comes to nothing.

A very fluid setup from Chelsea, this, but I believe it is a back four with Hato and Gusto as full-backs, and Pedro Neto trading in his usual wing-back role to play as an out-and-out winger.
