title: Arsenal: Martin Odegaard new role explained by Mikel Arteta after captain's Champions League winner at Napoli
author: Peter Smith; Nick Wright
content:
Arsenal: Martin Odegaard new role explained by Mikel Arteta after captain's Champions League winner at Napoli
Martin Odegaard scored his fourth goal in five games this season with the winner in Arsenal's 1-0 Champions League victory at Napoli on Wednesday; Gunners captain only scored once in 2025/26 but higher position and fitness have facilitated fast start to the new campaign
Thursday 10 September 2026 07:18, UK
Martin Odegaard is a player transformed at the start of this season - and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta puts his captain's impressive form down to fitness and new positioning.
Odegaard was the match-winner again for Arsenal on Wednesday, thumping in the only goal of the game in the Champions League victory at Napoli.
That hit followed his clinching strike against Chelsea in the Premier League on Sunday and takes his total to four goals in five appearances this season across all competitions.
Odegaard only scored once for Arsenal during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign but now his stats are up across a range of other attacking metrics, too.
- Napoli 0-1 Arsenal - Match report and analysis
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Champions League scores
- Latest news and rumours: Arsenal
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
"First of all he needs to be available and last year he missed so many games through injuries," said Arteta when asked in his post-match press conference about Odegaard's improvement.
"The quality's always been there. It's never been a question," added Declan Rice, speaking to Sky Sports. "Last year, to have two shoulder injuries like he did, then a MCL injury he did, it's never easy.
"But then you see him at the World Cup and how he's started this year. That's the Martin we know and we love, he's our captain. We need to keep giving him the ball and letting things happen."
Arteta also highlighted how fresh combinations with team-mates are playing a part.
"He's got that edge and different relationships around him as well and that helps," said the Gunners boss.
"He can start to go by different heights in the team, especially in the attacking phase, and when we get him into those positions he's a really dangerous player."
That is demonstrated by Odegaard's touches in the opposition box going up from 2.5 per 90 minutes last season to 4.3 per 90 minutes so far this term.
Arteta put Odegaard's freedom to advance into more threatening positions down to the skills of his team-mates in open play, which the Arsenal head coach suggested had been missing previously.
"We have a lot of players that can take the ball there and progress the ball much better than we did in the past," Arteta explained.
"When that happens, [Odegaard] needs to take different heights and angles and positions in order to disorganise the opponent and he's done that really well."
Christos Tzolis is likely to be one of those players Arteta is referencing. The summer signing has four assists to his name already, with three of those coming for Odegaard goals, including the winner in Naples.
But the Arsenal attack down both flanks and through the middle looked extremely dangerous at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.
Arsenal had 26 shots in total - their most on record (since 2003/04) in the competition. An expected goals total of 4.05 showed they should have got far more for their efforts.
Odegaard, though, did step up and deliver the key moment.
"That's what we need," said Arteta. "The players with the mindset to decide a game and play with personality. To keep taking chances and risks.
"He's getting into those positions much more in recent games and now you feel he has the emotional state that he knows the ball can go in, and he scored an incredible goal tonight."
Odegaard playing with freedom and flair
Analysis by Sky Sports' Nick Wright:
Odegaard is a player in form. That much was clear from early in the game against Napoli. He oozed class and confidence, demanding the ball then finding the gaps in Napoli's defence and threading passes forward. Everything went through him.
His goal, brilliantly taken from the edge of the box after a 29-pass build-up, proved crucial. He now has four in five games this season, a stunning turnaround having only managed one in 36 last term. Odegaard, uninhibited by injuries, looks a different player.
Showing his team-mates how to finish was only one part of his performance. He also ended the game having had more touches, made more passes and created more chances than anyone else on the pitch. Napoli couldn't really get near him.
The scooped pass to release Ben White for the golden chance somehow spurned by Piero Hincapie was one of many examples of his ingenuity against the massed ranks of Napoli players but there were plenty of others. He played with freedom and flair.
"Martin is contributing goals," added Arteta after the game. "That is obviously impacting results which is what we want from our attacking players, to be decisive, and certainly he was that today."
Arsenal continue to feel the benefits.
summary: Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard scored the winning goal in a 1-0 Champions League victory against Napoli, bringing his total to four goals in five appearances this season. Manager Mikel Arteta attributes Odegaard's impressive early-season form to improved fitness following an injury-plagued previous campaign, alongside a new higher attacking position. Teammate Declan Rice and fresh squad combinations have also helped facilitate the midfielder's fast start.
key_points: Martin Odegaard scored the winner in Arsenal's 1-0 Champions League victory against Napoli.
Odegaard has recorded four goals in five appearances this season after scoring only once during an injury-hit 2025/26 campaign.
Mikel Arteta explained that improved fitness and a higher attacking position have driven Odegaard's strong form.
Odegaard's touches in the opposition box have increased from 2.5 per 90 minutes last season to 4.3 per 90 minutes this term.
Summer signing Christos Tzolis has contributed significantly by providing three assists for Odegaard goals.

title: Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister scores stunning winner as Bradley Barcola has eventful full debut
author: Adam Bate
content:
Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid: Alexis Mac Allister scores stunning winner as Bradley Barcola has eventful full debut
Report as Andoni Iraola’s Champions League career as a coach begins with a 2-1 Liverpool win over Atletico Madrid thanks to Alexis Mac Allister's strike; Dominik Szoboszlai levelled Marcos Llorente’s goal; Bradley Barcola off with "cramp" on full debut
Wednesday 9 September 2026 22:49, UK
Alexis Mac Allister's superb strike saw Liverpool come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 at Anfield as Bradley Barcola went off with "cramp" on an eventful home debut.
Barcola was making his first start for Liverpool but felt his calf in the second half and the £123m signing was substituted having missed three good chances to mark the occasion with a goal. It did not impact the result thanks to Mac Allister's rocket.
Marcos Llorente had opened the scoring for the Spanish side with his fifth goal against Liverpool when put through well by Julian Alvarez on the Argentine forward's return to the starting line-up. But that man Dominik Szoboszlai levelled it up before the break.
- As it happened | Teams | Stats | Champions League scores
- Latest news and rumours: Liverpool
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Curiously, both Liverpool goals came in the immediate aftermath of Barcola chances. Jan Oblak saved to deny him in the build-up to Szoboszlai's goal, Ronald Araujo cleverly recycling the chance. And Mac Allister blasted in to spare his blushes for the second.
Liverpool had drawn their first two Premier League games of the season two apiece, and given the open nature of the game there was a risk of a repeat. But instead Andoni Iraola earned this Anfield victory in his first Champions League match as a head coach.
The key moments from Anfield
1 - CHANCE! Szoboszlai robs Koke but Isak drags his shot wide
15 - SAVE! Barcola chance in behind on the right but Oblak saves
17 - GOAL! Alvarez sends Llorente through and he beats Alisson
27 - SAVE! Alvarez shot from distance tipped just wide by Alisson
30 - SAVE! Wirtz denied by Oblak after starting the move himself
40 - GOAL! Araujo's clever flick puts Szoboszlai in to slot home
49 - WIDE! Wirtz sends Barcola clean through but he shoots wide
50 - GOAL! Mac Allister blasts in left-footed just second later
58 - INJURY! Barcola substituted after going down holding his calf
88 - OFFSIDE! Frimpong sweeps the ball home but is well offside
Iraola: Just cramp for Barcola
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola speaking about Bradley Barcola in the press conference:
"No, it's cramp. It's just cramp, there is no injury. With Bradley, it's about building his physical condition.
"We don't really know, or we didn't know until now probably, how much he can play, because he hasn't had any minutes in pre-season for PSG.
"He played 30 the other day. Today we had some question marks, how many minutes he can give us, and probably now we know.
"And I'm very happy because also he has had two very clear chances against the keeper. He hasn't scored, but I want him there. That is where he has to make the difference - arriving to those spots, those positions.
"And I'm very happy because in, I don't know how many minutes he's played, two times against the keeper is a good sign with Bradley."
Analysis: Barcola's Anfield debut
Sky Sports' Adam Bate at Anfield:
Barcola might have scored twice in the first half on his Anfield bow and missed a big chance at the start of the second but it was still a promising performance. He has been used on the left by Paris Saint-Germain but showed his versatility playing from the right.
His fitness looked sharper than his finishing and it did not take long for him to win over the Kop, his name being chanted inside 15 minutes when he tracked back to shut down an early Atletico counter-attack. That pace looks like it will be a real weapon for Iraola.
The worry was the sight of him trudging off before the hour. The Liverpool boss had stressed the need to manage Barcola given that he had not been involved in pre-season. Iraola needs him up to speed quickly. On this evidence, he can make a difference.
summary: Liverpool secured a 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid in the Champions League thanks to a stunning winning strike from Alexis Mac Allister. Marcos Llorente initially opened the scoring for Atletico before Dominik Szoboszlai equalized before halftime. Bradley Barcola experienced an eventful full debut for Liverpool, missing several scoring chances before being substituted with cramp in the second half.
key_points: Alexis Mac Allister scored the winning goal with a powerful left-footed strike.
Marcos Llorente opened the scoring for Atletico Madrid, assisted by Julian Alvarez.
Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool's first-half equalizer.
Bradley Barcola made his full debut for Liverpool, missed three scoring chances, and was substituted in the second half with cramp.
The win marked Andoni Iraola's first Champions League victory as a head coach.

title: Ødegaard ‘edge’ delights Arteta as Arsenal secure narrow win at Napoli
author: Ed Aarons
content:
After their record-breaking feats last year in the Champions League, Arsenal are at it again. But having been delayed along with hundreds of travelling supporters by travel chaos on Tuesday, Mikel Arteta’s side had to bide their time against Napoli until Martin Ødegaard continued his rich vein of goalscoring with the crucial strike 15 minutes from full time.
Perhaps it was the fact that, at Uefa’s insistence, they were forced to wear red shorts for the first time since a Premier League game against Watford in 2022 that Arsenal were not quite at their flowing best here and missed a hatful of chances.
Yet they were deserved winners in the end and the substitute Noni Madueke should have made the victory more comprehensive late on.
Having come so close to breaking their duck in this competition last year after becoming the first team to win all eight of their league stage matches, Arsenal look capable of going one better this time if Ødegaard can keep up this sparkling form.
He now has four goals in his last five games after scoring once in all competitions last year and it was the Norway captain whose name was being chanted by the fans who were kept behind more than an hour after the final whistle.
“That’s what we need – players with that mindset to decide the game and to play with that personality,” said Arteta. “He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games and I feel he has this emotional state that he knows that the ball can go in. He’s got that edge and he’s now got different relationships around him [in the team] as well. That helps.”
Arteta has bad memories of this stadium after being sent off in a 2-0 defeat during the Champions League group stage in 2013. But Arsenal’s most recent match here ended in victory as they qualified for the Europa League semi-finals under Unai Emery in 2019. Both clubs have been crowned domestic champions since then, with Napoli ending their 33-year wait in 2023 then doing it again two years later. Yet Champions League success has continued to elude them after finishing 30th in the league phase last season.
![Mikel Arteta talks with Kevin De Bruyne, the former Manchester City midfielder, after the match](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/480663030665d41e966918f0a7ed9ff1bbb63fc1/0_0_2300_1495/master/2300.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
That was in stark contrast to Arsenal, who were unbeaten over 14 matches before falling at the final hurdle. It was telling that Arteta kept faith with four of his back five that started against Chelsea on Sunday, with Piero Hincapié replacing Riccardo Calafiori at left-back but failing to match the Italian’s finishing ability with one glaring miss. Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyökeres also made their first starts of the season but largely disappointed, with the Sweden striker making way for Kai Havertz just before Ødegaard’s winner.
Those Arsenal supporters that did make it to southern Italy had no problem making themselves heard throughout, with plenty of empty seats in the home sections despite Max Allegri’s attempts to rally Napoli’s fans beforehand. The game quickly settled into a pattern as the visitors set up camp in Napoli’s half and the hosts attempted to hit them on the break. Kevin De Bruyne – no stranger to facing Arsenal after a decade in the sky blue of Manchester City – forced David Raya into a rare mistake after a typically driving run through the midfield but the ball was scrambled away to safety.
That came just after a spectacular overhead kick from Bukayo Saka at the other end had been saved by Alex Meret. Merino should have scored when he was set up by Eze’s clever header across the face of goal before Ben White drilled a shot straight into Meret’s grateful gloves.
after newsletter promotion
Matteo Politano managed to test Raya again as Napoli continued to find gaps in Arsenal’s normally watertight defence. Saka blazed over after a brilliant through ball from Ødegaard on the stroke of half-time, with replays confirming the assistant had been wrong to raise his flag.
![Martin Ødegaard scores the only goal of the match at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/708e7b03bd110881956f0dd4f0118917465a5fa0/919_128_3110_2488/master/3110.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Meret did not return for the second half and was replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, once on Manchester United’s books. The Serbia goalkeeper was a mere spectator for a flowing Arsenal move featuring a sumptuous scooped pass into the area that ended with Hincapié missing the target after being picked out at the far post by Ben White’s header. Suddenly Napoli found themselves suffocated by a blanket of red. Allegri, who knows what it feels like to have lost in a Champions League final after suffering that fate twice in three years at Juventus, responded by switching to a back five and trying to hang on.
Arsenal’s pressure eventually told when another substitute, Christos Tzolis, exchanged passes with White and teed up Ødegaard, whose shot flew in off the post despite Milinkovic-Savic just getting his fingertips to the ball. Havertz had a goal disallowed for offside in injury time, but the mission was already complete.
summary: Arsenal secured a narrow victory away at Napoli after overcoming pre-match travel chaos. Despite missing numerous chances, Martin Ødegaard scored the crucial winning goal 15 minutes before full time. The victory continues Arsenal's strong form in the Champions League under manager Mikel Arteta.
key_points: Martin Ødegaard scored the only goal of the match 15 minutes from time.
Arsenal missed several scoring chances before breaking the deadlock.
Manager Mikel Arteta praised Ødegaard's decisive mindset and recent goalscoring form.
The victory keeps Arsenal on a strong trajectory in the Champions League.

title: Chelsea 6-3 Leeds; Liverpool 2-1 Atlético Madrid, PSG 6-1 Slovan Bratislava – live
author: Daniel Harris
content:
Iraola is chatting to TNT, saying he loved the occasion and that he takes some responsibility for the first-half performance, having not predicted Atleti’s 3-5-2; he corrected halfway through the first half.
He’s happy he side showed character, but they’ve difficult homes and nasty aways, so there’s a lot to do. Barcola, he advises, had cramp, an absolute result, and he goes on to say this is a new team without the mechanisms in which every player knows what to do in every situation.
On Araujo, Iraola says he has good crossing ability, is good in the air and smart with his decision-making. Players like Frimpong and Tsimikas have’t played much, so are probably disappointed, but they contributed tonight.
Neto screeches down the right and cuts back to the edge, where Barco shanks horribly, only for Welbeck, always alert, to redirect into the net via header. What a ridiculous half (of football) this has been.
Danny Welbeck (right) heads home for his second, and Chelsea’s sixth, goal of the game. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA
Which he’s pretty happy about. Photograph: Isabel Infantes/Reuters
“Iraolaball has started rolling, slowly but steadily,” reckons Rupak Pramanik. “This Liverpool looked a lot like the Liverpool opponents feared during the Klopp era.”
Generous, I’d say – they were very vulnerable in the first half and the players just aren’t as good as those Klopp had, nor have they the physicality to play at the same tempo. But they played some decent stuff in parts.
Six additional minutes at Stamford Bridge,enough time for Chelsea to score and concede at least another couple. If they can get the defence and midfield right, in January and in the summer, they could be very nasty next season.
Atleti played well in the first half but Liverpool hung in there and were much the better side in the second. That’s a really important win for Andoni Iraoloa, his debut Champions League game and a difficult opponent sorted in uplifting manner.
Rogers has been filth since coming on and this, his third assist, sees him zoom down the left and cross low, the ball eluding all but Barco, on the far side of the box, and he lashes in a low finish. Surely the game is now over.
A corner is half-cleared and, when the ball is tucked back across by Dro, it hits a defender and falls into the path of Ruiz, who donkey-kicks into the net.
Paris St Germain's Fabian Ruiz (right) celebrates scoring their sixth goal. Photograph: Benoît Tessier/Reuters
Munoz, on as sub, breaks into the Atleti box and diddles his man by dipping infield, only to shoot too close to Oblak, who palms out Frimpong is there to ram home the rebound, but was offside when the intial shot was taken.
“Couple of Scottish Premier games tonight,” advises Simon McMahon – yes I’ve got them on my vidiprinter. “Rangers scoring in stoppage time to defeat St. Mirren by a goal to nil, while Celtic are leading by the same score at St. Johnstone with five minutes to go. The teams meet in the Scottish League Cup quarter=final on Sunday. Expect handshakes, pats on the back and general bonhomie all round fireworks.”
Grown-men action looks inevitable, even though away fans have been banned.
It’s been a quieter second half at Anfield – well, since the flurry at the start of it, when Liverpool scored their second goal. Atleti were really dangerous in the first, but have been largely shut down – and have, I think, missed Lee, who was hooked.
Incidentally, I love The Prestige, Christopher Nolan’s best film by a mile, in mine – it has blather and keks, which I don’t always find to be the case with him.
“There’s something uncanny about this PSG, as if they’re not fully synced up with reality,” says Kári Tulinius. “I can’t think of many teams that have had me entirely lose track of what’s going on, where the players and the ball just aren’t where they should be. At the risk of spoiling the movie The Prestige, while other sides are working within the parameters of the real, the Parisians seem to have found technology that allows them to break the bounds of physical space.”
They’re kind of the next version of Guardiola’s Barca, every player a technician but not, as you intimate, part of a system that tells them where to be and when; rather, they’re trusted to make sure that somebody is.
It’s a kicking! Rogers flies down the right and cut back along the carpet, Welbeck feinting to leave it for Palmer before taking it back the way it came and lashing low into the net. This is a seriously engaging football tea.
Danny Welbeck celebrates after extending Chelsea’s lead. Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty Images
Arsenal pop it about on the edge, Guimaraes into Tzolis, right of the box, and he plays back out to Odegaard, who laces a belting finish low into the far corner. You wondered if he was taking a step when he started crashing the box at the start of this season, and by the looks of things, that’s exactly what he’s doing.
Arsenal's Martin Odegaard opens the scoring. Photograph: Guglielmo Mangiapane/Reuters
It’s three goal in seven minutes! Palmer feeds Rogers in the middle, and he slides in to poke Neto, at inside-left. But there’s still a lot of work to do, the body opened and the finish passed low into the far corner. Chelsea aren’t great at the back, but goodness me, they’ve got some useful attackers.
Chelsea's Pedro Neto puts the home side ahead. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA
Neto (left) wheels away in celebration as Stamford Bridge erupts. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters
Spain press conference epa02237461 Spanish National Team player Jesus Navas smiles as he goes to press center on 05 July 2010 a Photograph: Juan Carlos C rdenas/EPA
I wonder what Enzo Maresca and Thomas Tuchel are making of Palmer so far this season. Every serious squad needs a maverick or two, and misunderstanding them says more about the managers than the players.
A throw goes towards Rogers, who kind of shrugs it off to Palmer, on the edge, and, using the defender as a screen to block the keeper’s view, he curves a low finish into the far bottom corner, the goal not unlike the one he scored for England in the Euro final.
All eyes are on the ball as Cole Palmer’s shot heads towards the far corner. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA
summary: This live-updating football report covers multiple matches, highlighting Chelsea's high-scoring win featuring goals from Danny Welbeck, Cole Palmer, and Pedro Neto. Liverpool secured an important Champions League victory against Atlético Madrid following a strong second half. Meanwhile, Paris St Germain recorded a heavy 6-1 win over Slovan Bratislava, and various other domestic and European results unfolded.
key_points: Chelsea secured a high-scoring victory with standout performances and goals from players including Danny Welbeck, Cole Palmer, and Pedro Neto.
Liverpool earned an important Champions League win against Atlético Madrid after overcoming a vulnerable first-half performance.
Paris St Germain defeated Slovan Bratislava with a dominant 6-1 scoreline.
Manager Andoni Iraola praised his side's character after successfully adjusting his tactics following Atlético's initial 3-5-2 setup.

Liverpool vs Atletico Madrid preview
Liverpool beat Atletico Madrid 3-2 on matchday one of the Champions League last season and punters should expect another high-scoring clash at Anfield.
Reds manager Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first Champions League match, five days after claiming his first Premier League win with Liverpool at Ipswich.
His side looked shaky in 2-2 draws with Newcastle and Nottingham Forest but Alexander Isak scored twice in the first ten minutes at Portman Road to set up a welcome 2-0 victory.
While Iraola is a Champions League rookie, his opposite number Diego Simeone has overseen 128 matches in the competition.
Only Carlo Ancelotti, Sir Alex Ferguson, Pep Guardiola, Arsene Wenger and Jose Mourinho have more Champions League experience than Simeone, who took Atletico to the final in 2014 and 2016.
Last season, they knocked out Barcelona in the quarter-finals and ran Arsenal close in a 2-1 aggregate defeat in the semis.
However, Atletico's campaign also included that opening defeat at Anfield, a 4-0 league-phase mauling by Arsenal and a 3-2 loss to Igor Tudor's Tottenham.
They had beaten Spurs 5-2 in a chaotic last-16 first leg and their defence was exposed again in Saturday's 3-0 La Liga defeat at Athletic Bilbao.
In the early years of Simeone's reign, Atletico were renowned for their defensive steel. More recently, though, they have been a far softer touch, particularly away from home.
Before their gritty semi-final against Arsenal, there were over 2.5 goals in 12 of Atletico's 14 European games last term and one of the exceptions was a 2-0 away win over ten-man Barcelona.
Star striker Julian Alvarez, strongly linked with a summer move to Barca or Arsenal, has made only two substitute appearances and may have to stew on the bench for a little longer.
Lee Kang-In, Ademola Lookman and Alex Baena have been used as forwards in a fluid 4-4-2 formation but Atletico look set for a high-scoring defeat at Anfield.
Liverpool finished top of the Champions League standings in 2024-25 and third last season, despite their poor Premier League campaign under Arne Slot.
Champions Paris Saint-Germain knocked them out in both seasons but Atletico are far less intimidating opponents.
Bradley Barcola, a two-time Champions League winner with PSG, could make his Liverpool debut and the Reds' attackers can ensure a memorable night for Iraola.
Back Llorente to end up in the doghouse
Marcos Llorente scored twice in Atletico's dramatic last-16 victory at Liverpool in March 2020 and also bagged a brace on last season's trip to Merseyside.
He named his dog "Anfield" to celebrate those goalscoring feats but could show too much bite in the tackle for the referee's liking this evening.
Liverpool have a host of dangerous wide players, including new signing Barcola. Llorente picked up nine yellow cards and one red last season and was booked against Sevilla on his first start of the new campaign.

title: US Open 2026 results: Carlos Alcaraz beaten by Ben Shelton in epic quarter-final
author: Harry Poole; Russell Fuller
content:
![Ben Shelton celebrates his US Open quarter-final victory over Carlos Alcaraz](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2560/cpsprodpb/2cfd/live/de377d00-ac22-11f1-9bd9-7b7da208bd5c.jpg)
Ben Shelton has equalled his best run at a Grand Slam tournament
- Published
Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence came to an end in a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton that ended at 03:34 local time - the latest finish in the tournament's history.
A large crowd remained captivated deep into the night as a modern classic unfolded over an unpredictable four hours and 28 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium.
The match did not begin until about 11pm in New York, after the start of the night session was delayed by Tuesday's earlier matches.
At its conclusion, eighth seed Shelton basked in a standing ovation from a delirious audience after completing a 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) victory that will live long in the memory of all those present.
"That was a war, an epic match, so physical," Shelton said.
"Carlos is one of the greatest champions in our sport already at 23 years old.
"It's ridiculous some of the stuff he comes up with sometimes - the most enjoyable match that I've had in my career, for sure."
This was the biggest - and certainly most significant - win of Shelton's career.
He had not beaten a top-three player in 17 attempts, and had lost each of his three previous matches against Spain's Alcaraz.
It also boosted home hopes of a first American men's singles champion in New York for 23 years.
Shelton was less than a year old when Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003 - but an American finalist is guaranteed when he and Frances Tiafoe meet in Friday's semi-finals.
World number three Alcaraz was competing at his first tournament since a lengthy injury lay-off, but that is to take nothing away from Shelton, who produced a phenomenal performance.
Seven-time major winner Alcaraz had exceeded expectations on his return after more than four months out with a wrist injury, including sweeping past 20th seed Tommy Paul to reach the last eight.
But the 23-year-old's lack of match fitness appeared to finally catch up with him in a high-octane encounter filled with breathless exchanges and astounding displays of athleticism.
Even when it appeared Alcaraz had emptied the tank, the two-time winner not only forced a deciding set but would go the distance as the players engaged in a tense 10-point match tie-break that provided a fitting conclusion to the contest.
"It was close. So I'm just not going to be disappointed about not getting the win at the end," said Alcaraz.
"I'm just proud about myself, about how I fought. I leave the court with a smile, healthy, and this is what I needed."
Shelton achieves seismic win
While home hope Shelton had the vast support of the hardy crowd, Alcaraz has always felt at home at Flushing Meadows.
The Spaniard had won 28 of his 31 matches at the tournament - the highest win rate at the US Open in the sport's professional era at above 90% - and last year became the first man to reach the final without dropping a set since Roger Federer in 2015.
The Australian Open champion was also on an 18-match unbeaten streak at Grand Slam tournaments, having missed the French Open and Wimbledon with injury, and was seeking to reach his fourth New York semi-final in five years.
Regardless of his opponent's current levels, for Shelton this was a victory that could prove seismic in front of a home crowd who passionately backed him throughout.
"It is incredible, I always say that this is the greatest stadium in the world," the 23-year-old said.
"I'm just hoping my best friend and sister don't have to be at work at 6am. It would be huge from their employers to let them have the day off."
The American number one is through to his third major semi-final, having lost to two of the game's heavyweights in Jannik Sinner at last year's Australian Open and Novak Djokovic in New York three years ago. Both went on to be crowned champions.
After ousting Alcaraz, Shelton is now the second-highest ranked player remaining in the draw after world number two Alexander Zverev.
It remains to be seen how Shelton will recover for the semi-final against Tiafoe, who completed a remarkable comeback from two sets and a break down to beat compatriot Alex Michelsen.
"For me, it's always about the people in the crowd - whether it's my coaches and my team, all of my family and friends," Shelton said.
"The city of New York that showed up tonight until 3am, that's what kept me going."
A closely contested first set offered a hint of the momentum swings that would define the match.
Alcaraz edged the opener on a tie-break - but only after surrendering his advantage after breaking for a seemingly decisive 6-5 lead.
Shelton, however, was ruthless as Alcaraz's level dropped sharply and embarked on a run of nine unanswered games to claim the second set and take charge of the third.
Refusing to fold, Alcaraz launched his fourth-set revival by saving two break points and then breaking when Shelton missed a backhand.
Alcaraz appeared to be sick into his towel during a changeover, such was his level of physical exertion, but would break Shelton a second time as he earned a fifth set as the time approached 02:30.
Both players failed to take break-point opportunities before a match-deciding breaker swung back and forth.
Shelton led 3-1 and Alcaraz regained control at 5-3.
But the Spaniard's uncharacteristically high number of unforced errors - the second seed made 53 overall - ultimately cost him, as Shelton captured five of the next six points before seeing out victory in style with an ace.
'An opponent has to take advantage - and Shelton did'
The first sign that all was not well with Alcaraz came at the end of the first set.
His forehand was off, and his serve erratic. Some of the rallies were stunning, but he was playing carelessly at times, and sometimes seemed disengaged as his concentration fluctuated.
All of which can be expected of someone who was playing just his fifth singles match since April and a first against a top-10 player.
But the opponent has to take advantage - and Shelton did so superbly.
Shelton has previously had a miserable record against the very best, losing all 17 of his previous matches against top-three players.
The flashy left-hander played plenty of shots and sent down one serve at 149mph, but was excellent on return and disciplined in defence.
By the fourth and fifth sets, Alcaraz was locked in again but could not prevent Shelton closing out the win of his life.
summary: Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defense ended in a dramatic five-set quarter-final defeat to Ben Shelton, concluding at 03:34 local time as the latest finish in tournament history. The grueling match lasted four hours and 28 minutes, resulting in Shelton's first career victory against a top-three player. With this win, Shelton advances to face compatriot Frances Tiafoe in an all-American semi-final, guaranteeing a home finalist for the first time in 23 years.
key_points: Eighth seed Ben Shelton defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7).
The match finished at 03:34 local time, setting a record for the latest-ever finish in US Open history.
The victory marked Shelton's first win against a top-three player after 17 previous losses.
Shelton will face Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals, guaranteeing an American men's singles finalist for the first time since 2003.
Alcaraz was playing in his first tournament back from a four-month wrist injury lay-off.

title: FC Porto 0-2 Manchester City: Erling Haaland earns Enzo Maresca a first Champions League win as City head coach but English side fail to impress
author: Sam Blitz
content:
FC Porto 0-2 Manchester City: Erling Haaland earns Enzo Maresca a first Champions League win as City head coach but English side fail to impress
Report as Manchester City beat FC Porto 2-0 away from home in Enzo Maresca's first Champions League game in charge of the club; Erling Haaland put missed chances in the first half behind him to score the winner after 47 minutes, then netted a second in stoppage time
Tuesday 8 September 2026 22:38, UK
Erling Haaland's double earned Manchester City a 2-0 win at FC Porto - but it was another game where Enzo Maresca's side won but struggled to convince.
City's main man up front was surprisingly wasteful in the first half, seeing two glorious chances in the area saved by Diogo Costa as well as heading another good chance over the bar.
Porto's goalkeeper was in inspired form in the opening 45 minutes, also saving well from Rayan Cherki from the rebound of one of Haaland's chances.

- Latest news and rumours: Man City
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
But Haaland took just two minutes of the second period to make amends, barging Jakub Kiwior aside to nod an Enzo Fernandez cross in off the post.
But City then took their foot off the gas as the Portuguese champions started to grow in confidence. Porto failed to produce a shot on target but Alan Varela curled just wide of the far post from the edge of the box in a warning shot.
Then Gianluigi Donnarumma was nearly caught in possession by Porto forward William Gomes, with the City goalkeeper lucky to see the ball run away to safety. City did find a way to seal the result, however, as Haaland tucked home Rayan Ait-Nouri's cutback in stoppage time.
Despite another game this season where City have won but struggled to impress at the same time, Maresca failed to win away of his three away Champions League ties as Chelsea boss last term.
He will see a winning start to this campaign as a positive - especially as City have become the first team to beat Porto at the Estadio do Dragao this calendar year.
But improvement is needed ahead of Sunday's Manchester derby at Old Trafford, live on Sky Sports.
The key moments from Estadio do Dragao
16: SAVE! Antoine Semenyo starts the game brightly and curls an early effort into Diogo Costa's gloves.
21: BIG CHANCE FOR HAALAND! Semenyo feeds Phil Foden who clips a cross into the box for Haaland - who is denied by a smart glove from Costa.
27: BIG MISS! Haaland heads over another good chance via a cross from the left, this time from Semenyo.
29: BIG SAVE! Foden goes on a mazy run in and around the penalty area and forces another save from Costa.
31: DOUBLE SAVE! A man possessed! Costa denies Haaland's low drive from inside the box, then gets up to stop Rayan Cherki at the rebound.
42: OUCH! Marc Guehi catches Gabri Veiga with his arm which causes a lot of blood. With Porto calling for a red card for a violent elbow, the Man City defender avoids punishment. It was more accidental rather than malicious.
47: GOAL! Haaland takes just two minutes to rectify his wasteful first half by nodding a header in off the post from Enzo Fernandez's cross.
49: NO PENALTY! City goalkeeper Donnarumma clatters into Porto winger Pepe in the box… but the offside flag goes up against the forward.
57: SO CLOSE! Porto midfielder Alan Varela gets a chance to shoot and curls just wide of the far post. That was Porto's first shot of the game.
66: NERVY! Donnarumma is nearly caught in possession by Porto forward Gomes, but the ball runs behind for a goal kick.
85: JUST WIDE! City substitute Ait-Nouri has the chance to seal the result but steers a shot wide of goal from a good area.
90+1: GOAL! Haaland seals the result by slotting home Ait-Nouri's cutback after he did well to get to the byline.
Should Maresca be happy about Man City's performance?
Man City striker Erling Haaland to Amazon Prime:
"I hope so, we win away in a difficult game. Look at this atmosphere, it was unreal at times. So I hope [yes].
"Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a difficult fight, man against man. They're a top team, impressive, all of them. They play amazing football.
"Well done to them. But with all the pressure, we have to deliver on the biggest stage. That's what we did tonight.
"Honestly we controlled the whole first half. Of course, it's a bit uncomfortable when they come high. But we created a lot of chances. I could have easily had a few more goals.
"But second half we scored and they managed to push us for a good 25 minutes. We managed to hold through and finish the game.
"These are the games we have to win. We had a great start to the season and in the Champions League, you have to win games. If not, you get all the pressure. You never know what's going to happen.
"We have to learn. Enzo has to demand a lot from us and each other. At Manchester City, you have to win games and win trophies, that's what we have to do."
And here's Maresca's verdict - he's happy!
Man City head coach Enzo Maresca to Amazon Prime:
"We could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. But overall we deserved to win the game. We created enough chances to win the game, we didn't concede a lot.
"It's normal to come here and concede some noises so overall I'm happy with the performance.
"If you think you're going to come here in this stadium and just play and not concede anything, it's not reality. It's normal that they are going to create something. They didn't create a lot - some actions, some mistakes from us. But I think it's normal."
Analysis: Man City continue to play with fire
Enzo Maresca has a point. You can't turn your nose up at winning away at FC Porto - an intimidating atmosphere, one that is not used to suffering defeat. Doing so in a manner where they conceded little in terms of clear chances is also a positive.
But look at City's performances this season. Trounced in the Community Shield by Arsenal, then a late show to overcome Bournemouth with a fortunate win. Then came a resounding win over Crystal Palace, but then they nearly dropped the ball in their 1-0 win over Coventry.
This was another game where they could have dropped the ball. City dominated for 47 minutes but then allowed FC Porto back into it. There were slack passes and constant losses of possession - a better team would have found a way back into the game.
And City face a better test on Sunday. No team will be more desperate to take advantage of such play than Manchester United at Old Trafford. It will be another big atmosphere for Maresca's City to overcome. But if they continue to play with fire, they will get burnt.
summary: Erling Haaland scored twice to secure a 2-0 away victory over FC Porto, giving Enzo Maresca a winning start to his Champions League tenure as Manchester City head coach. Despite the win, Manchester City failed to completely convince as they allowed Porto back into the match in the second half. The result marks the first time Porto has been defeated at the Estadio do Dragao this calendar year.
key_points: Erling Haaland scored twice after overcoming a wasteful first half that included multiple missed chances.
Haaland netted the opening goal two minutes into the second half from an Enzo Fernandez cross and added a second in stoppage time.
The 2-0 victory marks Enzo Maresca's first Champions League win in charge of Manchester City.
Manchester City became the first team to defeat FC Porto at the Estadio do Dragao this calendar year.

title: Simeone sends Anfield warning to Atletico Madrid players ahead of Liverpool clash
author: Carl Markham
content:
Atletico Madrid head coach Diego Simeone has warned his side to prepare for an intense atmosphere at Anfield when side faces Liverpool on Wednesday, following a lapse in concentration during their weekend defeat.
Atletico conceded two goals in the space of three second-half minutes on their way to losing 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao on Saturday.
A year ago, Atletico travelled to Merseyside for their opening Champions League fixture and trailed 2-0 within six minutes. Although they managed to recover to 2-2, they were ultimately beaten by a late Virgil van Dijk goal in added time.
Atleti have managed just one clean sheet across their past 16 Champions League matches and have lost on each of their last five visits to England.
"I don’t think it was (a lack of) motivation what happened to us in Bilbao, it was a lack of awareness, switching off," said Simeone, whose team reached the semi-finals last season.
![Julian Alvarez is not expected to start after missing out on a move to Barcelona](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/09/08/19/2026-09-08T174513Z_442284689_UP1EM981DBCVZ_RTRMADP_3_SOCCER-CHAMPIONS-LIV-ATM-PREVIEW.JPG)
"We are coming into a marvellous stadium, a great atmosphere, we have to look at the start of the game as it will be full on."
Simeone acknowledged that transfer speculation involving forward Julian Alvarez proved unhelpful before the window shut, with the player missing two days of training citing illness after learning he would not be allowed to join Barcelona.
The Argentina international is unlikely to start, nor is striker Jonathan David, who signed on loan from Juventus on 1 September and has made only two substitute appearances, though both are expected to play some part.
Simeone added: "Jonathan has only just arrived, Julian is getting better. I don’t see he could start tomorrow, but I am sure he could help at some point in the game."
Atleti left Anfield empty-handed last season, but they have enjoyed some success on Merseyside in the recent past.
Back in 2020, Simeone’s men knocked Liverpool out of the Champions League at the last-16 stage, securing a 3-2 triumph at Anfield after extra time to seal a 4-2 aggregate win after claiming a 1-0 victory in the opening leg in Madrid.
Simeone will hope for a repeat result on Wednesday against a Liverpool side that beat Ipswich 2-0 on Friday to seal Andoni Iraola’s first win since replacing Arne Slot.
summary: Atletico Madrid head coach Diego Simeone has warned his players to expect an intense atmosphere at Anfield when they face Liverpool on Wednesday. The warning follows a 3-0 weekend defeat to Athletic Bilbao, where Simeone attributed the loss to a lack of awareness rather than motivation. Additionally, Simeone addressed squad readiness, stating that forward Julian Alvarez and recent loanee Jonathan David are unlikely to start.
key_points: Atletico Madrid lost 3-0 to Athletic Bilbao prior to their Champions League match against Liverpool.
Diego Simeone warned his squad to be prepared for an intense start at Anfield.
Julian Alvarez is unlikely to start after missing training due to a failed transfer move to Barcelona.
New loan signing Jonathan David is also not expected to be in the starting lineup.
Atletico have lost on each of their last five visits to England.

title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto
author: Jamie Jackson
content:
Enzo Maresca admitted a liking for the “boom-boom” of house music, then oversaw a gritty performance that ended with Manchester City enjoying the sweet notes of victory.
They had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition and also lost the 2021 Champions League final at this venue, so to beat Porto and claim three points is a fillip for the manager’s nascent project.
Factor in, too, how City face Paris Saint-Germain on matchday No 2, and travel to Manchester United for Sunday’s derby, and Maresca can be exuberant at his start as Pep Guardiola’s successor.
All four games have been won – maybe more than even he would have hoped for, Erling Haaland’s double keeping the perfect start going. With 16 points the accepted target to qualify automatically for the knockout stage, as this was required in the first two years of this format, Maresca may have considered a win here vital particularly as targeting four victories from City’s four home matches as necessary to reach the tally might founder due to the visit of the double European champions next month.
Maresca stood down Elliot Anderson and gave Ayyoub Bouaddi a full debut, alongside Enzo Fernández in midfield. Haaland was not given the rest Maresca stated he will need at some point soon, as the No 9 headed an attack that contained Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo behind.
Bouaddi, playing deeper than Fernández, proved calm, though a surge forward was followed by the Argentinian heading in the area.
The issue was Porto being content to allow City to pitter-patter passes about their backline and middle third and there being no quickness of play or penetration. Francesco Farioli’s men offered an example of exactly how when Marc Guéhi’s ball short-changed Bouaddi, possession was nabbed, and suddenly William Gomes had to be stopped on the edge of City’s area. Earlier, Gabriel Veiga sliced through the rearguard and had Gianluigi Donnarumma saving: the offside flag went up but here were two warnings.
Quick Guide
Dortmund's Karetsas taken to hospital
Borussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal.
“Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.”
The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time.
Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence.
Real Betis twice came from behind to beat Lille 3-2 away, with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner.
Lille scored their opener in the 12th minute and regained the lead through Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to the face of an opponent.
AEK Athens made a winning start, beating the Austrian side LASK 1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half. Agencies
Discard the ponderous pace might have been Maresca’s message because when Foden switched flanks from the right and accelerated, Porto were splayed, and Haaland’s header from the cross required Diogo Costa’s gloves to keep the contest goalless.
A near-carbon copy came when Semenyo popped the ball over from the left but this time Haaland’s header sailed over. City were warming up: Foden, Cherki and Haaland all being denied, as Porto were caught in a chokehold in and around their area.
![Erling Haaland outjumps Jakub Kiwior to head City into the lead](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/506ab0c50e5ae09b9dccde1d2996ef81cdd23a93/0_0_4345_2830/master/4345.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
At Leicester and then Chelsea Maresca could draw criticism for a quasi-sideways style at times. Yet after the slowish passage, tonight’s XI had become direct and a threat, as when Bouaddi chipped the ball left from near halfway, it went forward at speed, and a panicked Porto cleared.
When Veiga went down after a challenge with Guéhi the match was halted, tempers frayed. The No 10 recovered – it appeared to be a head problem – and the action, finally, restarted before Szymon Marciniak blew his whistle for the break.
after newsletter promotion
After the now seemingly de rigueur fireworks before every Champions League game, Porto had begun with confidence sky-high after winning all five Primeira Liga outings so far and, when wandering off for half-time, they remained content.
The mood changed almost instantaneously. City, at last, showed the ruthlessness needed at this level. Cherki, breaking into the area, swerved left, leaving Costa stranded. He fed Fernández and Haaland headed his cross into the turf and home – the visitors had a priceless lead.
What would be Porto’s response? To rove upfield and go close to the equaliser, was the answer. Maresca’s team can be open, as they were when André Silva had an age to dip right and let fly, the former Portugal forward’s attempt hitting the side-netting.
The lead was slender, as it was in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry. Maresca acted as the hour passed, removing Cherki and Semenyo for Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye: two attackers for one forward and a holding player in Anderson whose role was to try and exert control for City, and aid Bouaddi in snuffing out any Porto threat.
A second goal would also stymie the hosts, so Ndiaye skipped across the grass, and unloaded, though the effort went straight into Costa’s clutches. Foden, too, tried to break in behind but the ball was shepherded back to the Porto keeper.
Whenever Farioli’s team moved forward City remained vulnerable despite Anderson’s presence. By the close, though, Haaland’s late right-foot stab ensured the result, and meant that even an interval dispute in the tunnel due to the Veiga-Guéhi clash was of scant import to City, despite tempers again meaning a further row.
summary: Manchester City secured a 2-0 away victory against Porto in their Champions League opener, driven by two goals from Erling Haaland. The win continues manager Enzo Maresca's perfect start in charge following four consecutive victories. Despite a slow start and some defensive vulnerability, City's second-half breakthrough sealed the three points.
key_points: Erling Haaland scored twice to secure Manchester City's victory over Porto.
Manager Enzo Maresca maintained his 100% win record at the start of his tenure.
The victory provides City with an ideal start in the Champions League before facing Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United.

title: Ballon d'Or: Sadio Mane and Achraf Hakimi nominated - but when will Africa win again?
author: Rob Stevens
content:
![A triptych showing Sadio Mane, the Ballon d'Or trophy and Achraf Hakimi. Mane wears a green Senegal kit with a yellow number 10 on the chest while Hakimi wears a red Morocco shirt with a gold number two on the chest. The golden Ballon d'Or trophy which sits between them is a football divided into hexagonal patches sitting atop a glittering chunk of mineral ore](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/2ea3/live/bf4f1a40-aba2-11f1-b109-879e35c24276.png)
Senegal forward Sadio Mane and Morocco right-back Achraf Hakimi are the only two Africans in the running to win the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or
- Published
Africa has only ever had one Ballon d'Or winner, and the wait for someone to emulate George Weah is likely to be extended further after this year's nominations were revealed.
Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi and Senegal forward Sadio Mane are the continent's two names on the 30-strong list.
Both players have previously recorded top-six Ballon d'Or finishes but, after a year in which Spain lifted the Fifa World Cup and Kylian Mbappe netted 10 goals to become the tournament's all-time top scorer, the chances of the Paris St-Germain right-back or the Al-Nassr winger lifting the coveted trophy appear slim.
And it is not the first time that Africa has failed to make a big impact.
Part of the reason for the historic lack of success is down to the fact the award, which was first handed out by France Football magazine in 1956, was not open to players representing non-European nations until 1995.
That was the year that Liberian striker Weah scooped the prize after his impressive form for PSG and AC Milan.
Yet, for all the stars the continent has produced, the only other time an African player registered a top-three finish came in 2022, when Mane was second behind France striker Karim Benzema.
Of course, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have dominated proceedings for most of this century, scooping 13 of the 15 available Ballons d'Or between 2008 and 2023.
Journalists from the top 100 nations in the Fifa rankings will vote for the prize, with the recipient of the 2026 trophy announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October.
The "symbolic choice of venue" for the 70th anniversary of the award is in tribute to the inaugural winner, England winger Sir Stanley Matthews.
But how do the historic Ballon d'Or numbers stack up for Africa?
Weah claims the crown
![George Weah, visible from shoulders up, wearing a black and red AC Milan home shirt, lifts the Ballon d'Or trophy which is being handed to him by a man who is out of shot](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/deaf/live/280eed60-aba0-11f1-8e72-a346833ed029.jpg)
George Weah went on to serve as President of Liberia from 2018 to 2024
The high point of Africa's Ballon d'Or history clearly came in the very first year the continent's stars became eligible, with Weah topping the vote in 1995 ahead of Germany's Jurgen Klinsmann and Finland's Jari Litmanen.
Five more Africans made that year's 50-player list.
But only once since, in 2007, has the continent had as many as six nominations. On that occasion Didier Drogba was the highest-ranked finisher, with the Ivorian coming fourth.
The pool has narrowed since then, with 30 players in contention since 2008 and just 23 in the running when the Ballon d'Or was combined with the Fifa's world player of the year award between 2010 and 2015.
One other stand-out year for Africa came in 2019, when three men finished in the top 10. Mane came fourth, Egypt's Mohamed Salah was fifth, and Riyad Mahrez of Algeria tenth.
Which African nation has the most Ballon d'Or nominations?
![Samuel Eto'o, visible from waist up wearing a blue and claret Barcelona home shirt, chases after a Champions League-branded football which is hanging in the air. His gaze is firmly locked in on the ball](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/2048/cpsprodpb/d5d4/live/c5b02b10-aba0-11f1-8e72-a346833ed029.jpg)
Samuel Eto'o finished fifth in the Ballon d'Or in 2009 after scoring in Barcelona's Champions League final victory over Manchester United that year
In total, Africa has received 76 nominations for the Ballon d'Or since 1995.
That makes up just 6.62% of the overall hopefuls.
Cameroon legend Samuel Eto'o has the most nominations, having been in the running nine times in a row from 2003 to 2011. His best finish came in 2009 when he was fifth.
Drogba follows with eight nominations, with Salah on six.
Five-time nominee Mane has the greatest longevity of any African, with the 34-year-old's first and most recent appearances on the list coming 10 years apart.
Nigeria has had the most individual players listed for the award, with eight in total. Victor Osimhen's eighth-place finish in 2023 is the best performance by a Super Eagles player.
Room for improvement
Thirty-nine African countries are still awaiting their first nominee, although Chad is surprisingly not among them after striker Japhet N'Doram was part of the 1995 list alongside Weah.
DR Congo and South Africa, ranked 43rd and 54th in the world respectively, are the highest-ranked nations still waiting to make the cut, while no player representing a club side on the continent has ever been nominated.
There have been nine years since 1995 when only one African was among the nominees.
The most recent of those instances was 2024, when Nigeria's Ademola Lookman finished 14th after scoring a hat-trick in the Europa League final for Atalanta.
African contenders have failed to pick up any votes on four occasions after being shortlisted: 1998 (Sunday Oliseh), 2000 (Geremi and Patrick Mboma), 2001 (Samuel Kuffour) and 2003 (Eto'o and Hatem Trabelsi).
Ballon d'Or nominations by African country
Ivory Coast - 15 (Didier Drogba 8, Yaya Toure 5, Kolo Toure, Sebastien Haller)
Cameroon - 12 (Samuel Eto'o 9, Geremi, Patrick Mboma, Andre Onana)
Nigeria - 10 (Jay-Jay Okocha 2, Nwankwo Kanu 2, Finidi George, Daniel Amokachi, Victor Ikpeba, Sunday Oliseh, Victor Osimhen, Ademola Lookman)
Senegal - 8 (Sadio Mane 5, Papa Bouba Diop, El Hadji Diouf, Kalidou Koulibaly)
Ghana - 6 (Michael Essien 3, Tony Yeboah, Samuel Kuffour, Asamoah Gyan)
Egypt - 6 (all Mohamed Salah)
Algeria - 4 (all Riyad Mahrez)
Mali - 3 (Mahamadou Diarra 2, Frederic Kanoute)
Gabon - 3 (all Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang)
Morocco - 3 (Achraf Hakimi 2, Yassine Bounou)
Liberia - 2 (both George Weah)
Chad - 1 (Japhet N'Doram)
Tunisia - 1 (Hatem Trabelsi)
Togo - 1 (Emmanuel Adebayor)
Guinea - 1 (Serhou Guirassy)
Similar story for Africa's women
![Temwa Chawinga, visible from stomach up with dyed blue hair and wearing a green Malawi shirt, stands side on to the camera and makes a heart gesture with her hands in front of her chest as she celebrates a goal. An empty stand with green and red seats can be seen out of focus in the background](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1800/cpsprodpb/4f95/live/8453e440-aba5-11f1-8e72-a346833ed029.jpg)
Malawi forward Temwa Chawinga received her second Ballon d'Or Feminin nomination after scooping the golden boot at this year's Women's Africa Cup of Nations
Since the women's Ballon d'Or was first awarded in 2018, only four African players have been nominated.
Nigeria forward Asisat Oshoala was the first, making the 20- and 30-name shortlists in 2022 and 2023 respectively.
Zambia skipper Barbra Banda has been nominated in every year since, joined by Tabitha Chawinga of Malawi in 2024 and then her sister Temwa Chawinga in 2025 and 2026.
It means no more than two players from Africa have ever been listed for the prize in any one year.
The continent has had a total of 10 nominations from the 195 players nominated overall.
Ballon d'Or Feminin nominations by African country
Zambia - 3 (all Barbra Banda)
Malawi - 3 (Temwa Chawinga 2, Tabitha Chawinga)
Nigeria - 2 (both Asisat Oshoala)
Additional reporting by Ian Williams.
summary: Senegal forward Sadio Mane and Morocco right-back Achraf Hakimi are the only African players nominated for the 2026 men's Ballon d'Or. George Weah remains Africa's sole winner of the award, having secured the prize in 1995 after non-European players became eligible. Since then, African footballers have received a total of 76 nominations, with Samuel Eto'o holding the record for the most individual nods.
key_points: George Weah is the only African player to win the Ballon d'Or, doing so in 1995.
Sadio Mane and Achraf Hakimi are Africa's only two nominees for the 2026 men's award.
Cameroon's Samuel Eto'o holds the record for the most African nominations with nine.
Nigeria has produced the highest number of individual players listed for the award, with eight.
Only four African women have been nominated for the Ballon d'Or Feminin since its inception in 2018.

title: 'I'm used to being in this position.' Gauff to lean on experience for 12th major quarterfinal
author: Cole Bambini
content:
'I'm used to being in this position.' Gauff to lean on experience for 12th major quarterfinal
![Gauff Jovic R16](https://photoresources.wtatennis.com/photo-resources/2026/09/08/46ff8c8d-8d3f-4065-8f84-d8860afe3797/GettyImages-2294058065.jpg?width=850&height=450) 
NEW YORK -- Coco Gauff doesn't find the fact she's into her 12th Grand Slam quarterfinal too surprising.
US Open: Scores | Order of play | Draws
Though it's the first time in three years she's back into the final eight at the US Open, the 2023 champion is -- humbly -- accustomed to being at this stage in tournaments. Following a 6-4, 6-1 win over Iva Jovic Monday, Gauff is primed for a US Open quarterfinal showdown on Wednesday with Roland Garros winner Mirra Andreeva.
"I think I just welcome it," Gauff said on the magnitude of playing in a Grand Slam quarterfinal. "I don't know how to say this without, like -- a quarterfinal for me, I feel like I'm at the point where I'm used to being in this position. I'm constantly putting myself in quarterfinals, so the moment doesn't seem as big anymore.
"That doesn't mean I'm -- I'm very lucky to play, be here in the quarterfinal. Obviously, I hope to play many more, so I think it's the fine line of appreciating the moment. I think so many people would love to reach a Grand Slam quarterfinal, but also knowing that I put myself in this position so many times that I should almost be used to it."
Gauff is riding high momentum, arguably the best of anyone actively. With her 1 hour and 33 minute win over Jovic, she extended her winning streak on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz to 10 matches. Furthermore, with her straight sets win, the two-time major champion has now won 20 consecutive sets, having last dropped one in her Cincinnati second round vs. Liudmila Samsonova.
Next on deck is Andreeva, an opponent that Gauff has never lost to in five meetings. Four of those five meetings have come on clay, however, with the lone on hard court coming at the 2023 US Open when Andreeva was finding her footing on tour.
To advance to the quarterfinal, Gauff handled a valiant Jovic. By the scoreline, it may have seem one-sided, but Jovic played Gauff tightly, forcing long games and rallies. The pair's lone previous battle came on the Italian clay, where Gauff edged the younger Jovic 5-7, 7-5, 6-2 in Rome's Round of 16. Gauff would eventually progress to the final of the Internazional BNL d'Italia, falling to Elina Svitolina in the championship.
Monday's first set would be quite opposite of what transpired in Rome, with Gauff securing it in just under 35 minutes. Despite being broken in the opening game, Gauff went on a tear by taking the next six games. At one point, from midway to the first set to 0-30 in the second set, Gauff had won 25 of 30 points against Jovic, who ultimately made the second set much more contested.
Jovic exited Arthur Ashe Stadium in slight tears, disappointed in her performance where she won just 45% of points on her serve. She was down one break before leveling at 3-3, but Gauff managed to strike back at the perfect time with a break at 5-4 with an opportunity to serve for the match.
"It's always great when you can play your best tennis when the points are closer and when they're able to come back," Gauff said. "Obviously, I would like to be up a break and stay up a break, but that's not tennis. It's a back-and-forth game.
"I'm doing a good job of when I maybe miss opportunities or lose some games, just keeping it in the past and focusing on the present, and I think that's the main thing. I don't view it as opportunities lost sometimes. I try to just view it as what to do better and just trusting that I'll be in the same position again."
What it means?
- Since 2000, only Serena Williams (15) and Maria Sharapova (13) have reached more Grand Slam quarterfinals than Gauff before the age of 23.
- Gauff has won nine matches in a row in straight sets for the first time in her career.
- The top six seeds have reached the US Open quarterfinals for the first time since 1998 -- Martina Hingis, Lindsay Davenport, Jana Novotna, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, Venus Williams and Monica Seles.
summary: Coco Gauff advanced to her 12th Grand Slam quarterfinal and her first at the US Open in three years with a 6-4, 6-1 victory over Iva Jovic. The 2023 champion extended her winning streak to 10 matches and 20 consecutive sets following the win. Gauff will next face Roland Garros winner Mirra Andreeva in the quarterfinals.
key_points: Gauff defeated Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-1 to reach the US Open quarterfinals.
The win extended Gauff's winning streak to 10 matches and 20 consecutive sets.
Gauff's next quarterfinal opponent will be Mirra Andreeva, whom Gauff has never lost to in five previous meetings.
Before turning 23, only Serena Williams and Maria Sharapova have reached more Grand Slam quarterfinals than Gauff since 2000.

title: Man City XI vs Porto: Confirmed team news and predicted lineup
author: Arthur Ferridge
content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
City kept their perfect league record intact as they edged past Coventry last time out, winning 1-0 thanks to a customary goal from Erling Haaland, and Maresca is expected to ring the changes as the club’s European campaign gets underway.
The Coventry match turned up a pair of injury concerns. Nico O’Reilly was due to start the match but dropped out of the starting lineup having sustained a lower back issue in warm-ups, with Enzo Fernandez called in to replace him. Deadline Day signing Iliman Ndiaye then came off with an apparent knock, joining fellow winger Jeremy Doku on the treatment table.
![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/09/07/17/01M1XSPQ9P2JM6A4YVXKKQM7C0.jpg?trim=201,0,201,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=960)
Maresca had already promised to make changes at the Estadio Do Dragao, however. Speaking after sinking Coventry, he told reporters: “We saw today with Ayyoub [Bouaddi], [Ryan] McAidoo, Iliman Ndiaye, they haven’t played in Champions League but they need to start, so on Tuesday they are going to start to get minutes in the Champions League.”
It remains to be seen whether Ndiaye will be fit to feature in Porto. He has been pictured in training, though, suggesting he is clear to play. Should that prove to be the case, he will line up on the left flank, with Antoine Semenyo making way for McAidoo on the opposite side and Enzo Fernandez in as a No10.
Ayyoub Bouaddi will partner Elliot Anderson at the base of midfield, in front of what should be an unchanged back four comprising Josko Gvardiol, Marc Guehi, Ruben Dias and Abdukodir Khusanov. Matheus Nunes has been named to the travelling squad, and could also feature.
Maresca has made clear Haaland will need to be rotated in and out of the squad over the coming weeks as City compete on four fronts, but the prolific Norwegian will likely lead the line in Portugal anyway.

summary: Manchester City prepares for their upcoming Champions League match against Porto with manager Maresca planning several squad changes. The team recently defeated Coventry 1-0, though that match resulted in injury concerns for Nico O'Reilly and Iliman Ndiaye. Despite a minor knock, Ndiaye has been spotted in training and is in contention to start alongside other rotation players like Ayyoub Bouaddi and Ryan McAidoo.
key_points: Manager Maresca plans to rotate the squad and give minutes to players like Bouaddi, McAidoo, and Ndiaye against Porto.
Nico O'Reilly and Jeremy Doku are injured, while Iliman Ndiaye is a doubt with a knock but has trained.
Erling Haaland is expected to lead the line in Portugal despite upcoming plans to manage his minutes.
